***Review posted on The Eater of Books! blog*** 
 Her Dark Curiosity by Megan Shepherd 
 Book Two of The Madman's Daughter series 
 Publisher: Balzer + Bray 
 Publication Date: January 28, 2014 
 Rating: 3 stars 
 Source: ARC sent by the publisher 
 Summary (from Goodreads): 
 To defeat the darkness, she must first embrace it. 
 Months have passed since Juliet Moreau returned to civilization after escaping her father's island--and the secrets she left behind. Now, back in London once more, she is rebuilding the life she once knew and trying to forget Dr. Moreau's horrific legacy--though someone, or something, hasn't forgotten her. 
 As people close to Juliet fall victim one by one to a murderer who leaves a macabre calling card of three clawlike slashes, Juliet fears one of her father's creations may have also escaped the island. She is determined to find the killer before Scotland Yard does, though it means awakening sides of herself she had thought long banished, and facing loves from her past she never expected to see again. 
 As Juliet strives to stop a killer while searching for a serum to cure her own worsening illness, she finds herself once more in the midst of a world of scandal and danger. Her heart torn in two, past bubbling to the surface, life threatened by an obsessive killer--Juliet will be lucky to escape alive. 
 What I Liked: 
 Believe it or not, I have a positive opinion towards this book. You'll see my next section, with the dislikes, and probably think that I absolutely hated this book. Not the case. I enjoyed it. I was interested throughout the book, even if the overall plot was cyclical. The events in this book kept my interest, even if some pissed me off. The romance was horrendous, but I think things get resolved at the very end of this book. ONE CAN HOPE. 
 Juliet has returned to London, but she is getting weaker and weaker, since the injections are working as well as they used to work. As everyone should have expected, Edward appears in London, and he needs her help. He can barely control his monster side, a side that wants Juliet, a side that Juliet is attracted to. But Juliet is determined to create a cure for herself, and for Edward. Even though she loves Montgomery, he's not there, and Edward is, so everything is all about Edward. 
 I'm a little bit cynical when it comes to Edward. I don't like him at all, as a character, and as a love interest. He's a creature, an abomination, and he shouldn't exist. I wish someone would just kill him already! Meanwhile, I really like Montgomery, and not just as a love interest. He's definitely the better man in this book, even if Shepherd wants readers to think that he is "bad" or "has secrets" or has "done terrible things", or whatever cliches authors invent to make decent people seem "bad". 
 I wasn't a fan of Juliet in this book - she had a little more backbone in the first book. However, if things go a certain way in the third book, I'll overlook her poor character in this second book. Sequel slump, you know? Although, I gave this book and the first book the same rating. But technically, books in series should get better and better, right? 
 Anyway. I did enjoy the plot of this book (not necessarily the series' plot). I was curiously as to who was doing the killings - even when we think we know who was doing them, it seemed like more than one person was killing in London. And all of the digging into Juliet's father's past was interesting. I'm curious as to how Shepherd will use all of this past knowledge in the third book. 
 I am looking forward to reading the third book, after this book's ending. If this book hadn't ended the way it had, then I would not be looking forward to reading the third book. This book was mediocre at best, hence the rating. 2.5 stars was my original rating, but I'm giving it 3 stars because of the ending. Please let certain things happen and the love triangle be resolved. Please please please. 
 What I Did Not Like: 
 While my opinion of this book was overall pretty positive, there were still some things that I didn't. For one, I feel like the skeleton plot of this series is going in circles. Juliet is questioning her humanity, her sanity, her romantic feelings, her past, her being like her father. It gets tiresome, the woe-is-me attitude, the romance drama, the back-and-forth human/monster dilemma thing. I feel like nothing ever gets resolved, in any of the books. I understand that this book is part of a series, but each book could resolve something. 
 For example (and this might spoil things for book one, if you have not read it yet), how do we know if her father is really dead? How do we know if Edward is really going to die, or even Juliet, because of their animal attributes? Because I know Megan Shepherd LOVES her stupid little love triangle in this book, and so she wouldn't possible have Edward die. No, Juliet is going to be a hero and save the day by creating a cure for herself and Edward. And then she'll really have to choose between her and Montgomery. 
 Everything goes back to the romance in this book. Why would Juliet agree to help Edward? Where did Edward comes from, to begin with? OF COURSE he survived from book one. We can't just have someone important and a part of the love triangle die, can we? Is there no such thing as tragedy in books anymore? And why does everything have to be planned so that we get the "perfect" love triangle, waiting to be resolved in book three? Gosh I hate love triangles. I hate them so much. 
 The sad thing is, Juliet knows that she doesn't LOVE Edward like she loves Montgomery. She knows that her animal side is attracted to Edward, but she really LOVES Montgomery. Yet she keeps being an insecure pansy who doubts that Montgomery loves her, that she loves Montgomery. She's the equivalent of a modern-day bimbo floozy, in my opinion. Her knowledge in science and medicine isn't even that great, from what I saw in this book. STOP VACILLATING. Stop making dumb, rash, thoughtless decisions, like consorting with the wrong people. As "smart" as Juliet is supposed to be... she acts really dumb in this book. 
 So. I didn't like the romance, UNTIL Montgomery reappears. You knew he was going to come back. If Edward did, he would too. Once Montgomery was back, I breathed a little. Especially at the end. Although the end just sets up everything so that Juliet will throw herself into creating a cure for Edward. Montgomery will be jealous and angry, because he thinks it's a waste of time to try to help something that is an abomination, that shouldn't exist. AMEN. WHY DOES JULIET WANT TO SAVE EDWARD. He's a creature, a monster, something that shouldn't exist. He's no one's blood relation, not a human being, nothing. UGH. 
 Would I Recommend It: 
 Um. If you read the first one? Then yes, it is worth reading this sequel novel. Especially if you're a fan of Montgomery or Edward, in terms of the romance. By the end, things get pretty clear, in terms of the romance. This is a love-triangle-based series, so I know how important romantic decisions are. Heck, I'M glad the love triangle is (hopefully) resolved. I hate love triangles. 
 If you haven't started reading this series, hold off. Don't start reading until the third book comes out - or maybe don't bother at all. Especially if you absolutely hate love triangles. Because this love triangle might survive into the third book, who knows. It shouldn't though. 
 Rating: 
 3 stars. I think I liked this one about as much as I liked the first book - even though the ending of this one made me super pleased. These books have a way of balancing the good and bad, into a nice middle-of-the-road 3-star mixture. I cannot wait to read the third book, because of the way this one ended!

reference_books.title: The Butterfly Garden (The Collector #1)
reference_books.review_text:
This book borrows elements from The Silence of the Lambs, The Collector and a bad episode of Criminal Minds before then pulling them through a Sucker Punch shallowness filter to create one sloppy book. 
 I'm not trying to be mean, and there were elements to enjoy in this book but, I was not a fan. I would have quit at several different points but every year I try to finish a book that I hate. 
 Of course, I never think I will hate the book at the start. We all know that sinking feeling once you've just dug into a promising book only to realize: 
 Despite that feeling, I try to make myself finish one every year because I am a firm believer that you can learn as much about writing from bad writing as you can from good writing. And from this book I learned (or was reminded) that the following drive me crazy: 
 *Unrealistic dialogue with either no dialogue tags or unnecessary adverbial dialogue tags 
 *Unrealistic characters with unrealistic character motivation 
 *All telling and no showing 
 *Clunky exposition 
 *Horrible transitions 
 *One-dimensional good cop/bad cop FBI agents who are good because they have daughters and are bad because... they are bad... and because tension... 
 *Withholding information from the reader (and the interrogators) to try to add suspense but using completely illogical character motivation to do it 
 *Really anytime the Mary Sue Narrator decided to without info for no reason 
 *Generally wasting what could have been a great book structure (an interrogation) 
 *Introducing a love interest in the last third of a book... A love interest who may do the right thing? Or might do the wrong thing? But who is still also a rapist (or at the least is a piece of human garbage by taking advantage of the situation) and either an oblivious idiot or knowingly complicit BUT he is really good at the violin. 
 *Trying to manipulate the reader by introducing a character (another kidnapped and raped girl or "Butterfly") with down syndrome out of nowhere so she can quickly die by falling from a tree after imitating the narrator climbing a tree all while saying "I can be brave"-- Seriously? 
 *Use a play within a play... 
 *A "twist" in the end that meant nothing and did nothing because of no foreshadowing or stakes. 
 *And... 
 Oh screw it, I'm done thinking and reviewing this book. Do yourself a favor and read something else.

reference_books.review_text:
I've read and enjoyed several of Adam Nevill's short stories both in his first collection Some Will Not Sleep: Selected Horrors which featured the excellent "Pig Thing" and The Best Horror of the Year Volume Eight which featured his curious and slow burn short story "Hippocampus" (a story I wasn't impressed with on the first reading but grew to really admire after subsequent reads). 
 I kept seeing this novel (his first published in America) recommended as one of the scariest books to come out in the past 10 or 20 years and has been turned into a movie which comes out in the UK and Europe this October. Check out the trailer if you're interested. 
 So I picked up the book and thought I'd read the first chapter to see if it grabbed me, a couple hours later and I was done with the first part of the novel and couldn't wait to finish the second part where things take a turn in a very Black Metal direction (not Death Metal mind you). 
 While I think the Part Two: South of Heaven (obligatory Slayer link) does lose some steam and could have had 25-30% cut, I ultimately enjoyed the ending. I think that switch hits some readers as so jarring because of just how well plotted and fucking relentless Part One: Beneath the Remains (obligatory Sepultura link) reads. With short cliffhanger chapters I'm glad I had the time to read this as quickly as I did. 
 In his acknowledgements author Adam Nevill mentions several books essential to his research including Lords of Chaos: The Bloody Rise of the Satanic Metal Underground which covers the rise of black metal bands like Mayhem (or the fictional Blood Frenzy) and the church burnings and at least two murders that were related to that scene in Scandinavia in the early 90's. It's worth a read for metalheads and true crime weirdos alike (Just don't get lost in an internet black hole of reading about the stupid opinions/provocations of neo-nazi shithead Varg Vikernes [and stop listening to Burzum for fucks sake]).

sample_reviews.review_text: I had heard of this book (and Manson) for pretty much my whole life, but it wasn't until I read 2016 "The Girls" that I was inspired to read Helter Skelter. The book is very engaging, but was not quite what I expected. I thought it was going to be more of a biography of Manson and the Tate/LaBianca murders, but in fact it was an in-depth look at the trial and how Manson and the girls were convicted. Of course, details of the murders and Manson (and other's) motivations come out as part of the trial, so it served the same purpose. I realize this is a big "Duh", since the book is written by the trial attorney - which I have to say at times was annoying, since there were quite a few times where the author was basically saying "look how clever I am!" This book is definitely not a non-biased or balanced portrayal. A few minor criticism; it was very hard to keep track of everyone, since not only was there a ton of cops, lawyers, witnesses, "Family" members, but many of the people had aliases or nicknames and were referred to by first name, last name, or nick name at various points. Secondly, and this actually amused me, but there were 60s-70s terms used sometimes, such as having "rap sessions" with Manson. I just picture them all "yo let me tell you a story bout...."
Manson is a crazy SOB. Good read.

Classic true crime. Vincent Bugliosi may have a generous ego, but this book about his prosecution of Charles Manson confirms that he also had an unbending work ethic and even, at times, a sense of humor.
The author did a great job writing this book. It gave me chills throughout. It seems so unreal that one man could make all those people commit such horrible murders.
This took me back to my Tween years.
Haunting, clinically detailed and thorough, a must read for fans of true crime.

I recommend this book both for those who know the story, and those who don't. Manson, and most of his group of followers, are still serving time with life sentences, but the Manson legacy continues to live on.

Helter Skelter is the true crime classic written by the lead prosecutor of the infamous Tate-LaBianca murders that shook Hollywood in 1969, the man who heroically (it says here) withstood frequent incompetence by the LAPD, a bumbling cast of defense attorneys, and a violent band of burned-out cultists to secure convictions against the loony-toon Manson Family, much to the great relief of Middle America, terrified their teenage daughters might fall under the failed singer's sway. 
 It's hard to blame Bugliosi for taking this 600-page victory lap, given that he lost two years of his life investigating and trying this massive (and massively bizarre) case basically by himself, and getting a jury to convict was not necessarily a slam dunk. Manson was not in either house, after all, and there was a real dearth of physical evidence left behind to implicate the other four defendants. So the tone of self-congratulation coursing through the whole book? He earned it. 
 In terms of laying out how Manson's acolytes committed these savage crimes under his command, Bugliosi's exhaustive play-by-play of the entire case is peerless, a testament to the man's diligence and ferocious attention to detail. It is notably less successful in laying out why, beyond the stated motive of the impending race war that gives the book its name. Bugliosi is not a sociologist nor a biographer, and so only hints at what made the Family (particularly the girls) tick. 
 Nor is he a prose stylist. This book is about 20 percent too long, mired in names and dates and repetition; I suppose the prosecutor in him couldn't help including every detail, every aside, every decision (all favorable to Bugliosi, of course) to make his case to us.* 
 Final analysis: Hard to shake, vivid in detail, and certainly the point of departure for anyone interested in this sensational crime, but not quite definitive. 
 *To be fair: Before he died, Bugliosi published a veritable murder weapon of a book about the Kennedy assassination that weighed in at more than 1,600 pages. Helter Skelter is a beach read in comparison.
Bugliosi is a publicity whore, and sensationalizes these horrible murders to his benefit. Well-written, but...vile.

Interesting writing and a well known story. Since I was eight years old at the time and the whole incident has become legend, reading the story written at the time it happened offers a lot of information lost as the years have gone by. Manson seems less a demon than a common cult leader, albeit one who commanded a level of obedience that seems unreal. 
 Bugliosi doesn't glorify the violence as many true-crime books do these days. 
 Worth the time if you have any interest.

book_b.title: The Sherlockian
book_b.user_review: total guilty pleasure read

sample_reviews.review_text: I rather liked this! I don't get the 2 star ratings of this from other reviewers - it's a fun little read, and fairly well-written. It's very engaging, even for someone like me who isn't really a mystery fan and is a sort of passive Holmes fan.

I read this the first time in probably 2011 and gave it 3 stars but no review. I have just finished rereading it for my mystery book group and decided it definitely deserved 4 stars! A very well written book by a 28 year old that covers two time periods. It's a delight for anyone who loves Sherlock Holmes but I also think the average reader will come away having enjoyed this book. 
 Highly recommended!
I'd have given this book 10 stars if I could.
DNF at page 101. Just didn't grab me as hard as it could have.

This book was alright. I liked the story set in the past and that focused on Arthur Conan Doyle more than the contemporary storyline. It started out as a good idea, but I lost interest (in the contemporary story) towards the end.

I almost put this book down after reading the first chapter. The present-day characters, Harold and Sarah, whose search for a missing diary written by Arthur Conan Doyle, alternates with Doyle's efforts to solve a murder mystery, are wooden and unappealing. However, once the story shifted its focus to Doyle, I became captivated. For the rest of the book, I found myself plodding through the present-time chapters in order to enjoy the late-Victorian ones. 
 Sherlock Holmes fans will probably love this book and give it a higher rating than I did. Though I'm not a devotee, I would nonetheless recommend it for the gems of writing brilliance. 
 I was especially enchanted by the unfolding of Bram Stoker's character. In my favorite scene (this is NOT a spoiler), he expresses his feelings about the death of Oscar Wilde. The quality of the writing is of a much higher caliber than elsewhere. 
 This author can certainly write well. He just needs to do it more often.

I love a good mystery. By love, I mean I relish the oh-so-satisfying feeling of being wrapped up in a puzzle that is at once both imminently solvable and and hopelessly perplexing. I do not get to read as much of the genre as I would like (mostly because I do not get to read as much of any genre as I would like), so up to this point, I have mostly kept to the classics, namely Agatha Christie and Sherlock Holmes. Incidentally, yes, I lean toward Sherlockian rather than Doylean identification. I branched out into this bit of modern historical fiction by first-time author Graham Moore (son of Michelle Obama's Chief of Staff) thanks to a recent Barnes and Noble sale ($2.50 hardbacks with free shipping for orders over $25 is a terrible combination for my wallet). I have high standards for any book that casts Dr. Arthur Conan Doyle as a character, and Moore fortunately met them (mostly). 
 Before going any further with the review, I want to stop and say if you are a Holmes-fan or a Vicatoriaphile generally, this book is a no-brainer. The story moves back and forth from investigations conducted by Doyle himself and Harold in the modern day, a man obsessed (in an affably eccentric way) with Holmes and the romance of his time. To get a feel for the entire work, consider this: 
 Harold took a breath while he thought of how to proceed. "Look, I get it, I'm a white, heterosexual man. It's really easy for me to say, 'Oh, wow, wasn't the nineteenth century terrific?' But try this. Imagine the scene: It's pouring rain against a thick window. Outside, on Baker Street, the light from the gas lamps is so weak that it barely reaches the pavement. A fog swirls in the air, and the gas gives it a pale yellow glow. Mystery brews in every darkened corner, in every darkened room. And a man steps out into that dim, foggy world, and he can tell you the story of your life by the cut of your shirtsleeves. He can shine a light into the dimness, with only his intellect and his tobacco smoke to help him. Now. Tell me that's not awfully romantic?" 
 The novel walks the fine line of being self-aware in its characters' nostalgic longing for a time that did not really exist and overt goofiness. Harold knows he is somewhat ridiculous but does not care, and is effective in his investigation despite his penchant for the dramatic. I would compare the atmosphere to some of the more serious Basil Rathbone films. 
 Moore' writing is top quality, and the dual mysteries he weaves are engaging throughout the novel. Harold's quest seems the more traditionally Sherlockian of the two, but both are well laid out. The length of the book allows Moore to include more twists and turns than the standard Holmes story, some more or less obvious than others. My only criticism of the book is the same I have for many modern mysteries, which is that the book does not break any new ground. Moore seems to have stuck a little too closely to his source material when plotting out his book. This may not be a real problem, though, because I believe anyone familiar enough with the Holmes canon to notice this will still appreciate The Sherlockian for what it is: a labor of love. 
 So don your deerstalker, prepare your pipe, and delve into this sure-to-be intriguing investigation. 
 --Josh
Nice combination of historial and present day mystery, although the "big secret," when revealed, was kind of lame.

I really was looking forward to this book. The plot seemed good, and I was anxious to read it. What I got was a very poorly put together mystery story, a character assassination of historical figures, a horrendous understanding of turn of the century technology, and a protagonist's mystery solving ability which was more Hardy Boys than Sherlock Holmes.

The problem with the story's 2 distinct timelines is that the 1900 timeline with Arthur Conan Doyle and Bram Stoker is thrilling at times, while the Present Day timeline is a blander DaVinci Code with a vanilla, close to unlikeable hero. 
 To make matters worse, the end of the 1900 timeline story doesn't provide a narrative answer to why Conan Doyle decided to start writing Holmes stories again. This is a work of fiction: I wish the author had spun more of Baskerville into his story. 
 3 stars for the moments in the 1900 timeline where the story is chilling.

reference_books.review_text: My thoughts on this...First let me say this is Jordan Marie's first book. It's also one of my first MC books. It is also my first interracial romance book. That being said, the only thing shocking to me is how mobster-esque this seems to me. The violence was shocking. Not that I thought that they would stop on the side of the road and pick flowers, but the bathtub thing? Yeah, wow! (I'm also the one person in the USA that's never seen an episode of SoA, I think!) So, here we have Nicole, aka Mama, and Detroit, aka Dragon. They couldn't be more different if they were born on different planets. She's from money and affluence, though she disdained it. He was from .....well, I can't tell, because I'm afraid he'd hunt me down and put me in the bathtub. I'm from Kentucky and he's from Kentucky, so I'd rather be safe. Needless to say, he's from the wrong side of everything. But from the moment they met, snarky remarks and sparks flew. He was quite the demanding and naughty mouthed man. He didn't care who heard him say what. She wasn't such an experienced gal and though his words were exhilarating, she was a little afraid of him. (This would lend you to believe that she would roll over and let him run roughshod over here because he is such a dominating character....but you'd be sadly mistaken. This girl doesn't take his crap and gives it right back and she won't be kowtowed by him.) But that ended obviously and holy smokes when they got together...(https://textuallove.wordpress.com/201...) Read rest of review behind the link.

reference_books.title: Storm (Ashes & Embers, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
We meet up with Evelyn as she's heading to a meeting for work, trying to follow directions on her GPS when a snow storm derails her, thankfully, Storm Valentine, lead guitarist for Ashes and Embers is on his way up that very mountain. He saves her, only to get stuck himself, and they had to tuff it out in his truck for two days. And neither of them would come from this weekend unscathed. 
 She has been in a relationship for twelve years. He never wanted another relationship again. But they found themselves drawn to one another. 
 This is the first story in the Ashes and Embers series. I had already read Lukas, but thought I'd come back and read the first book. I didn't feel a connection with either Evie or Storm. But then I had a deep connection with Lukas and Ivy. That isn't to say that this book isn't well done, it just didn't have that connection with me that the other did. We did get to meet the other members of the band, including Lukas and Ivy. (The concert scene was really interesting being seen from Evie's POV!) And though I'm certain it'll make me ball, I'll probably get and read Vandal's story soon. But I'm pretty certain, I'll bawl. Just sayin'.... 
 Ms. Cole is creating this world were the men are absolutely dedicated. And by that I do mean absolutely. At least as far as Lukas and Storm are concerned, I cannot speak for the others, but wow. I really love that about her books that I've read so far. And this book does involve a love triangle between Evie, her boyfriend, and Storm, but really...there's no real triangle here. It's just that life is complicated and there aren't any clear-cut lines and sometimes the best way out of a sticky situation isn't always clean or easy. So I really appreciate that realness. So would I recommend this book to others? I would, because this band of men and family are very interesting and Ms. Cole does a really good job of building their world.

reference_books.title: Bound by Duty (Bound, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
We meet Amelia at Brighton College. She's an awkward girl who's not familiar with social graces. Her best friend is a Southern Peach and loves getting her out and involved and Bethany has a hankering for Micah. Off they go to a party and there, when Amelia tries to get away from everyone there, she meets Aiden. Amelia isn't your normal awkward girl though. She has this magic inside of her and she's supposedly someone important and engaged to the prince of this immortal race. Only, she never met this prince, she hadn't heard anything good about his mother the queen, and she just wants to be normal and do things normal girls do. But meeting Aiden...now he gets her heart and her magic singing. Only there's a big problem. He isn't the prince...and her time is running out and her magic is beginning to run amok. 
 I really liked Bethany and Cole and Amelia, even though she can be bratty sometimes. I understand why, I would be too, plus she's 18. There's still time for her to grow up. And we get to know Aiden's story. So, knowing his story, it makes these words more powerful than they'd be otherwise. 
 "Pick me, Amelia. Please, pick me. Be the one who finally picks me." 
 Honestly, my heart pitter-pattered and as if he weren't insta-book-boyfriend material before, THAT sealed it right there. I really liked his character and I am BEYOND excited to read the remaining parts of this series. 
 Ms. Smith writes a compelling tale. It's interesting how she gradually releases bits of it as the story unfolds. We're learning and confused and angered and afraid right along with Amelia. I have never read anything by this author before, and I am CLEARLY not understanding why I hadn't started reading this earlier, but BOY am I glad I did! AND DOUBLE BOY am I glad I waited until I had the whole series, because ummm...I'm not sure I'd be able to handle waiting for more. So would I recommend this book? Oh yes, I would. I am suggesting that you buy the entire SERIES before you start reading it because you'll want to read it all in one sitting. IT. ALL. Just trust me on this...

reference_books.review_text:
We meet Shay and Kellen at school. They're not a part of any crowd, in or otherwise. Everyone moves out of their way or does what they say. They're beautiful, their players, and their dangerous. Shay doesn't look like her brothers and sister. Where they're tanned and golden and beautiful, she has raven hair, pale skin, just as devastatingly beautiful. I can't tell you what I know, because it'll truly be a spoiler. I will only say that there are plot twists and turns and what you thought you know doesn't exist and what you didn't think existed is beyond real. I will say that I'm really impressed and I really liked how this book was. Gosh, I really wish I could tell you more! But this is one of those books, where I truly can't, you just need to experience it yourself. 
 This is the first book by Tijan that I've ever read. I have no idea what too me so long. She has this way of setting a scene that's mesmerizing and I swear there were a few times, my heart was skipping beats and I found myself biting my nails. I need to read more by Tijan now. :D So, would I recommend this book? You bet your bottom dollar I would!

book_a.title: Darker Water (Once and Forever, #1)
book_a.user_review:
Laney and Carson make amazing friends. They have that right amount of lightheartedness and depth for one another. Throw in the constant stream of come on's that Carson throws her way, and it's fun and flirty and sweet. Especially for a man who doesn't make friends easy....especially with women. And Laney, who's normally a doormat finds that she can truly be herself and make demands without feeling ridiculed and picked apart. And yes, things get physical between them. And things do get messy, and ugly and beautiful and right. I really enjoyed this story. I loved Carson and Laney together. They worked so well together, like a well crafted timepiece. 
 Ms. Stewart worked a wonderful story around how sometimes, a simple kiss can turn a frog into a prince, or sometimes a prince into a frog. And her ability to write such chemistry between two people and show just how COMFORTABLE love really is, is a wonderful treat. Most romance books the love is super passionate and rarely comfortable, but with these two characters, whether they realized it or not, were in love before they ever got down to business. So would I recommend...(https://textuallove.wordpress.com/201...) Read the rest of the review behind the link.

sample_reviews.review_text: Carson is a persistent one, "then we should probably go to my place instead. You can take off your clothes and get cleaned up." He knows how to make the girly bits tingly, "s***." He backed up and adjusted his pants, his clenched jaw expressing everything he was feeling. "Expect me to be inside you about four seconds after you say yes. And don't make any plans for the rest of that week." When his girl is nervous Carson knows how to concoct a plan, "I leaned towards her, peeling her fingers off her pants and whispering, "It'll be okay. Whenever you want to leave, squeeze"--I couldn't help myself--"my c***." Sometimes it's Laney who has to do the reassuring, "I don't want more than a c*** right now." Without turning to me, she reached over and wrapped her hand around my package. "I'm happy with the one I have." I liked this book I loved Carson.
Really good. Really funny, but with a bigger message to say.

Don't look at the cover and the title! It really don't have a think with the story. 
 Beside the bathtub, there is no reference of water...Yeah, I'm naive, I thought there would be a distinct link with water...nope. 
 But it's a great story, the characters are really likeble, reliable and everything positivly -able.

WOW! Is there an option to give this 10 stars? No, well there should be! 
 I LOVED this book. Maybe it came to me at a time when I needed this kind of rom com, maybe I just needed a new book boyfriend. Either way, I have found him. Carson Bennett is beyond drool worthy, and a player. Laney Temple is a young woman that has been wronged so many times that she now knows exactly what she wants - and it's not another prince (she'll only end up turning him into another frog anyhow). 
 When these two meet the sparks fly instantly. The comedic banter between these two will keep you roaring with laughter. They develop a friendship like neither of them have ever shared with another soul. They share their hopes and dreams, and a few stolen kisses, until one night they let go of all previous inhibitions and form a relationship that carries only one simple rule - DON"T FALL IN LOVE. 
 Easier said than done. The sparks that fly between these two could set a soaking wet building on fire. 
 Sure, there are some pretty predictable moments, but that's what romance novels do to us, they get us to automatically assume the ending, and most of the time we are usually correct. But that didn't matter with this book, the fact that it was an HEA is what drew me in. I wanted these two to make it. In fact, I pleaded with the Kindle to make it happen. lol 
 This is one love story that will steal your heart, and make you wish that the end of the book never appeared. Well done!

I am a sucker for the friends to lovers. My only issue would be: I didn't really feel any connection with Laney. I absolutely loved Carson and thought his character was perfectly done. I look forward to reading more by this author.

I really enjoyed this book! Carson was a great character, very funny and someone to easily fall in love with. A sweet romance, steamy love scenes and great characters, I am looking forward to more books in this series.

I absolutely LOVED this book!! 
 Review to come!

What a fun read! I laughed outloud at the witty dialogue so many times I lost count! I liked both Laney and Carson's charcters immensely. It was refreshing to read about a couple who were honest, blatantly honest at times, with each other. The angst is minimal but very well written; it's not over the top crazy scenarios which make me nuts. I could easily see why each character felt and acted as they did and felt for them both. I'm excited for the next book and Hayden's story!

a funny HEA story. characters were fun to read and "participate " in their interactions. Laney, tired of kissing all frogs and never finding a prince finally decides to give up on love. But she then meets Carson, who only wants FUN and wants to help Laney become stronger. ..but if love becomes involved, it all ends. Even with the romantic comedy, there is a deeper level in the book w the past abuse, but the way handled is very empowering and helps take the abuser out of power and give strength to the "weaker"...highly recommend and can't wait for more in this fairy tale series.

book_b.user_review:
We meet Ivy in New Orleans. She works for a secret order and protects humanity against those that they don't wish to believe were real. She meet Ren, a transfer from another branch of the secret order. Only, he's not all she thinks that he is, and she's not all that she believed either.  I liked Ivy. I liked Ren. I REALLY LOVED Tink! Just sayin'. Honestly, I'm not sure exactly what to say. If I gush about it as I want to, I'll give away too many of the twists and turns of this story. If I don't gush about it, you'll not really understand what's so great. So, what a conundrum I've found myself in. Just know this is truly an amazing book. TRULY. I am sad that the next book isn't out yet. I wished it were and it's set to be immediately on my TBR list when it does. 
 Ms. Armentrout is a new to me author. So many have recommended her, and I can completely understand why. She's an amazing author. This story isn't the YA I thought it was. It's more NA, but don't let that sway you. The nookie is there, but it isn't graphic. GAH! Ms. Armentrout has created such a vibrant world that it's hard for me to let it go so I can move on to the next book on my schedule. So, would I recommend this book? YES! But if you need the whole series in order to start, then you must wait. However, if not, I suggest you get it right NOW!

sample_reviews.review_text: That. Was. Painful.

At 88% I started skimming. This book is mind-numbingly long and boring. After getting through it all, I ended up skimming the grand finale. Total waste of my time. 
 How is there a secret society within a secret society without anyone in outside secret society knowing about it?? [Pg88] wow...talk about confusing and absolutely having no bloody sense. I mean, I'm pretty sure someone within the society had to know about it, or otherwise the stupid idiot wouldn't be blabbing it out to this girl. 
 She writes too internally. I really don't want to read pages-and-pages of her inner monologue thank you very much and I just found it so boring. 
 Could do with a good editor. As in cutting all the unnecessary words describing something. Sentences were also super long that it was just messy and confusing. 
 One bad phrase: He might have looked relaxed with his hands shoved into the pocket of his jeans and his legs crossed at the ankles. But anyone who walked by him knew he could strike at any given moment. [Pg 109]...Okay!! What the hell is right with this sentence? It's too long, there could've been one or two more commas and IT DOESNT BLOODY MAKE ANY SENSE. Why would someone know that he could strike at any given moment???? He's not a snake coiled up ready to attack, most people tend to just walk by people without a second thought, not 'oh god, that guy looks like he's going to attack someone'. 
 Also, didn't she just met this new guy and suddenly she's all in love. I mean, come on!! This is so unbelievable that it makes it impossible to get into the story. 
 Why are all guys sexy or hot or models? And the main guy just has to ride a motorcycle. I wish she was a bit more original. How cool would it have been if he drove an old green mini? It wouldn't have taken away his hotness, it would have made him a lot more likeable. 
 "Ron was stupid hot, as in the kind of hotness that made you want to do stupid, fun things you'd most likely regret later, but that didn't mean I trusted him a hundred percent." 
 Why are they all talking about sex and getting laid? I don't mind the main character thinking about it and doing whatever, that's fine. But then two other character talk about it in quick succession just gets boring. I mean they have all this drama with a secret world that might go up in flames, but yet they still want to talk about the hot cutie and getting some action. 
 Just started chapter 12 - this book seems to drag everything out, we keep getting boring everyday details of what she gets up to. I really don't want to keep reading these over-and-over again. This book turned into a chore to pick up, because I knew nothing was going to happen and I'd be slugging through the same old thing over-and-over again. Not something you want a reader to think, the only reason I read it is because I want to see the ending- to see what I think is going to happen happens. 
 Is it just me, or does the cover of this book just totally not suit the story inside? 
 "I've been fooled by a Winchester wannabe." - These stupid references are making me hate the book more. 
 they weren't just kissing or touching. Oh no, they were doing much, much more. - what age are you?? This is ridiculous, I'd rather be told what they're doing than this crap. 
 They were everywhere and there were so many of them. At least thirty - ...what?? How the hell does she count thirty when she's in a busy nightclub and you also do not lead with 'there were so many of them' when you're actually going to give the number...stupid writing. 
 I gave it one star...Because I'm a tiny bit curious on book two, but I'm not sure if I'm going to pick it up.

So far I don't think that I've read a Jennifer L. Armentrout that I haven't liked. There is something about her writing style that makes me fly through her books. They are really addicting. And fortunately this book didn't disappoint. I'm not saying that it's the best book ever, because it's not. The plot was predictable and the characters were a bit one dimension. However I couldn't stop reading. The world building was done well, it wasn't a complicated world, but still it was great. 
 Even though the characters weren't that complex they were still fun and enjoyable. 
 The thing a loved the most about this book were the references. I loved them. There was Harry Potter, Lord of the rings, Game of Thrones and lots of Disney princes. 
 ''You gave Tink a scarf. Tink is free. 
 I loved this scene. Especially Ren's confused look.

This book was pretty predictable book with characters that weren't exactly original...it was an okay read. It wasn't terrible and I didn't dnf so that's something, the book just did not make any lasting impact and I didn't connect with the characters. In fact the only character I did enjoy, mostly, was Tink. I definitely won't be continuing with this series, which is a shame as I really loved the Lux series. Perhaps part of why I didn't love this novel was because of Ivy, the heroine. I just felt no connection to her. The author who usually makes me love her characters didn't succeed in really drawing me into the world of the book and making the characters evoke emotion in me. I'm disappointed and I would advise to maybe give this one a miss.

I did not think that Jennifer could create a character as hot as Damon but she has done it with Ren. I could not put this book down. It kept calling to me to finish it and now that I have, I need more..... Can't wait for the next book. Hopefully it will be here before we know it.

PLEASE CAN YOU MAKE IT A SURPRISE GIFT RELEASE IT MUCH EARLY BECAUSE GAH. ANTICIPATION KILLS ME SLOWLY! BUTT!!! IT'S BETTER TO WAIT THAN NOT WAITING ANYMORE BECAUSE OF FINISHING THE BOOK.  The writing style for this book was like that of the 1800s. That's not necessarily bad, it just slowed down the pace and made the story less enjoyable for me. I much prefer this author's 1st person narrative. With that being said, it was perfectly edited.

1.5 stars 
 me after writing this review 
 Seriously though, I'm almost scared to actually rate this book it's so damn well beloved. The whole Lunar Chronicles series seems to be everyones and their mothers favorite and the third book especially people just go nuts about. 
 And really, I tried. I tried to understand the hype and with Cinder and Scarlet I kind of get it. But with Cress? I'm sorry, you lost me. 
 For me, reading it was tedious, boring and frustrating. But worst of all, I HATE ALL THE SHIPS. You all freaking love the ships and I just ... don't ... understand? 
 Cinder and Scarlet both got 3 stars from me. They aren't my favorite books, but I enjoyed them. The premise itself is okay, the execution is interesting and new and the characters are fun to read about. They also are rather fast paced and have a good length. In Cress pretty much everything I enjoyed in the first two books disappeared while the things I didn't enjoy stayed. 
 THE CHARACTERS ALL BORED ME 
 * Cinder had such great character development in the last book, but here? Nothing. Yeah, there's a second where she questions if the end justifies the means, but I guess the real exploration of that is coming in the last book, because it wasn't here. 
 * Scarlet barely is in the book at all, so we can skip her. 
 * All Wolf is doing is whining that Scarlet is gone, so let's skip him too. 
 * Thorne, oh Thorne. What happened to you? He was for sure my favorite character, but he was so dull. It almost felt like someone else wrote his scenes and tried to recreate the charme that Meyer gave him in the first two books, but failed. 
 * But my biggest issue by far is Cress. I'm really sorry, but she can fuck right off, she's so annoying. I get that she might be a bit weird and insecure after seven years in solitude, but that doesn't mean I have to enjoy reading about her. No matter what happens she is always blushing, shrieking and hiding. Her quirk of daydreaming I guess is I supposed to be cute, but it just wasn't. 
 THE WEIRD AND CREEPY SHIPS OF THE LUNAR CHRONICLES 
 Supposed to be cute, but isn't is also how I feel about pretty much all the ships in the Lunar Chronicles. One thing I don't understand is that people always talk about how much they hate insta-love, but I haven't seen anyone complain about the insta-love in here? It's literally every couple. Kai and Cinder, Wolf and Scarlet and Thorne and Cress all BARELY KNOW EACH OTHER. But even if I ignore the insta-love, Thorne and Cress might be the worst couple I've ever read about. I'm pretty sure Thorne is a sexually experienced adult who is at least 20 years old. Cress however might be 16 or something, but she acts like she's at most 13 years old. I don't know about you, but that creeps me the fuck out. I will NEVER ship them, because all I can see is a child and an adult men. Their relationship would've been so much better as a sort of sibling-relationship. But for some fucking reason everyone needs a love interest. Yeah I know this is supposed to be a fairy tail retelling, but can't we have a princess that doesn't need a prince to be happy? It just feels forced to me, 3 boys 3 girls and they all like each other! It's so convenient. 
 THE CONVENIENT AND THEREFORE TEDIOUS PLOT 
 But convenience and luck is also the basis of the whole plot, so I guess we have a theme here. Really though, am I the only one who is bothered by that? To give only one example: Cress and Thorne crash only a few miles from the city where the Doctor and Cinder currently reside and then Cress gets kidnapped, but don't worry because the kidnappers sell her exactly to the people she was looking for anyway! And it also turns out that the Doctor that is with Cinder is her father, surprise! That's only one instance, but it happens all the time. There's no excitement in reading a plot that just happens by chance. Apart from the last 50 pages there was no scheming or thinking at all and even that 'scheming' leaves much to be desired. 
 Safe to say I didn't enjoy the third installment of the Lunar Chronicles. The characters were bland and/or annoying and the plot was weak as hell. I was pretty determined to finish this series, but after reading Cress I wonder if I really will. It just seems that the whole series isn't really my thing and I just cannot understand the hype of it. Also the length of Winter and my investment into the characters and their lifes just doesn't add up. Maybe one of you can convince me to give Winter a chance.

Originally posted here. 
 One of my goals this year is to do more readalongs because they're a lot of fun. I read Three Wishes by Liane Moriarty along with two good friends, Janice and Holly. I first discovered Liane Moriarty, Australian author of contemporary fiction, when I read 
 What Alice Forgot 
 last year. I enjoyed it so much that I wanted to read the rest of her books. 
 The cute cupcake cover for Three Wishes is deceiving. I thought I'd be reading a book about quirky triplets, something light and fun. Maybe there would be a couple of problems thrown in but I definitely wasn't expecting the book to feel as emotionally heavy as it did. Also, the synopsis describes the book as a family comedy but I didn't think it was funny. The narrative does change from one Kettle sister to another but I feel like the focus is more on Cat's marriage problems and how her husband cheated on her. As a result, she's a very angry person throughout most of the book and that affects the dynamics with her sisters. It also felt like Cat, Lyn and Gemma weren't as close as they wanted people to think. Sure, they meet regularly and they talk to each other all the time, but it felt like they weren't really there for each other when it mattered. Now I don't want to mention spoilers but it did frustrate me that the sisters kept major life events from each other. Some snippets that I included in Goodreads status updates: 
 "The bills would keep on coming, no matter what else was happening in your life and that was good because it gave you purpose. You worked so you could pay them. You rested on the weekends and generated more bills. Then you went back to work to pay for them. That was the reason for getting up tomorrow. That was the meaning of life." 
 Also, this: 
 "Death was the hot bath you promised yourself while you endured small talk and uncomfortable shoes. You could stop pretending to have a good time when you were dead." 
 Not very cheerful, right? I'm sorry to say that I didn't enjoy reading Three Wishes as much as I was expecting. I wasn't invested in any of the Kettle sisters and I just wanted to finish the book so I can move on to a better one. It has taken me a while to write this review and I'm already on another readalong with Janice and Holly - we're reading Whiskey Road by Karen Siplin. We haven't been lucky in our readalong choices so far but I'm keeping my fingers crossed. If you're interested in giving Liane Moriarty's writing a try, I suggest that you start with What Alice Forgot. It was a more enjoyable read for me than Three Wishes. Although like I always say, people don't always react the same way even if we do share reading tastes so you might like this book a lot more than I did. I've seen more positive reviews so it may not just be a book for me.

Totally loved this book. It was so hard to put it down, and I enjoyed almost all of it. Although, some parts were kind of hard to digest. At some points, the book comes off as really cheesy and fluffy, and its hard to believe that the point of view is appropriate for 16-year olds. Despite that, the writing style was so, so amazing! And the shifts in POV were what made the book special.

"Eleanor tenia razon. Ella nunca se veia bien. Se veia como el arte, y no se suponia que el arte se viese bien, sino que se suponia que te hiciese sentir algo." 
 Ya desde Fangirl que Rainbow Rowell me deja con un pequeno vacio que debo llenarlo con algo: helado, un libro, cafe, fotos de Logan Lerman, cualquier cosa con tal de olvidarme. 
 En este libro, tenemos a Eleanor, una chica como cualquier otra, pero a la que juzgan casi todos. Tiene el pelo rojo, enrulado y muy desordenado. Viste extrano. Es timida, y no habla con nadie. Tambien tenemos a Park, quien viste siempre de negro. No es popular pero tampoco deja que lo tomen como un marginado. Es medio asiatico y le gustan los comics. Ellos se conocen cuando, en el autobus, Eleanor no sabe donde sentarse y Park (duramente) le dice que lo haga con el. De a poco se forma una relacion, ella mirando de reojo a los comics que el lee y este, dandose cuenta de que ella lo hace, le presta alguno para que Eleanor lo lea tranquila. 
 La historia me gusto. No comparto la misma euforia al igual que a mucha gente que le encanto. Se me hizo entretenido, pero no le llegue a agarrar el hilo de la emocion por la historia. En muchos momentos, las escenas se me hacian aburridas y las leia rapido para pasar a otra cosa. Ojo, eso no quiere decir que las veia innecesarias pero, personalmente, me hubiese gustado que diera otro giro. 
 Algo que me gusto mas que la historia, fueron las frases. Hay muchas de ellas que uno puede tomar y apreciar, leerlas y memorizarlas. Tengo un algo con los libros en los que si estos traen frases hermosas, es mas probable que me gusten mas que la historia misma. 
 El final me parecio brusco, me dejo con muchas dudas. Odio eso. Pero, creo que esto es lo que caracteriza a Rainbow Rowell, ya que en Fangirl ocurrio algo similar. 
 Tengo ganas de recomendar este libro a mucha gente que todavia no lo leyo. Y es que aunque yo le haya dado tres estrellas (me gusto) no significa que no marco algo en mi. Hubo muchas escenas que me dejo boca abierta y otras que pense que eran innecesarias. Pero a simple vista se ve que es un libro lleno de significaciones que a uno luego lo va llevando a entender muchisimas cosas. 
 Una cree que si abraza a alguien con todas sus fuerzas, lo tendra mas cerca. Una cree que se puede abrazar a alguien con tanta fuerza como para seguir sintiendo su presencia, grabada en ti, cuando te separas. Cada vez que Eleanor se separaba de Park, tenia la misma sensacion de perdida irreparable. 
 Ahora realmente quiero helado. Y alguien que me abrace.

You have been warned, my review will have many spoilers! If you haven't read the last book, please don't read this review! 
 Now what I loved about the book was that finally reader's got to know the Darkling's backstory. Since the first book, I wanted to know what his life was like, and what made him become that way. Though, I am not fully satisfied with his story. I also appreciated that Baghra revealed her past as well. At first, I thought that Morozova might have been the Darkling's father, but he's not. In fact, he is the Darkling's grandfather. 
 I also loved the side characters especially Genya. I loved the scene where the King tries to accuse her of treason, but she stands up for herself. She is definitely one of the characters that I loved from the start. She proved that she could be a badass: 
 Na razrusha'ya. I am not ruined. E'ya razrushost. I am ruination. 
 I was so happy that she and David finally got together. I was rooting for her happiness the whole time. I loved that Genya had her happily ever after. 
 I loved the Alina and Nikolai moments in this book. I got so excited when Nikolai showed up in the book! 
 "Being around Nikolai was always like this, watching him shift and change, revealing secrets as he went. He reminded me of the wooden nesting dolls I'd played with as a child. Except instead of getting smaller, he just kept getting grander and more mysterious." 
 I just love the way he showed up in the book: 
 "I saw the prince when I was in Os Alta," said Ekaterina. "He's not bad looking." 
 "Not bad looking?" said another voice. "He's damnably handsome." 
 Luchenko scowled. "Since when--" 
 "Brave in battle, smart as a whip." Now the voice seemed to be coming from above us. Luchenko craned his neck, peering into the trees. "An excellent dancer," said the voice. "Oh, and an even better shot." 
 "Who--" Luchenko never got to finish. A blast rang out, and a tiny black hole appeared between his eyes. 
 I gasped. "Imposs--" 
 "Don't say it," muttered Mal." 
 Overall, I just loved Nikolai in this book. Now one of my favorite moments between Alina and Nikolai was probably the meteor shower part. I really wanted Nikolai and Alina to be endgame so badly. Nikolai respected Alina, he accepted her for who she was. I wanted them to get married at the end of the book. I liked how Mal tried to be more of a friend for Alina, instead of love interest. I thought that the book was going to end with Alina and Nikolai's relationship. My heart broke when Nikolai became one of The Darkling's shadow soldiers. Nikolai went through so much. Even though he was able to return to normal, he lost a bit of himself after the battle. I was happy that he was finally able to become King. 
 I did like Mal much more in this book than the two previous books. I did not like Mal in the second book. He was very insecure in the second book. This book changed my view on him. I liked how he was willing to sacrafice himself and his happiness for Alina. He put Alina first and he wanted her to marry Nikolai. Mal thought it was best that Alina if she were Queen. I like Mal as her friend rather than boyfriend. Mal is a good character, but I feel that Nikolai and The Darkling are far more interesting than him. 
 I really thought that the Firebird was going to be the amplifier. I would have never imagined that Mal would be the amplifier that Alina needed. I had to put the book down when I read that part, because I was a bit shocked. I took some time to think about Mal being the amplifier and it may have been a bit obvious, but I didn't see it at first. I really liked that twist. Alina couldn't have found the other two amplifier's without Mal's help. 
 Lastly, I am glad that Alina is not one of Morozova's descendants. For a second, I thought she was related to the Darkling, and thank goodness that was not the case! 
 Now here's what I didn't like about the book. For the last book in the series, I was hoping for it to be longer. Like a 100 more pages would have been better. Secondly, I really wanted there to be more Darkling in this book, he appeared way less than I would have imagined. I did like his interactions with Alina, but he hardly appeared in this book! I really wanted the Darkling to redeem himself at the end, but he just proved to be evil. I didn't want him to die! I wanted Alina to save him. 
 Also, I thought the battle between The Darkling and Alina was going to be a bit more epic. I felt a bit sad during his funeral. 
 "Aleksander." 
 His eyes fluttered shut. "Don't let me be alone," he murmured. And then he was gone." 
 Where was the strong Alina from the second book? I felt that she lost her motivation to her cause. She felt much more weaker to me. Not as a strong leader I was hoping her to be. Alina could have done so much as a Queen!!! The ending was bittersweet for me. I really wanted Mal to stay dead. 
 I felt that Alina could have achieved much more with Nikolai. She could have reformed her country. I just didn't like how Alina wanted to fade into the background either! Even though she lost her power, she could have at least tried to become an ambassador or worked in the court. Though she settled down with Mal, I feel that he kinda hinders her growth as a person...

I feel that as a couple, they would have been able to achieve much more reform as rulers. I do feel that they are a power couple. I am really sad that they were not endgame.

sample_reviews.review_text: Finding love is like freeing your soul. A.L Jackson makes me feel that love is the strongest, most powerful thing we could ever have. "Hearts have a way of finding their own way home." 
 This is a cheesy way to start a review, but oh goodness, this book pulled on my heartstrings. Although I often enjoy a book, and I generally feel a connection with well-written characters in a novel, it's not so common that I feel genuinely emotional whilst reading a book. I went through pretty much every emotion on the spectrum during the course of A.L. Jackson's Come to Me Quietly, though. The novel is a beautifully written account of two broken people trying to repair what they once had. Jackson's novel has so much feeling throughout - love, passion, self-destruction, pain, longing, forgiveness - all of which come together and form an achingly captivating story that will stay in your mind long after you've read the last page. 
 Come to Me Quietly is a dual-perspective novel told, in alternating chapters, from the point of view of both Aly and Jared. Aly is a young woman who has simply gone through the motions - living life, but not really feeling it - after the sudden departure of her best friend Jared, when she was only 14 years old. Jared had his reasons for leaving. He needed to escape everyone. Everything. Six years on, and he's still struggling with his demons, convinced that he doesn't deserve anything good in his life. Things all change for both of these characters, however, when Jared finds himself on an old friend's sofa, and is awakened in the middle of the night by none other than the girl he left behind so many years ago. 
 Although startling at first, these two characters quickly fall back into the role of best friends but, far from being the young teenagers they were six years ago, they find themselves struggling with feelings for one another - both old and new. The relationship develops slowly between the two characters. Oh, how I love a fictional relationship with a slow burn. It simmers at first, and slowly becomes more and more passionate until it's something outwith their own control. I loved how realistic and emotional the whole thing felt, and I wish more novels had the same kind of captivating, fervent romance. 
 Aly was a wonderful heroine. Far from the Bella Swan archetype that is often found in YA and NA romance, Aly is passionate, strong and determined. She is determined to help Jared through his self-loathing and self-destructive tendencies, and prove to him that he is more than deserving of the love that she's held for him for so long. 
 Jared broke my heart many a time during the course of the novel. He was a fantastic character with many complexities, and the level of dedication and respect he held for Aly throughout the novel was very admirable. I often wished that he'd stop torturing himself but, when you find out the details of his past, it becomes clearer why he feels he is undeserving of love and kindness. 
 By the end of this novel, as I said earlier, I was a bit of an emotional wreck. I thought about the novel for days after, and found it difficult to read anything else for a week or two after I finished it, because nothing gripped me or evoked the same kind of emotional response as this novel did. I'm very excited to read the sequel to this novel, which is waiting on my Kindle as I type this! 
 If you're a fan of second chance love stories, and love a book that will make you feel as though you've been on an emotional rollercoaster by the time you're done, then Come to Me Quietly is the book for you. I absolutely loved it, and I would highly recommend it to fans of similar genres.

Aly Moore grew up running behind her older brother Christopher and his best friend Jared. Come To Me Quietly was the first book I'd read by AL Jackson, but most certainly not the last! Her writing style was a little different than what I was used to, but God did I love it! She has a way of making you feel so deeply with her words. They grab a hold of you and don't let go, they leave you begging for more. 
 Jared and Aly's story touched me all the way through to my soul. I felt their heartbreak, when there was heartbreak, their joy, when there was joy, and their love all throughout. 
 Jared is a troubled man, unable to see through his pain. He feels he should suffer for things that have happened in his past that he really had no control over, but is too blind with rage and self-hate to see it. 
 Aly is an amazing young woman, who has loved this man her whole life (even when she was a little girl and he was just a boy), but never dared to let anyone in on her secret, especially when they were children. Jared took off at the tender age of 18, she was hurt, heart-broken, and has always felt something missing. 
 When Jared finally comes back to town years later and they come face to face, neither one knows what hit them. Aly is immediately flooded with all those feelings she's kept hidden for so long, and Jared is thrown for a loop when he discovers he has feelings for this beautiful girl. Although he does not believe he is worthy of this girl who is so good, the light, when he is so bad, and dark. He feels undeserving of love and happiness and does not think he's allowed it. And this is where their real story begins... 
 This book totally unraveled me. It tore me open and put me back together, but I still feel like a piece of me is missing. I cannot wait to read the next book in this series. I don't think I'll be whole again until their story is finished! 
 Thank you Amy, for this absolutely Amazingly wonderful story!!!

 I really loved Come To Me Quietly. It was a great story and I couldn't put it down. While this isn't my first book from AL Jackson, I am always impressed with her beautiful writing. If you haven't read anything by her yet, this is definitely one worth taking a chance on. 
 After everything that he has been through, Jared doesn't believe that he deserves to find love since he destroys everything he touches. But when he returns to town and runs into an old friend, he finds himself staying with Christopher and his sister Aleena. Chris and Aly had once been his best friends, but neither of them are the same people they once were, especially Aly. Though Jared is drawn to Aly, he is determined to stay away from her since he knows that he would only destroy her. But it becomes harder and harder to fight what is between them, and Aly is just as determined to show him that what they have together is worth taking a chance on. 
 I absolutely loved both Aly and Jared. They had so much history and I was instantly captivated with their story. I had to know more about them and what all had happened to make Jared leave everything behind. My heart broke for him as he was so hard on himself. I just knew there was so much to this sweet guy that you didn't know and I couldn't wait to find out what it was. Aly was perfect for him, and I was so glad that she didn't give up on him. She gave him exactly what he needed and I couldn't have imagined anyone better for him. Their chemistry was strong, but it was their undeniable connection that made them such a special couple. 
 I will say that there were times that Jared frustrated me with how down on himself he got. He kept pushing Aly away because he didn't believe he was good enough for her, and after awhile it got a bit old. I still really loved the story and the characters, but that was what kept this one from being a five star read for me. I am excited that AL Jackson has continued their story in another book. While there is a good stopping point here, there is room for more and I am excited to see what happens next for them. I highly recommend this one to NA fans and readers who love emotional romance stories. 
 **ARC Provided by Publisher**

First off this book probably pissed the he'll out of me. 
 To start, the beginning of this book was boring. It took me so long just to go to 100 pages. there was so much background information that I felt was not necessary. 
 Second, the way the story was told was confusing. It was told like the present but in the past. I was confused some of the time. I had to re-read some sections again. 
 Third, the relationship was annoying I hated how it turned out. 
 Fourth, I absolutely HATED the ending. I felt like nothing was answer for me. It felt very incomplete. I just wish for more answers but no....... 
 The storyline was decent but it took too long in my opinion. it could have been shorter. the one thing I really like in this book was the friendship until the author decented to ruin it. That right there 100% pissed me off.

reference_books.title: Of Neptune (The Syrena Legacy, #3)
reference_books.review_text: This book was so good at the beginning, but then it slow down drastically. I felt like some of the sections were not necessary. It was so boring towards the middle. Emma was such a frustrating character but I understand what she was feeling but still she made some of the dumbest decisions. However the ending totally made it up for me. If the ending was bad, i would of given this book a really low rating, but I love the ending. I do feel like this could of been a two book series. That is just my opinion.

reference_books.title: Lips Touch: Three Times
reference_books.review_text:
1. The first story was okay. I like the story line. It was good. 
 2. The second story was decent. Again story line was good. 
 3. The third story was horrible. I had the hardest time getting through it. I felt like it was lacking something. I could not for the life of me finish it. I finally pushed myself to read it. It was so boring. I was so disappointed in this story line. 
 However I love the pictures in the story. They were just fanatically drawn. I love that the most in the book. 
 I give this book an overall 2.5 rating.

book_a.title: The Lovely Bones
book_a.user_review:
** spoiler alert **

I felt that there was so much that could of been taken out. For me there was too many pointless scenes. This book was so boring, it was so hard for me to read. It did not interested me as I read on. I really wish she could of shorten the book. It was still a good book but it was too long in my opinion. I was very upset at the ending. They never ended up finding her body and they never caught the guy who did even though you, as the read, knew from the beginning who it was. I was very upset, but I guess maybe she wanted to end it realistically. I don't know but I really didn't like it. Also I didn't like how she wrote the mother. I understand that it was hard for her, but still to cheat isn't something I think someone would do during those times, but hey it is whatevers. I wont say that this would be something I would read again, but it is not the worst book I have read. It was an okay book for me.

I hated this book.

It took me a little while to get into this book, but once I did it was fascinating. Narrated from such a unique viewpoint. I can see why it was made into a movie, it reads very much like a movie. Absolutely amazing!

I would actually give this 3 1/2 stars and maybe 4, because I honestly couldn't put this book down. I think I gave it 3 because I like happy endings and this book started out with an unhappy ending so it was hard for me to read. The author did a really good job with the characters and their emotions, although there was a scene in the book that I thought "Really? She chose that to be her wish?" and when you read it, you'll probably understand what I mean!

So here's the summary: Beginning of the book, amazing; middle of the book, slowly gets annoying but didn't lose interest; end of book, stupidest ending ever! Not satisfying and honestly... 
 SPOILER 
 The dead girl inhabiting another girl's body and using it to have sex with her ex boyfriend??? WTF???? I know the point of the book is to appreciate life while you have it and it has a charming way of making you feel warm and sad at the same time. I loved that about it, but they didn't even catch the bastard that killed her and they never found her body???? How unsatisfying an ending is that??? And I hate the tendency for contemporary authors to HAVE to put sex into their books even when it's creepy and unnecessary. Sharing a kiss with her ex would have been sweet on many levels. The author didn't need to take it that far, but she had to go there. Ugh.

When I picked up this book a few years ago, I'd heard only good things about it and, as such, didn't even fathom that I would dislike it. Oh, how ill-prepared I was. 
 Now, it has been years since I read this and I am nowhere near willing to pick it up again, so I apologize for not going into specifics. The writing did nothing for me. I could tell the author was going for something pretty and poetic with her descriptions, but often, it just came across nonsensical. Even though I was privy to Susie's most intimate thoughts, I found myself uncaring towards her. She didn't hook me, she didn't interest me, and that is the kiss of death for a book. I didn't care about Susie, I didn't care about what she was doing. The supporting characters fell flat to me as well, and, without any interest in any of the characters, I just could not appreciate the plot. I remember forcing myself to finish this, thinking that it must get better, there must be a reason for such high praise. Sadly, it seems that this book just wasn't for me.

Could not finish. The story idea was a good one but it was not well executed. The characters were hard to like and the plot was dragging and never got interesting. The writing, well, I have seen much better. I tired and I tried to finish but there was nothing holding me in the book: the language, the characters, nor the plot.
I just really liked the writing style - and the suspense in place where, even though you know what happened to her, you're kept turning pages to see if and when other people might learn that.
