book_a.title: Beneath the Truth (Beneath, #7)
book_a.user_review:
You know I have very mixed feelings about Beneath the Truth... and it has nothing to do with the book itself. I picked up the first book in this series Beneath This Mask, and gave this new author a shot. Sometimes as a blogger you get a winner and sometimes not so much, when trying out an author that is new to the Indie publishing space. With Meghan March I knew that I'd hit a gold mine! I was so excited reading that first book in the series. Meghan's thoughts were tied together seamlessly and it's very rare that a new author gets a five star out of the gates from me these days.... My first review brings back memories... 
 "I absolutely LOVED this book.. Hands down one of the best reads from a new author I've read this year. I was gripped from the beginning of the story right up until the end. It will keep you guessing and on your toes, as each chapter seems to bring more drama and intrigue to the story line. Charlie is one strong heroine, even though she doesn't appear to be in the beginning, in the end she shows the bravery of a thousand soldiers marching into battle. I give this one my full 5 stars! I loved it beginning to end and I highly recommend it." ~ Review from Beneath This Mask 
 So why the mixed feelings.... Simply put I DON'T WANT IT TO END!!!!!!! I have loved these characters from the very beginning of this series. I have followed them through the ups and downs and the crazy plots that Meghan weaved throughout this series. It's not often I feel such an attachment to a group of people that aren't real, that I could never meet in person, yet feel that every one of them is real, and I could just fly to NOLA and meet them at Con's tattoo parlor. That's how much this series pulls you in. This last and final book in the series is bittersweet. After Beneath these Lies, and Shadows, I had no idea what Meghan had left in store for us. Both of those books had whopper's of a storyline, but I knew that Rhett was something special through this series, and she did not disappoint in delivering on his book and the ending to this series. 
 What I didn't expect was how much I would love the heroine in this story. She's completely awkward, her mouth runs away from her when she's nervous and she's had an unrequited love of Rhett since she was a little girl. Ariel is a spunky business woman that has paved her way from awkward teenager to make a name for herself. The problem is that when she has to return to her hometown and come face to face with the man she loved all her life, she isn't as over the feelings as she tried to tell herself... Ariel is one hell of a heroine and she's not afraid to tell it like it is, even if she's not eloquent in her delivery, you love everything about her! 
 I always knew that I loved Rhett, but I loved him even more in this book. He's not afraid to go after what he wants even if he feels he doesn't deserve it. Based on the scandal that has once again rocked his family, he's faced with some tough issues and decision to make. When Ariel's safety is threatened he will stop at nothing to get to the bottom of why she's become a target in this ongoing scandal that has rocked his family... I wasn't sure where Meghan was going to take this story or these characters and boy was I shocked when I realized the "Truth"! The bombshell was quite unexpected and what happened at the end was shocking to say the least, Meghan had stretched her wings with some pretty grave situations but this one really took me by surprise. In a good way. 
 That is all I will say about the ending I don't want to ruin it. Overall this series is simply one of the best I've read, with the exception of one of the books they all ranked a 5 star rating from me, which is in its own right amazing, since series usually end up dwindling off for me after a few books. Meghan keeps each book in this series engaging, intertwining the characters so they all have a place throughout the entire series of books. Beneath this Truth couldn't have been a more fitting end to this series. Even if I don't want it to be over! If you have not read any of these books I highly encourage you to read them. Meghan's had many books in between and her hero's and heroine's are all amazing, but this series has a special place in my heart, since it's where it all began for her! Take the time and read these books. I promise you won't be sorry!

sample_reviews.review_text: This has to be my most favorite book in the series. Loved the suspense and mystery and how we got to see glimpses of all the previous characters. You rocked it out of the park!

Deception, betrayal, secrets follow Rhett and Ariel, who have an uphill battle in finally getting that HEA. Rhett must confront his past and the secrets that have surrounded his life for way to long, Ariel returns for vastly different reasons or so she thinks. With each page turned, the story twists and turns as the plot thickens, literally. I was captured from the very beginning and with each page turned I was drawn deeper and deeper, laughing, crying, cheering and gasping in disbelief as everything is finally revealed. This book had me enthralled, so much so, that I couldn't put it down until the very end. Great job Meghan.

5 stars!! 
 I really did love everything about this book. The story line is action packed - full of twists, drama, conflicts. It really keeps you on your toes trying to figure everything out. It's an exciting and thrilling read as well as sexy as hell. I totally recommend reading and I can't give away too much without alluding to a spoiler. 
 I do need to gush about this book couple though - Team Awesome (Ari & Rhett)! This is the best couple I've read in some time. Now, as much as I love the romance genre, I do take issue with the heroines many times. I always want them to have more gumption, self-confidence, not get steam-rolled by the alpha hero, etc, the list goes on. Ari is smart, witty, confident, strong-willed, and just the right amount of quirk. Rhett is a total alpha but realizes he can't "own" her, control her, or put her on a pedestal. They both agree they are stronger as a team in life, but he can still totally boss her around in the bedroom.

PDL's Review: 4 Punches (Liked) 
 I haven't read every single book in this series just yet, but 3 out of seven and I already know it's a series I am determined to back track. From what I know, the author does an amazing job of getting us to fall in love with the characters instantaneously and all we do is root for them. 
 Just from the last 2 books and this final one, I can confidently say that there is no better ending to a series - on that note, it confirmed that I WILL be going back to start from book #1 without a doubt.

This is the last book in this series and its everything I could have wanted and more. You will follow in love with Rhett! This book will take you to so many different places but the emotions are so worth it in the end.

Beneath the truth had an explosive beginning literally and an emotional explosive ending. When former detective Rhett Hennessy returns home to find his family home has gone up in explosive flames, Rhett is determined to clear his father's bad name of being a bad cop and finding out who is responsible for blowing up the family home. Rhett is thrown together with his best friends little sister Ariel Simpson now a powerful CEO of her own computer company. Ariel thought she had gotten over her childhood crush on Rhett until they need to come together to save each other from someone evil. I have loved this whole series, every book has been brilliant and this one was no exception. The characters were lovable, strong and engaging. The sex was hot. The story line was full of twists and turns and threats that no-one could ever see coming, and it all concludes with a final visit from all the characters from the previous books. Very sad to see this series end.
Love this book!! Absolutely love this series!!

What I've come to realize about Meghan March's writing, is that she always writes with her whole heart and soul and it just SHINES through with every turn of the page! Yes, this is the first book that I've read in this series, but I'm no stranger to the BRILLIANCE that is Meghan March. Her brand of storytelling transports me to another world, where all of my worries and all of my problems disappear, if only for a little while. Her writing skills are impeccable. Her characters are magnificent. Her prose is both captivating and beautiful. She brings ALL THE FEELS and ALL THE EMOTIONS with Rhett and Ariel's story. It's EPIC! It's BEAUTIFUL! It's HEART WRENCHING! It's pretty damn SENSATIONAL! 
 "I refuse to be anyone's mistake. if anything, I'm a goddamned privilege." 
 I wanted to start off with a quote from our heroine, Ariel, because she is by far, one of my FAVORITE female characters that Ms. March has ever created. I like her style. I love her sass. I was complete infatuated with this woman from the very beginning. Since this is the first book I've read in the Beneath Series, and I only got a little taste of Rhett Hennessy, I still knew that Ariel, was going to be one hell of a match for our hero. Because this is what Meghan March does. She gives us a gorgeous, alpha male hero and pairs him with the only woman who can bring him to his knees. Ariel shows us a vulnerability about her, but at the same time she is independent and confident. I absolutely adored her and I saw right away that she was going to be perfect for our beloved hero. 
 "I'm going to touch every inch of you. Memorize you. Drive every other thought from your head except how perfect you are. How much you matter to me." 
 Cue all of the SWOON! I mean, can this man be any more PERFECT! Typical of all of Ms. March's men, I fell and I fell HARD for Mr. Rhett Hennessy. This man was EVERYTHING! I'm sure fans of this series will say that the author saved THE BEST FOR LAST! I can see all of the reviews now. The think I loved most about Rhett was that he kept reassuring Ariel of her worth and of her beauty. It was so incredibly beautiful. It made my heart want to burst right out of my chest. Trust me when I say that Rhett Hennessy will make you feel ALL THE THINGS! 
 "Tell me you want this as fucking bad as I do, Ari." 
 "I want it all." 
 This was a happily ever after that I wanted to devour over and over again! I can't tell you how hard I fell for every single character...how excited I got for every single sex scene...and how my chest hurt with every single emotion that was displayed between these amazing lead characters. Although, this is the end of the Beneath Series, I'm even more excited at what's to come from this incredible author. I'm not only certain that she gives the readers EXACTLY what they want with Rhett's story, but I'm EXTREMELY CERTAIN that she did this series and these amazing characters, justice. I can only hope that I did this review justice with how much I absolutely ENJOYED this story and this author's work. 
 Meghan March is a force to be reckoned with in the romance genre. She gets better and better with every new release, and I've quickly depended on her to be a GO TO author for me. I can assure you that you will not only love Rhett and Ariel's story, but you will become addicted to the storytelling that Meghan March so eloquently represents. I'm kicking myself for not finding this author and this series sooner. Even though BENEATH THE TRUTH is the final book in the series, you can be rest assured that I plan on inhaling EVERY SINGLE BOOK in this series. I'm just so grateful that this can be read as a standalone, because I wouldn't want to miss out on the initial excitement that this book will most definitely bring!

 Beneath the Truth is the seventh book in the Beneath Series by Meghan March, but don't worry about starting here even if you haven't read the previous books. This one is a standalone story that is able to be enjoyed even if you are brand new to this series. This series was my first experience with Meghan March's books and I fell in love with her writing style. I have enjoyed it from start to finish, and this series will always be special to me. That being said, Beneath the Truth was so good and just might be my favorite of them all! 
 Ex-detective Rhett Hennessy has been living life off the grid since everything he thought he knew about his life was turned upside down. Determined to solve a case that hits close to home, Rhett returns to New Orleans to find answers. But what he never expects is for his best friend's little sister Ariel to complicate everything. 
 I loved Ari and Rhett. Ari was so strong and sassy, and I loved that she wasn't the same girl she had been when Hennessy had known her before. She was so real and genuine, with a ton of depth to her, I felt like she was exactly what Rhett needed. Rhett was impossible not to love! He was sexy and alpha and I couldn't get enough of him. I loved the history between these two and the forbidden nature of their relationship. This is always a favorite trope of mine, but these two were just perfect! Their chemistry was strong and I loved the banter and intensity of their connection. 
 Overall, I felt this was a really great end to the series and I am sad that it is over. While this can definitely be read as a standalone, I highly recommend the entire series. I have loved each book and I think that they are books that fans of romance and suspense will enjoy. Meghan March does a great job of hooking the reader right from the start and keeping them interested until the last page. The Beneath series is filled with sexy alphas, likable heroines, suspense and twists to keep you guessing and the romance is done as only Meghan March can. I can't wait to see what she has in store for us next, and whatever it is I will definitely be reading it.

book_b.user_review:
It's always terribly hard to write a review when it's not the popular opinion but I was offered an ARC in exchange for an honest review. I had never read a Katy Evans book for before this one. Between the cover and the synopsis I thought for sure this would be a WINNER for me... Now I preface again I didn't read any other books in this series, and my reason for disliking this didn't have anything to do with not understanding what was going on. 
 The one thing that I did like was that Katy made it so that this book was a stand alone, you understood that Tahoe and Regina were best friends of another couple and that's really how they met. That part was clear to me, so I wasn't confused at all. 
 For me the book from the beginning had promise but very quickly fell apart. The scene that was setup at the beginning was great! The party, the atmosphere, I got a good sense of what type of MAN Tahoe was, but then his interaction with Regina seemed so forced and unnatural. I got that he was trying to not like her because he didn't think he was good enough and couldn't commit, but it was a lackluster at best first interaction between them. I felt no heat and no real connection with them at all. Everything was all telling and not showing, and very monologue heavy which is something I hate. 
 I kept going hoping that Katy would reel me back in and make me fall in love. Then in the next few chapters it started jumping all over the place, we go from this party and are very quickly jumping months ahead with nothing real happening. We get lots of monologue from Gina about how she puts on makeup to hide, but never got a sense of what she was hiding from? Was it all just because her ex walked out on her? Idk. It just didn't make sense to me at all. The most confusing part to me was her job, it said that she'd been in college. But now she's working just at a cosmetic counter in a department store, I don't understand at all why? Was she a college drop out? It didn't make any sense that this smart girl was stuck in this job, if she'd gone to college. I kept waiting for Tahoe to offer her a job or something at his company so she could keep her apartment that she loved so much. I truly felt like this was a major disconnect. 
 When Gina starts to date Trent, I was completely perplexed. There is one scene where particularly, I couldn't understand AT ALL why this girl would call Tahoe, not only that she called him, but that he came, picked her up, and then stayed with her. *smh* I kept thinking did that really just happen??? Gina, doesn't seem to like Trent at all, he is so much like her EX that she repeatedly says it yet she keeps dating him hoping she will connect even though she's practically in love with Tahoe, and for what reason I still don't get, because he was literally sleeping with women constantly and right in front of her, continually. Trent was literally a doormat. But his constant comments about her hair, they were just creepy and everything about their relationship felt completely forced. I just didn't understand why Gina would keep dating him when she clearly had nothing in common with him. 
 All in all the book didn't connect for me on many levels, and the fact that it takes until 88% for anything to really get going and then seems to end really abruptly. I wish that I could have loved this book, but I just really couldn't get past all the things that made no sense and feeling no connection between the characters. Even when they did finally get together I didn't at all feel like they fit as a couple. Sadly it just didn't work for me at all.

Katy Evans has a style of writing that I find completely irresistible. Her men always seem to be primitive and predatory, described as lions or panthers or similar and I get kind of obsessed about them. Actually, I get TOTALLY AND COMPLETEY BLOWN MY MIND OBSESSED ABOUT THEM. 
 Remy? Malcolm Saint? Yes please. 
 So, now we're at Tahoe, Saint's friend. The Ladies' Man. 
 Oh, yeah. 
 This book is about the delicious tension and attraction and development of a relationship between a manwhore and a woman who has been hurt in love. While that's not a new idea, the way this is written makes it feel totally new, totally unique, totally fresh and spellbinding. 
 I've been reading so many awesome books lately. Add this one to the list. Zillions of stars and I want to reread already.

I loved Manwhore and when I met Tahoe Roth I knew I wanted to read his book, he was truly a ladies man. He was so much more, he swept me off my feet and I fell for him so hard. 
 Full review to come.

** ARC PROVIDED BY THE AUTHOR FOR AN HONEST REVIEW ** 
 Having not read any of the other Man Whore books I wasn't really sure what to expect and I have to say I was thrilled with what I got to read. This book was a 5 star read for me and if the other books are as a good as this I will be happy to back to the start of the series and read them all. I have to say that I didn't feel that I was really missing anything by not having read the other books first because of the way the story focuses around the main characters and explains any extra information quite well. 
 Of course with the title of Ladies Man you expect a charming player that we can't resist in wanting and that is what you get. Tahoe Roth is a wealthy playboy that loves to have fun and has women flocking to him as soon as he appears and he doesn't deny them what they want, well not usually, not unless they are Gina. 
 "his smile is so contagious and comes so easily. I've never seen a guy smile as much as he does. It's an irreverent smile, a mocking smile, because really, Tahoe never seems to respect anything." 
 Gina had previously turned Tahoe's offer down so she was shocked when he declines her offer of one night and instead has to watch him walk away with other women. Over time she starts dating Trent but it might not be what she really wants and has some hesitations with him. During this time though there is a strong bond that develops between Gina and Tahoe and they become close friends. 
 "Cuddling and a warm bed...friends do that, too, right?" 
 Watching the friendship develop was quite good to read as you saw the doubts and frustrations it caused for Gina and you felt the inner struggle she was having. To be honest, there was no way that you ever saw her develop anything with Trent as he wasn't a strong character in the book at all. It was good to see that she didn't judge or criticize Tahoe or become bitchy about his manwhoring ways but accepted it like an adult and a friend. It was like watching two of your friends who you know want each other for more than just sex as they have a deep connection but that they couldn't quite seem to get it together. We learn more about why Tahoe is who he is and see how he helps Gina realize who she is too. 
 If you're going to read expecting lots of sex (as I said I haven't read the other Man Whore books but the title somehow implies they will have lots of sex) then this is not really what you'll get. Yes, there is sex in the book and at times it is quite sexy and hot reading but I feel that there was more to this book as it was more about the connection between the characters and what they meant to each other and what they were afraid to lose. 
 At the very beginning of this book there is a playlist and there are more songs mentioned at certain parts of the story and while I read I listened to that music and for me as a person who loves music and the different emotions it can illicit anyway, I felt that it worked amazingly well. The different songs and their lyrics added to the story and gave an enhanced mood to go along with what you were reading. 
 As I'm sure you've grasped by now I loved the characters in this book and how they develop because of the amazing writing and storytelling. The whole book is written from the perspective of Gina but that doesn't mean that you can't understand Tahoe and get into his head a little. When he opens up to Gina and through the conversations he has with Gina your heart hurts for him and you get to understand him. Without a doubt I'll go back and read the other Man Whore books before the next installment in the series comes out next year as I'm already anticipating it. 
 Reviewed by Louise G.

sample_reviews.review_text: Not as good as the rest of the series. This one seemed like odds and ends cobbled together. A pretty dreary story.

I wasn't impressed at all. The characters were all taken to the extreme, and by that I mean Kitty was made extremely stupid and selfish; Anne was made perfect in every way; Jane was portrayed as only out for herself; the Duke was an evil genius; and Henry was a fat slob whom did whatever suited him and made people fear him. 
 There was more to complain about, but what I've stated here was enough to ruin the book for me.

Far more than just a sequel to the Other Boleyn Girl, the Boleyn Inheritance strives to tell the story of three powerful women in the English court, all diverse in their fates and ideals. Anne of Cleaves is the fourth wife to Henry VIII, a lost lamb in a English world, adjusting to the foreign world she is unmercifully thrown in. Jane Boleyn, or Lady Rochford, is the wife of George from the Other Boleyn Girl, a great gossip and plotter at court. And lastly we have Katherine Howard, a new Howard maid sent in to seduce the king. 
 The story uses a combined narrative of all three women, slipping in easily from the naive and greedy voice of Katherine Howard to the more anguished and scheming voice of Jane Boleyn, and lastly to Anne of Cleave's gentler yet mature tone. I love how much stronger the women are in this chapter, so much more sincere or defined in terms of personality. Yet, all have their deep obvious weaknesses and none were as perfect, as desirable and intriguing as Anne Boleyn. 
 The novel focuses a lot more on inner turmoil instead of only hot blooded seductions, a contrast to the previous novel - which I do like. In particular, Jane Boleyn obsesses frequently about the young and beautiful George and Anne Boleyn, gone from the world. She reminisces about their perfection, their desirable smiles, their capricious attitudes. However, Jane struggles with that same sense of loss, and more as she was the only one that survived. The king is old, and romance has lost its charm now, so emotion and comfort, power and independence are much more prevalent themes in this book. 
 But as I read more and more into Gregory's writing, I see the same things I have disliked over and over again. I am repeatedly reminded that women are worthless pawns in the world, cast off only to win favors with the rich yet easily disposed of when failing to do so. Katherine Howard, and even Jane Boleyn or Anne of Cleaves (at first!) show the same reluctant and pathetic attitudes as Mary Boleyn in The Other Boleyn Girl, they let themselves be controlled by men - their lives dictated by fathers, uncles, and husbands. I admired Anne of Cleaves at the end for seeking her true self, and Anne Boleyn's fiery self possessed manner; they were breaths of fresh air in such novels. 
 Also, Gregory's writing is awfully bland at points. She may excel at romance, or even at dialogue and actions but she utterly fails at description. Her descriptive writing, modifiers and imagery lacks severely - weakening the appeal of the Tudor court and the spirit of the age. The book seems quite simple in language as well, and the words repetitive and often crude. I think I had an unrealistic expectation of fanciful metaphors and imagery painted on velvet curtains for this novel, but I do feel if Gregory's writing was a bit more descriptive, the rating would be higher. 
 I don't really think I'll read another Gregory novel, but we'll see. However, I enjoyed the Boleyn Inheritance far more than the Other Boleyn Girl, and perhaps if I'd somehow read it first, it would be a great read to me. I don't really recommend this novel if you've disliked the Other Boleyn Girl, the novels are truly not dynamically different.

3.5-4 STARS (not exactly sure) 
 Have you ever felt like the words you've been reading had etched into your soul? That they have a life of their own and that they won't rest until you've had them all sucked into your being? Bang is like that. Every word, every idea, every undertone makes it difficult to catch a break and escape from that dark, twisted world -- a world that, for some, is the never ending reality. You're trapped into its merciless cobwebs of sentences, disturbed by their meaning and hurt by their intensity. You feel yourself delving deeper into that hopeless yet scorching land where lies are truths and pain is weakness. And still -- you keep coming back, ignoring that imperative need to press DELETE and erase it all from your thoughts. You want more. You crave more. You goddamn ache for more. 
 Our main character is Elizabeth who's living a double-life as Nina Vanderwal in the shape of a wife's mogul. Her husband, Bennett, is so enamoured of her that he's oblivious to the hatred that lives inside her soul. We got pages of her life filled with horrors that no one should ever encounter, so the readers don't know what to expect until the very end where things start to click into place. But there's one thing we know for sure: she's here for revenge. 
 Take Leah from the Love Me With Lies series by Tarryn Fisher and multiply her cunningness ten times. Strip her bare of all that is lovable. Make her unforgiving, restless and wicked to the bone. If you felt that Leah would have your mind reeling in shock like no other, then you're not ready to experience the confusing storm that is Elizabeth. But whereas I down-right hated Leah although I couldn't help than pity her, Elizabeth truly amazed me. She's strong, patient, calculated. Determined and vicious. Broken. But she's also the villain that's about to go on a killing spree, shredding her only hope of redemption. 
 "The truest part of a person is always the ugliest. And with your evasiveness, I would bet that you're pretty damn ugly beneath all that gloss." 
 Elizabeth's story is complicated and disturbing and definitely not for the weak-minded. It makes you painfully aware of how life can be a cruel bitch and how monsters really do exist. It's gut-wrenching, terrible and depressive and Elizabeth is the result of all that was unforgiving in her life. I wasn't exactly shocked about her childhood, because such subjects have made their way into my regular reads quite often, but believe me when I'm saying it still wasn't easy to stomach. 
 It was so easy to hate Elizabeth in this book. She reminded me of Emily from the Revenge TV Show, but unlike Emily's targets, who deserve to rot in hell, I'm not sure Elizabeth's victims truly deserve what she's planed for them. I don't know how to explain this without spoiling anything, so I'll just say that Elizabeth's mentality is quite harsh and she's not judging things clearly because of her tragedy. 
 "One day, when we're out of this mess, I'll find a way to make you happy." 
 "I don't believe in happiness," I weep. "I don't believe in anything anymore." 
 He brushes my hair back and scoots down to look me in the eyes. "Believe in me." 
 In order to finally have a shot at her missed happiness and to rebuilt her life, she's messing around with three guys: Bennett, her husband; Pike, her best friend and brother; Declan, the game-changer and the man that falls for the devil. But her complex scheming makes her double-question her reasons, because there's one glitch to her master plan: she didn't expect to fall in love. 
 I really liked Bennett. He's caring, thoughtful, sweet. His devotion knows no bounds and he's so helplessly in love with his wife. Too bad she's just a demon in disguise. The true motive behind Elizabeth's need to take him down was really the only thing anticlimatic for me -- I expected something much more cruel and worthy of such plotting. But I guess that in Elizabeth's mind, Bennett's role in her downfall is the worst. Again, subjective (and kind of immature) thinking. 
 I adored young Pike. I couldn't have been more happier that poor Elizabeth wasn't alone in her darkest times and that she was able to find a true support and friend in Pike. He was hopeless yet protective, caring and determined, miserable himself and still powerful enough to bring a smile to her sister's face. Despite my love for the kid, I had countless issues with the adult Pike. I don't know, he just made my skin crawl and he seemed such an obsessed freak. I never trusted him completely. And that horrible thing he did in the end? That was the lowest blow he could land and it showed how selfish and desperate he really is. 
 Now imagine a mix between a tamed Christian Grey (FSoG) and a Braden Carmichael (ODS) and wipe your drool off your chin cause he's mine: Declan McKinnon. He's so intense and addictive, alone and lovable! My heart ached for him every time I remembered how he's playing right into Elizabeth's hand. He also had his fair share of self-loathing and regrets which only increased my love for him. He's a sexy and swoon-worthy alpha-male and trust me when I say you'd want someone like him to wait you at the end of a tiring day and yes, I'm implying a ton of things right now. 
 Bang ended in a rush and I felt that the last few pages were meant to be the sucker punch. The emotional trigger. The final piece to my mind's downfall. And oh, it succeeded. The ending left me shocked, heartbroken, scared and rattled completely. So many things happened and I couldn't keep up with the feelings that followed. And, as expected, there was a sort of cliffhanger that somehow managed to satisfy me with the last resolutions we were left with. Echo, the sequel, better come out quick cause otherwise I'll be turning insane. 
 This is my first book written by the mastermind that is E.K. Blair and I've had my eyes set on her others for a long time now, but damn, if they're as intense as Bang, then a well-deserved break is in store for me before I catch up with her books. She had a way of creating the story and unraveling it afterwards in a unique way that had me hooked from start to finish. I was disturbed, angry, captivated and desperate for more. I guess that's what kept me reading -- the desire to find out all the pieces to this puzzle. 
 Bang is just a book but at the same time it's so much more than that. It's a powerful weapon, it's manipulative, it's confusing and it's sometimes unbearable. The Black Lotus series is the queen of mind-fucks and it has definitely started its dynasty with Bang. She's here to stay and she doesn't mind collateral damage in the form of her readers' bewilderment. Read it, dissect it, live it, shy away from it. God knows I did and I still don't know if I'll ever recover completely. 
 ENJOY! <3

I FEEL LIKE I NEED A CIGARETTE AFTER THAT MIND SCREW!! DID YOU GET BANGED BY EK BLAIR YET? 
 5 BUMP WORTHY , CRAY CRAY, MANIPULATIVE, HOT, BRUTY, SCOTTISH, TEARFUL STARS***** 
 I have edited and re edited this review a million times. I just don't have adequate words to review this story and not give away any spoilers...don't worry , I don't. In addition , it leaves you in such a state your emotions are all over the place which is evident by my review. Well, here it is I hope I can do it justice. 
 So many reviews have been written about this book being careful of spoilers so I too will be careful but I hope I can add enough to lure each and every one of you to the world of Black Lotus....now not later! 
 The writing is nothing short of perfection. There I said it, I went there! I challenge every single one of you to find a story that is as plot driven and as well developed as this one. Each crazy piece of story line is tied to another and then tied up into a perfect bow....well or will be. 
 Yes it's a dark, suspenseful, intense, emotional read that will pull you to and from every corner of your heart and back again. 
 Enter Nina and her intro to us ....a very likable heroine from the start whether you want to like her or not, she grabs you. I don't know what it is but she just does. Even when you want to hate her, be mad at her, you can't ...you will try but you just can't. Every single action, thought, and word spoken from her is fitting to where and what she came from. If she acted any other way would it be true to who and what she is? Should we like her? I don't know but ...I do and you will too. She is strong, weak, sassy, calculating, manipulative, irritating. So complex , flawed , and perfectly developed as is every other character in this book. From the first scene with Nina to her thoughts before, during, and after her and Bennett are together your pulled in. 
 Bennett, oh poor Bennett, or not??? Who the hell knows at this point. We get just enough of him we assume we like him. There are hints that afterwards you'll look back and think did he, noooooo, wait, what?? I know, its confusing but I SIMPLY CAN NOT TELL YOU ANY MORE. 
 DECLAN, GAHHHH DECLAN, OH MY!!! Yes I'm shouting and will shout DECLAN FROM THE HIGHEST ROLLING SCOTTISH MOUNTAIN or preferably the highest floored, mirrored wall, penthouse, on top of my own personal Scottish mountain. So hot. Enter Nina to a party , imagine scanning the room taking in who you know , eyes land on a hot, tall, bruty (yes I am making up my own word..he deserves it) male ,high ball in hand with a cocky grin, staring at you from across the room regardless of who witnesses this act??? WHAT WOULD YOU DO??? Then he saunters over to you in front of your husband and introduces himself , kisses you on the cheek, and then flirts openly with you but not in a crass, douchy way. Declan stole my heart from his first scene. And, that is all I can say about him. 
 Pike. Oh My God, Pike. This one is tricky , how do I not give this away? He is a great friend to Nina.... I am grateful he was there for her during those horrific terrible times. I am grateful she was there for him. He may be a product of his environment.. OR NOT? 
 There are parts of this story , as hard as they are to read, are necessary for the story. Are necessary to understand Nina and others. As soon as I thought the story was going one way, emotionally it went another. There are parts so difficult to read I had to put the book down and come back to it. It is not forced , each and every one belongs in the story. They had to happen to make Nina who she is , what she has become, to explain the predicament she finds herself in. Quite simply to understand her. When you think your heart can't take any more, that it will burst , you turn the page and there's another blow. 
 The story totally engages the reader and you will find yourself guessing(and you won't even come close), wanting to guess, waiting to find out. Though not all answers are given , many are and you don't see them coming...but they do fit, we just aren't as crazy as Ms. Blair to be able to figure her/the story out. 
 Favorite scenes: 
 Nina and someone in the hotel suite sitting knee to knee on the floor both looking out the window watching the snow and what happens afterwards. 
 The steamiest, hottest scene in the book and quite honestly I haven't heard specifics about it in the buzz out there. I can't wait for you all to read it....OMGGGG!! 
 It has been such a long time since I read a smart,true, good mind screw. I love them, I love deep emotional books that tear out my heart so having both combined is perfection for me. 
 OK so I get it we all hate cliffys, but every now and then a book is worthy of the wait , dare I say , worthy of the CLIFFY. Why would you deprive yourself of a BRILLIANT read? We don't like cliffy's but we will buy up all the serial's that are currently being released? I just don't get the difference. Something to ponder... 
 I hope you get caught up in Bang and let it blow you away like I did. Trust me on this, READ IT NOW. 
 "You consume me, you know that??" 
 "Everything you want from me is exactly what I want to give you. You don't even have to take it. Just have it because it's yours."

I feel like the author took so much time building the story to climax and then ended it way too quickly. Everything was taken care of within a few pages and I wanted more. I have read a few reviews about this book, when it was newly published. And those reviews made me decide to wait a while with reading this book, until I would have forgotten some of the negatives. To my own disappointment, I have to agree with the negative reviews, so I am sad that this book did not live up to my usual level of enjoyment a Maya Banks book gives me. 
 For me, this book lacks suspense, and battle scenes and planning. It has an enormous lot of feelings and emotions and Donovan thinking: they are mine, they are my family, I just know it, I will never let them go. In my eyes, he is a psychopath. The way he takes over their life completely, their care, how he is determined to deal with their bad past on his own, forbidding Eve to even think about it. 
 And his whole family just accepts this as normal behaviour, Donovan has not known these people for 5 minutes and he thinks as Eve as his, and her half brother and half sister as his kids. Yes, I know, in the other books his brothers acted much the same, just knowing the woman they are supposed to treat as a job, is much more, and can be the one. But there is still some courting, and not this complete taking over as Donovan is doing. He was creepy in his desires. Eve is still recovering from her injuries from the storm, very malnourished and weak, and he is determined to have her in his bed that same evening. No, just not. He talks about taking things slow, but he is a steamroller and just does whatever he thinks is the right thing to do. 
 And then there is Eve, who has been on the run from her stepfather for a while now, she is at her wits end. She doesn't want to trust Donovan but she has no other choice. She also loves being his family, and with his family, something she has never known herself. (She grew up with an aunt as her stepfather did not want her, until recently). She fell for him, and did not question much about anything, until she thought he had betrayed her and only wanted the children. 
 I also did not really believe the behaviour of little Cammie, four years old, scared of everyone, and suddenly accepting of Donovan, wanting to call him daddy, and asking freely for food or toys, when she was absolutely conditioned not to. 
 What I did like was the little storyline of Rusty and Sean, which I had seen coming for a while now. 
 The other Kelly's of course all play their part in this book as well, as it takes place in their hometown and later in the compound where they all live. The couples are all very happily married, and breeding like rabbits. But the attitude of those men for "the wives" really grated on me from time to time as well, keeping them out of everything, keeping them safe. Ignorant, pregnant and chained to the kitchen sink is more like it. 
 So, I liked the writing style, and the story itself, because it is Maya Banks. I would have DNF-ed the same book by another author for sure. I really dislike Donovan and his attitude in this book though, the characters act really unbelievable. I know this is fiction, but it still has to be believable in some sense for me to enjoy a book. I have to like the characters, and I really did not. Eve was not strong enough, she did not stand up for herself against Donovan and all those other Kellies who were just happy that Donovan found his future in her. 
 I liked the first part, with Travis working and supporting his sisters, but after Donovan took them into his house, I just did not like it anymore. 
 4 stars out of 10.

TSTL = too stupid to live, right? Well, this installment in what used to be a good series introduced me to: TSTQ. I was ALMOST to stupid to quit. I made it to 70%, skimming the sex scenes (!), and finally decided my time, my LIFE, was too valuable to waste even one second of it reading this absolutely absurd and ridiculous story. And wahhh! Why did the author have to invent two of the most boring characters in this series? I found myself thinking, "well, why doesn't this other character show back up -it would make more sense. Why does the 4 yr old little sister (who is terrified of men because her own dad is a pervert) take one look at the Alpha male lead and decide she'll go to his arms, and tell him she loves him in the next scene/ chapter? Why does ... ARGH! I could go on and on with stupid premises or never-gonna-happen incidences and I'd rather go to sleep. I'd rather vacuum. I'd rather clean my toilet with my toothbrush. I have wasted time and given this 'novel' (yeah it's novel that every single character in this book is ridiculous!) too many chances. At least it's a library book ... :)

Around three years ago I was traumatized by "Shades of Gray" and decided to avoid KGI series for a while (I did read Forged in Steele though). 
 I returned to it, after 3 years with "After the Storm", which is Donovan and Eve's story. 
 Eve is a 24 year old Belle, on the run with her step siblings Travis and Cammie, until she comes across Rusty, and ultimately Donovan. 
 We know Donovan has had a soft spot for damsels in distress and kids, and has always wanted a family- so when he finally looks at Eve and her siblings, he knows in his heart he's found them. 
 What begins is an OTT-knight in shining armor-esque love story in which Van and the Kellys' literally rescue them from a storm and take them in. 
 Mixed is sweet love making, nostalgic feelings seeing the Kellys brood growing and their family love, a perverted stepfather who deserves to die and FINALLY scenes of Rusty and Sean (which were AMAZING!) 
 There is good angst around 3/4th of the book (its when the book finally gets GOOD), but it all culminates to a saccharine HEA. 
 Keep your insulin handy for this one! It was quite monotonous and it took ME! 3 days to read this, but it does get interesting towards the ending.

I stopped counting how many times in was mentioned in this book. I thought the general story was good, could have been so much better though. Nothing really happened until the last few chapters. I get the whole love at first sight thing, but it didn't really work for me here for some reason. I'm moving on to Swanny's book now, and hope it's more exciting, and believeable.

So. Yall know, I love me some Kelly brothers. Absolutely love them. These guys are pretty much everything I look for in a hero or fictional family. I'm always pretty damn excited when a new one hits the shelves. So it's pretty incredible for me to actually be typing this but After the Storm has joined the minuscule list of books I've DNF'd. 
 There were things I liked, of course. I mean, it's the Kelly family, hello! They're amazing! Sexy and alpha and all make-a-girl-swoon amazing. And there were some nice scenes at the beginning that really had my heart pounding. But it was the romance that had me calling this one quits by the 50% mark. 
 The big issue here, like I said, was the romance. Donovan has always been the geek behind the KGI operations and the one that most longs for a family of his own. He's a total champion of women and kids. He's geektastic and panty melting at the same time, right? 
 So when he sees Eve and her siblings are in need of help it's a pretty perfect situation, really, and understandable that he could eventually see them as a package deal and want to make them his family. I am all on board at that point. Great set up in my opinion. A man who craves a family and a family that desperately needs someone to love them and that they can trust and love in return. Excellent! 
 The problem was that from the moment they lay eyes on each other until there are declarations of becoming a family and of the L word it's about 48 hours give or take a few. And in that time they're actually in each others physical presence maybe 4 hours? Of which she and her siblings are either terrified or suffering from severe injuries. Even for romantic suspense--where love and passion are lightning fast-- it was just...absurd. And not done in a way that was believable or convinceable at all. 
 Adding to the issue is that Eve and her siblings have been abused. Her little sister has been molested by her father, fears all men and strangers, yet hardly knowing Van is asking if she can call him Daddy and clinging to him. Hrm. It just...really did not work. 
 I was just so disappointed and got to the point I was forcing myself to turn pages. And I just had to call it quits. From too much telling and not enough showing, to Donovan's constant thoughts on how much he loves/wants/cherishes this family--with no real explanation or reasoning behind it other than they're in need of rescue-- to editing blips and confusing scene transitions this just isn't one I could or would recommend--even to hard core KGI fans. 
 I'll read more from Banks--because really one book does not negate the dozen others I've read and a secondary storyline going on was awesome!--but I'll definitely be more cautious from here on out. Hopefully this was just a fluke read.

sample_reviews.review_text: Mary Norton was a woman after my own heart - a woman whose own heart, head, and soul was filled with magic. What a great story! Have you ever wondered where all those little things disappear to in your home? Maybe you have borrowers! They are little people who live in various places in your home or on your land. They borrow what they need to make their home, to eat and to care for their families. 
 This is the first book in a series in which this world is explored. What a wonderful kids' story. It is very different from the movie of the same name starring John Goodman (which was also very entertaining)! 
 This is an award-winning childrens' book.

This is a fun children's book (on the 100 Top Children's Books list) about little people who live under the floorboards of the house. And they don't "steal" from the home owners, they just "borrow." Therefore, they are "The Borrowers." But their biggest fear is to be "seen" by one of the home owners who might bring a cat in to catch them! So this is part of the plot of this book which is the first in a series of five, written for children ages 7-10. Very cute, and would be fun to read to children in a classroom or to your own child/grandchild!

Engaging, endlessly creative and inspiring, Mary Norton's classic children's book "The Borrowers" took me back to a time when dolls, doll houses, fairy tales and cartoons filled my afternoons and week-ends. Wonderfully accompanied by black and white illustrations by Beth and Joe Krush, it reminded me how important family and friends are regardless of their differences. Originally published in 1953, the book's magic really holds up and I know children would be just as captivated, as I was, by it today as they were in the early 1950's. Set in a large house, with a dual existence above and below, the story is told in flashback by an elderly woman, Mrs. May, to Kate, a young girl she's teaching how to crochet on successive visits. 
 Fantastical and overwhelmingly lovely, the mysterious "borrowers"-Homily, Pod and Arrietty- provide the whimsical and hopeful aspects of the book by interacting with each other in a loving and respectful manner and befriending two lonely humans, when they need someone the most. 
 Finally when the two worlds come together, an obstacle occurs that changes the course of the story, leaving me with a desire to read the rest of "The Borrowers" series and their author.

This is a very thought provoking book, challenging in a way, because of its subtle complexity. Often, it reminded me of the bible. Not only was Buck's prose reminiscent of the King James', but the characters behaved much like some of the old prophets and kings in the bible, and the gods were just as whimsical. The book was occasionally difficult for me to digest because, on the one hand, it told a tale of a Chinese family and described Chinese culture and history, but on the other hand, it was written by an American 'missionary'. It felt sometimes like a Ragged Dick story, but, to be fair, it wasn't too overtly moralistic or didactic. 
 This book leaves me wondering so many things, but that is often the reward of great literature. The plot was engrossing, but I felt the narrative voice maintained distance between me and the characters. Buck was very matter of fact about many aspects of Chinese society, and she spared us any editorializations, so some of the book was shocking and slightly off putting for a modern-day Westerner. But, nonetheless, it was compelling and interesting, encouraging and poignant.

This is the second time I have read this book. It was one of the few books I didn't resent being assigned to read in High school. I thought about giving it 5 stars but I just can't quite get there, however, I really do like this book a lot. 
 It is the story of Wang Lung who in the beginning is satisfied with his life and his land and only desires to have children. As the story progresses he is changed in many ways and easily loses sight of what was important to him. 
 Throughout the book the one thing he always clings to is his land. It continually renews him whether times are good or bad. His fortunes change frequently for the better and worse in different ways and while I read it I found that the moments that stood out to me the first time I read it still strike vividly in my mind. I have never been able to think about pearls in the same way since reading The Good Earth. 
 Wang Lung has intense moments of cruelty and fleeting moments of regret but I think had he made different choices he would have been essentially a good man. Some things can feel unresolved at the end of this book (I haven't read the sequels to know if they ever do get resolved) but I think that is so often like life that I was ok with it. Occasionally, I like a story where you can say well, that is life and what's to be done? I know the author could mold the story any way she wants but to give everything in it a solid conclusion and to give everyone in it exactly what they need (O-lan's retribution, Wang Lung's realization that he is mirroring the hated old lord he buys land from) would be false and less fulfilling to me. 
 The language can indeed feel slow but I think it has it's own beauty to it and paints a vivid picture of life in China at the time it is set in. I am going to get around to the sequels sometime although I never really cared for any of Wang Lung's sons as people in the book. Still, it will be interesting to find out what does happen to the family after the revolution. In the end, though, I feel like The Good Earth is good enough to stand on its own without the need for sequels. If the sequels are written as well as this one, I am sure I will enjoy those too.

Originally reviewed on my blog Reading the Best of the Best. 
 The cover and synopsis of Cinder had me entranced. A futuristic sic-fi re-telling of Cinderella? Yes, please! Sadly, I wasn't happy with this book at all. While I enjoyed certain aspects, like the characters, it wasn't enough for me to love this book. I do have Scarlet, the second book in the quartet on hand and I'm hoping it's better. 
 Let's start with the plot. I want to point out that there was so much potential for the plot to be amazing but sadly, it was really predictable. Besides knowing who's going to end up with who (after all, this is a re-telling), I figured out a key aspect of the plot almost 15% into this book. There was no sense of surprise in this novel for me and that was not okay. I found myself getting bored and I even admit to skimming some pages because I just didn't care. I thought about not worrying about it since this was Marissa Meyer's debut novel but that seemed wrong. The second half of the book had much more action which was fantastic because the first half was a chore to get through. 
 I was also surprised at the lack of world building. As I said, this is considered a sci-fi book but I found some aspects to be border line fantasy. All of the special powers that some of the characters possess seem to just be there. I really wanted more background as to how it all came to be. The only explanation was that it was because they lived on the moon. Being the science nerd I am, I began to wonder if it had to do with DNA changes or particles in the air or something else that caused the powers. But nothing was explained and that was rather sad. 
 I did like many of the characters. Cinder was a fantastic protagonist. She was brave and smart and loving. She was also willing to do whatever she needed to to help her step sister (the one who likes her anyways) and for the people she cared for. Even though she was strong willed, I liked the aspects in which she was confused or sad since it made her seem more relatable. Iko was hilarious and a much needed distraction from all of the drama but she was also the best friend Cinder needed. Kai wasn't as fleshed out as I had wanted him to be but I was willing to put that aside. Honestly, I wasn't in love with their relationship. I felt like there was no spark and all of the times there should have been tension between the two, I felt nothing. 
 Overall, I didn't like Cinder. I liked out protagonist but combined with the predictable plot and lack of world building, it wasn't a book I enjoyed. I want to give this book more than 2 stars but really, the 2 stars come from liking Cinder and Iko. I will be reading Scarlet and I'm hoping to love it!

This was a nice hybrid mix between cinderella and sailor moon with a dash of cyberpunk. The lack of vampires or magic (the lunar effect could be explained through science so I do not count it as magic)was refreshing but the book could have had so much more potential! The background for the storyline was bleak and underdeveloped. I would have loved to see the author explain in a more understandable way the migration to the moon. I understand this is meant to be a young adult romance novel, which it is and I would much rather my adolescent daughter (if I had one) read this rather than twilight or any other vampire-ridden book (special apologies to Anne Rice and Bram Stoker who's books I am not reffering to here) but if the author took the time to work on the history of earth, description of the city and scenery as well as the mechanics then this would be one heck of a cyberpunk romance novel. Ommitting the many cultural and historical inadequacies, I found some things to be a nice twist in the retelling of Cinderella such as: 
 -> one of the stepsisters being actually amiable 
 -> a companion to make witty remarks (although those fell quite short. I do appreciate the effort) 
 aaaand that's it. There were too many things going on here that deserved better descriptions and explanations but instead built up an unnecessary parade for the love plot which even though was inventive in having such a surrounding background fell short for my taste. Now that i think about it, the whole story could have used a bit more drama. Either that or the internet has made me an emotionless zombie or I am simply not 16 anymore. 
 Overall it's a nice one-time read with a refreshing new scenery. The love plot wasn't overdone in a sick way as I've seen it in many YA dystopian novels from the past 2 years but could have been worked on a bit more story-wise. The writing style wasn't all that bad either and was quite comprehensible. It sadly also had no surprising twists as figuring out the plot was a no-brainer early on. 
 But i'm babbling again. 
 Give it a read. Get inspired to read more cyberpunk literature and go find better books ;) or just go read sailor moon. Because all this book gave me is an immense need to take apart my wrist watch and crossbreed it with my toaster :) 
 PS. Be kind rewind. This is my first review here on goodreads. Please don't pulverize me.

sample_reviews.review_text:
So I gave the series another chance, and the inconsistencies and boredom just grew. 
 First of all, I love reading. I give books that have been hated or put on a banned book lists a chance to speak for themselves. However, in this case I wonder not only how the heck the series achieved being put on bestseller lists, but how is it possible that people give this drivel more than 3 stars? I'm confused. 
 The Shadow of Night takes off from A Discovery of Witches immediately with Matthew and Diana in 1590 England to hide from both the congregation and multiple creatures who hunt them in the present. Before returning, the couple hopes to find other witches to train Diana to use her magic and to look for more clues regarding the magical manuscript, the Ashmole 582. 
 I just can't even write a full summary on this book, I am that depressed by it. So instead, here's my play by play in case you were really that curious. 
 1. Matthew and Diana go back in time...to 1590. 
 2. Matthew meets father, Phillipe who hates Diana...then loves her. 
 3. Matthew and Diana officially get married. 
 4. They get pregnant. They miscarry. Marriage falls apart. 
 5. Oh ho, they get pregnant again. So hooray? 
 6. Diana spends pages upon pages describing all the uncomfortable outfits she must wear. Matthew is happy no one can see her body. 
 7. Diana creates a dragon. Yes, a DRAGON. Which she conveniently stores in her rib cage. How nice. 
 8. Diana finds out she is one of the rarest types of witches in existence. Proceeds to speak to three of them in 1590. THREE. 
 9. Diana adopts kids off street to help fill her empty womb. 
 10. Diana almost killed by Matthew's sister and best friend with LANCES. As in JOUSTING. 
 Honestly, just don't even bother. It's long. It's repetitive. And to make up for huge plot gaps and inconsistencies, the author bombards the reader with as many historical figures as she can muster in hopes of distracting from the fact that this love story and overall story just do not make any sense.

Not as good as the first in the series. The author jumps all around in this book it seems to be based around sex scenes and not good characters where the first book was cheesy this one was borderline bad. But I read this book because I read the first one, because the third book won some goodreads award if I remember right for being better than some really great books. So hopefully the third book makes up for this one.
This book was soooo long! Unfortunately, most of it could have been left out and the story still been told and make sense. Ugh. So glad I'm done!

If there is one thing to be said about this novel, it's that it is long. 
 It isn't a fast read, and for that I am grateful. I love that Deborah Harkness has the skill to create a story that is so much more than just getting to the end. I find that most of the second novels in a trilogy lack true depth and are used mostly to fill space before the end. This was not one of them. 
 Matthew and Diana grew as both individuals and as a couple, and spent much of their time trying to reconcile their inner conflicts in order to help each other. The pace was slow but rich with description and little things that helped make this story seem so natural to read. 
 While at times I felt like I was being drowned in a vat of history and names and events that I just didn't know (or really care) about I still felt that it was all very integral to the story and the entire series. I had a hard time keeping track of everyone (and what their true place in history was) so I am grateful there was a list in the back. 
 The one element that I loved the most (and that is very important to the entire structure of this trilogy) was the alchemical aspect. Incredibly interesting and so very magical!

I really enjoyed the first book in this trilogy and the second one, Shadow of Night, lived up to that standard. The characters are interesting, complex and intelligent. The books put an interesting spin on various historical figures such as Sir Walter Raleigh, William Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe. An enjoyable read - I am ready for the third book now, The Book of Life.

Beware of some spoilers? I don't know. 
 Oh...this book....this loooong amazing book. 
 At times I loved it (I did love most of the first in the trilogy) and at other times I wanted to tear it up and chuck it out the window. But then...I don't know. 
 At any rate, here's what I loved: 
 - The firedrake. Okay, so it got a little annoying at times but I loved every scene in which Diana actually got to use her magic. She was more independent, powerful, and admirable in these scenes, especially when she was without Matthew. Don't worry, I'll get to that. 
 - I did finish it in the wee hours of the morning. That was half because I was enjoying it and half because I didn't want to have to read it the next day because it was so bothersome. 
 - It was well written (for the most part). 
 - The humor. Oh Gallowglass. You make me giggle. 
 - Ashmole 782... I have a thing for books about books, which is one of my favorite components of this series. That is all that's going to keep me going to book 3. This part of Book 2 gave it life and is, besides Diana's magical schooling, the only thing worth reading some of those historical passages. 
 There are a few more things I liked, but these are the ones I found most worth mentioning. 
 Now...the things that made me claw my own eyes out: 
 - Dialogue. Oh, good God, does no one realize that there is no trace of Elizabethan English in this? 
 - Shakespeare. NO NO NO NO NO. NOOO. You cannot throw William Shakespeare into a HF novel and not address the mystery surrounding him. It's like he's just hanging out talking to other historical characters in the novel. We don't even know if this guy was ONE guy! You can't just... oh dear I should stop now. 
 - That damn queen of England. Oh my good gracious this book was overly long. Get an editor. Get a better dose of how good of a writer you are. There is not enough substance to this novel to make it more than 500 pages! Nothing much happens yet she still found a way to drag it out. And yes, one way is by tossing Elizabeth into the mix. Why? Just why would we have diplomatic discussions and be forced to leave England, then Prague, then back to England. 
 - Matthew. I abhor this man, this vampire, this character. He is a misogynist. Yes, I realize that's just how thousand+ year old vampires are, but no. Use your damn author's license and make the man a nice guy. The dominance made me gag. His protectiveness was appropriate at times, and obnoxious at others. 
 - Did I mention this book is excessively long? It really could have been 300 pages. 
 - As much as I loved seeing him...Stephen Proctor. He seemed like he'd been flung in there, just to, may I say it, make it longer. He has his purpose. Diana misses him, there are things he can tell her, he's good comic relief, but still. Is that necessary to the plot? 
 - And that was the main problem with all of these things and the length. What is the purpose of each of these things that make it longer? Anna Karenina, as real literature, had scenes in which everything (almost) was important. Everything is put there for a reason. And that makes this one frivolous novel. 
 It also makes this novel fall into that terrible category of MID-LOW fantasy. This is not high fantasy, but it certainly cannot be called crap. It has so much goodness in it. Yet I still could not fully love this one, and for that I am highly repentant.

I actually liked this sequel more than the previous book, A Discovery of Witches, and I am looking forward to the third book upon its release. This book was preferable to me as there was less of a focus on the paranormal romance aspect (but it was still there), and more on being introduced to places and people in Elizabethan history (some real, some invented by the author), which I really enjoyed.
I did not enjoy book one and only read book two b/c it involved time travel. No real plot and vampires and witch stuff so uninteresting and book had weird sexual focus.
Much better than the first one, if only because I loved the setting. Because of this, I dread reading the next one.

It took me awhile to finish it, but it was worth it. Shadow of Night continued nicely where a Discovery of Witches left off. I loved the historical aspects of the book and how they tied in seamlessly throughout the book. I cannot wait for the third installment to be released. You have to read the first book, A Discovery of Witches, in order to read the second book, Shadow of Night, as it would make no sense otherwise. Overall, Shadow of Night was well written, fast paced, a page turner, and well worth reading.

reference_books.title: One Thousand White Women: The Journals of May Dodd (One Thousand White Women, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
This book started slowly, and I found myself irritated by the whole thing, but it really grew on me. If you look at all of his reference material, you can see that he chose to weave together a number of different social phenomena of a certain time together into a story. We have the woman committed to an institution for "promiscuity" which was a definite social trend, and then the various Indian tribes and their interactions with the white men - the broken treaties, way of life... And the experience of the military men who had to carry out the government policy. Obviously a lot of the events portrayed in this book really happened - John Burke was a real person who wrote a book about the time, and someone else wrote a book about him. And although I have no idea whether the idea of white women as brides for Indians ever actually happened, it seems plausible that someone might have suggested it! 
 Why did the (male) author choose a feminine perspective? You could see reading all of the history and writing a book from John Bourke's perspective. The female slant, even bringing in the institution beginning - was an odd choice for a man. What motivated him?? 
 There were a number of interesting themes for discussion in the book: 
 * The question of civilization: Where were the Shakespeares and Mozarts? P174 - There was no time to record or ponder, they were too busy living. Aristotle says the unexamined life is not worth living. Some people can't help but introspect. Is it possible that there are specific brain mechanisms just not present in that culture (Gardners intrapersonal intelligene). Why do some cultures evolve and others don't? 
 * The Indians revered those who were different - Dog Woman, those who were considered mad. Our culture values conformity. 
 * No central authority or system. A leader, but punishment was by group, not by law. Did not give up their enforcement to outside authorities. The white women dared flaunt several cultural rules. The place was surprised by no specific punishment. He rules seemed to have evolved, not been designed and were by mutual consensus. 
 * The community of white women was so important. How would thi book have been different if May had gone off to do this alone. What a community can provide in times of stress and testing. 
 * The shame of going back to civilization. They had been happy and suddenly saw themselves in the eyes of others. Helen said why let the tiny minds bother you. But it is hard in a society that values conformity to feel how different and reviled you are. 
 * Did not blame the women when they got raped as European culture still seems to do. The women were still loved when they came back. Nobody found them disgusting. 
 * How did the Indians deal with birth control? The ydidn't seem to have that many babies? Quiet one only had one older girl. 
 * Form of government - tribalism. John Bourke said they had to give up tribalism for individualism. But these days, we try to get third world groups to give up tribalism in favor or a larger community - the democracy. Is it too big? 
 * Whiskey - The American Indians are one of the few cultures that never developer fermented alcohol.

reference_books.title: The Address
reference_books.review_text: Had to stop reading this half way through. Some people might like the kind of stress filled drama that launched from the 49% mark but not I! Interesting setting - the building, staffing, and launch of the famous Dakota building in the late 1880s, combined with an interesting mystery as to who killed whom under investigation in 1985 BUT too much heavy handed false accusations, uncharacteristic behavior and two dimensional characters that were either good but naive or simply bad. Not my thing, though not badly written in terms of pure writing style.

reference_books.title: Bossypants
reference_books.review_text: Very very funny - lots of fun. Light, easy and a pleasure to read.

reference_books.title: Her Fearful Symmetry
reference_books.review_text: I didn't like this book. The Time Traveller's Wife is a hard act to follow, but even still. The writing was reasonable although too much extraneous writing was added when none was needed. I had no issue with the odd premise, but too many stupid things had to happen for the plot to work - always a bad sign. I did like the characters, but they were abused by the author!

reference_books.title: Tallgrass
reference_books.review_text: I'm really becoming a Sandra Dallas fan - she writes novels with wonderful characters and spans all sorts of different times and events in our history - usually centered in Colorado. Nice, clean writing style as well. This books tells a story in the context of a farming community in Colorado during WWII who has a Japanese internment camp built in their midst.

book_a.title: Breakfast with Buddha
book_a.user_review:
I don't understand why I enjoyed this book so much. I stopped about 1/3 f the way through, but then picked it back up and just kept reading. It felt like a non fiction essay - full of one man's search for truth and enlightenment kind of thing. It was written in the first person and had all the trials and tribulations, doubt and skepticism that usually accompanies such essays. But it is fiction. In a little afterward the author explain that he trip across the country was one he had made, so a lot of the detail on scenery, restaurants, little inns... were based on reality (and his descriptive style is excellent - it felt very real). 
 The Rinpoche - the spiritual advisor he travels with - is based, he explains, on his readings across many many spiritual philosophies and lessons. My only complaint about the spiritual portion of the book is that it was a shallow coverage - and made it seem so easy (although the descriptions of the little bit of peace of mind were very good. One yoga class, one 2 hour meditation (which again, was explained fairly well for a one page description) managed to open this guys mind to what Rinpoche was saying. But again, maybe that's all it takes. The character of Rinpoche was very Buddha like - always laughing, enjoying everything, unflappable. It's funny that the book didn't feel like a good read, but obviously was. 
 One thing that is never addressed. If everyone lived the life Rinpoche does, we would never be able to get anything done. What id the right balance between turning off the mind, and turning on the mind to accomplish? LSD allows you to see the world in complete beauty, but unless you're in the garden of Eden with all things provided for, or not in a body that needs nourishment, you have to come out of it. 
 There were some nice ideas in the book - like the way saints get born - when so much love or need is concentrated in one place. I liked the model and imagery there. 
 At the very end, he goes down on his knees in front of the spiritual master. It seemed like the right thing to do. That I didn't like. I couldn't see it. Although, perhaps being in close proximity to a powerful being has an effect I can't imagine.

sample_reviews.review_text: Predictable but thoughtful book.

A man in his 40's, a couple of teenagers at home, and a cross country trip to make to sell the family farm after his parents died suddenly in a car crash. Added complication: his sister's guru joins him for the drive. He's already pondering the mysteries of life as a result of his parents' death. A few days in a car with a spiritual leader opens the floodgates. 
 This book started off so well. Incredibly promising. But, ultimately, as the narrator neared his destination it all became too pat, too easy, and ultimately, one of those endings where everything works out wonderfully for everybody involved. 
 It's definitely a thought-provoking story for anybody pondering those mysteries, but, well the ending fell flat for me. This is one of those times I wish Goodreads had half stars. I'd give it 3 1/2.
Can't say I read it all. Resorted to the every other, then every third paragraph. Easy spirituality couched in an easy-read book without much plot and without much depth of insight.
Great book, great descriptions of the American landscape and culture as well as an understanding of the benefits of eastern practices. Well done!

It took me awhile to get into this book, but I found it enjoyable, particularly the last half. Otto Ringling was a rather spoiled, self-satisfied man who benefited greatly from his trip with Rinpoche; he learned to laugh at himself with Rinpoche's guidance. I particularly loved the yoga scene....and of course, who cannot like the "bohling" adventure!

A road-trip with an odd couple. An easy read. A few things to think about. Some funny situations. Some nice ideas about family and careers and life. 
 I always find these types of books hard to love though--I expect to get the answers of the universe by the end. So I am always disappointed.

book_b.title: China Rich Girlfriend (Crazy Rich Asians #2)
book_b.user_review: You know, this is a silly book, but I admit I couldn't put it down once I made it half way through. Fun style, crazy, rich people - as advertised.

sample_reviews.review_text: Meh. Not as good as the first one.

As summer appears in all its sweltering glory China Rich Girlfriend is the sumptuous equivalent of a decadent ice cream in book format. The novel is Kevin Kwan's follow-up to his biting and over-the-top debut Crazy Rich Asians about people with more money than brains and taste. In China Rich Girlfriend, much of the original cast is back, along with some new stereotypes of the uber-wealthy including the porn star trying to reinvent into herself into a society lady and the heir to the money throne who buys cars the way the rest of us buy ice cream (OK, the way I buy ice cream). Even in this rarified atmosphere Kwan is quick to draw lines between the blue bloods of Hong Kong and the oh-so-gauche Mainlanders, who while they may have the money do not have a pedigree and try far too hard to show off their wealth. 
 The rest of this review can be read at The Gilmore Guide to Books: http://wp.me/p2B7gG-14D

Kevin Kwan's writing had me laughing again. While this book is certainly crass at times, I enjoy the easy read while hawking at lavish living and drooling hearing Chinese food dishes described. The first book in this series, Crazy Rich Asians, was an Asian retelling of Pride and Prejudice. This sequel, however, didn't really resemble an Austen novel. It did, however, have moments of intrigue and mystery, which I loved.
