sample_reviews.review_text: Creo que en toda mi vida le habia dando tan baja puntuacion a un libro, pero, en serio, me cuesta creer que J.L haya escrito esto. Quiero decir, me gusto mucho Te esperare y el POV de Cam, pero Be with Me.. DIOS. Fue HORRIBLE. Tessa me desespero tanto, tantisimo, que tenia ganas de tirar mi Kindle por la ventana, y eso que el pobre no tenia la culpa, lo termine de leer para no dejarlo a medias.. :/
Jase is the perfect guy! if only he were real, His love for Tess is unreal. I think he kicked Cam right out of the water with his story! he is so much better than Cam.

2.5 
 Eu ja tinha lido em outras resenhas que a protagonista era meio mosca morta, mas nao sabia que era tanto! Serio, endureca essa espinha dorsal, mulher!! Quando parecia que ela ia criar uma, no paragrafo seguinte ela perdoava o heroi. NO!! 
 De qualquer forma, a minha avaliacao se refere mais a outras coisas que a protagonista. Eu adoro o cliche da menina que e apaixonada pelo melhor amigo do irmao. Nao me perguntem o porque. Isso nunca aconteceu na minha vida real, mas adoro ler sobre. Senti que nao foi bem executado aqui. O Jase ficava indo e vindo na decisao dele e a Teresa so ficava esperando ele voltar. Sei la, achei muito anticlimatico. 
 Outra coisa que vem progressivamente me incomodando e essa necessidade que as autoras de NA sentem de colocar um drama gigantesco como sub-enredo. Nesse livro tinhamos dois. O do Jase me pareceu mais apropriado, mas o da Teresa foi muito demais para mim. Nao o que aconteceu no passado dela, mas o que acontece durante o livro. Quando apareceu o plot twist dessa parte eu fiquei, serio? E um drama desproporcional com o resto da historia e fica deslocado na narrativa geral do livro. Ao inves de eu levar a serio o que estava acontecendo, tudo me pareceu muito falso e forcado. Nao entendo porque precisa ter essa dramalheira. Achava que a autora deveria ter se concentrado muito mais na carreira artistica dela que tinha acabado do que no drama que ela desenvolveu. 
 Enfim, vou continuar a serie, mas vou pular o terceiro livro, porque se eu ler mais uma historia sobre uma garota virgem eu vou ficar sem cabelos... Os livros 4 e 5 tinham premissas mais promissoras pelo menos. Vamos la!

Ehhh ... 
 Spoilers ... read at own risk. 
 What can I say? It wasn't y favorite Jennifer Armentrout book. The plot was kind of boring and Jase, although hunky, I wanted to love him, I just couldn't. 
 Tess ... I liked the idea of her. Bouncing back after a injury and all that but most of the time I just wanted to slap her. When a guy insults you as much as Jase did, you don't willingly just get into a car with him just because he tells you to. Repeatedly. So many times she needed to just run the other way, or start looking for another guy anywhere else cause this one made it clear he wanted nothing to do with her. Tess just keeps pushing him anyway. 
 I rolled my eyes so many times I'm surprised they aren't permanently lodged in my skull. 
 Nothing about the story surprised me. The minute Jack entered the scene, I knew who his father really was. The minute Jase and Tess finally got together I figured he'd pull the whole "this was a mistake thing". Again. The second Tess saw Debbie's body hanging in the bedroom I knew that Erik had done it. 
 Disappointed. Though I supposed everyone has a bad book somewhere. I still love J. Lynn and will continue to read her books. I look forward to Stay with me. :)

Actual Rating: 3.5 stars 
 "We need to tell your brother." 
 And that would be terrifying. For Jase. But I smiled. "Maybe I'll just update my Facebook to 'in a relationship' and tag you?" 
 So here's the thing. I cannot see this book loose from Wait for You. I can't help comparing them and the thing is.. this just wasn't as good. It's still a good read, don't get me wrong, I really enjoyed reading it and it was a one-sitting kind of book. I stayed up until five in the morning to finish it (and was a zombie the day after - totally worth it) and I have no regrets. 
 J. Lynn (or Jennifer L. Armentrout) has a very compelling writing style. It reads really fast and you get sucked into it whether you want to be or not. Her characters are people you can't help but root for and her stories always have that extra touch aside from the romance. I think she knows that. I also think she tried a little too hard here. 
 The story picks up where Wait for You and especially Trust in Me left off. Theresa Hamilton (Cam's sister) is the main character. When an accident and the following knee-surgery put her dreams to become a professional dancer on hold, she is forced to start college - something she never imagined she would do. It leaves her a bit hollow, worsened by the fact that she will now have to keep running into Jase Winstead. Her brother's best friend and the guy she has been in love with for ages. It gets even better when it becomes really clear that he is not interested in seeing her. 
 Theresa was nice enough even though I had imagined her quite differently before. I guess I expected her to be more like Cam. Confident. Strong. I know there was her past to consider, but I imagined life as a semi-professional dancer had hardened her. That wasn't the case. I wouldn't go as far as to say she was insecure, though. Overall she was pretty mainstream. There wasn't anything that made her stand out. You'd think the fact that she got beaten up by her ex-boyfriend on a regular basis would have done the trick, but somehow that part felt a bit... staged. I didn't get the feeling she was really struggling with it. It was mentioned often enough, but I wasn't feeling it. Not the way I did with Avery's heavy past. The same applies to her lost dancing career. It didn't really make an impact on me. I did love her relationship with her brother, though. How she relied on him in many ways, but also told him off when he was being overprotective. 
 And Jase.. Well, he was definitely no Cam Hamilton. He was swoon-worthy enough. Handsome, flirtatious, confident and abs so hard you'd probably need a bucket to collect your drool. Most of the time he was really, really great but.... well, but. He has his own demons from the past he needs to reconcile with. And as heavy as that stuff was, I don't think it justified the way he treated Theresa. He was caring, he was sweet and most of the time he was there for her. Yet I couldn't help but feel that he was also a terrible jerk who kept dragging her along. It was completely understandable that it wasn't easy for him to commit to a serious relationship. In my opinion that still doesn't mean he could just jump her whenever he felt like it and then say: 'I'm sorry, this was a mistake'. If he wasn't ready, well then he needed to keep it in his pants. Just saying. 
 Maybe better writing would have helped as well. It was so very repetitive and plain. Especially when it came to describing Jase. Theresa kept going on and on about his stunning gray eyes. And yeah, they probably were. I felt myself completely swooning the first time. The hundred time? Yawn. Not so much. She changed things up in the second half, though. Then they suddenly became 'liquid silver'. Okaaaaaay. I also thought the cupcake-thing was insufferably cheesy. 
 Too much. Which also applied to the drama-level. Both Theresa and Jase have pasts you wouldn't wish on anyone. Yet somehow that wasn't enough. Dramatic events kept piling up until I just couldn't take it seriously anymore. I guess technically it was possible for all of this to happen to a single person - but it just didn't feel authentic. And when a contemporary doesn't feel authentic anymore - it changes from something that will stay with you forever into something meh. 
 But I hopelessly enjoyed all the scenes with Cam and Avery. And there are many. I love it when cherished characters like them make a reappearance. They obviously aren't as developed as they were in their own book, but trust me - this alone makes the book worth reading. I got all squeamish the first time Cam came into view. To be honest, they kind of stole the show. I may have loved them more than I loved Tess and Jase - which is not a very good thing. 
 I also enjoyed the return of Stephanie a lot more than I should have, haha. 
 So yes. Good read. But not nearly as good as Wait for You. Because that one really touched my heart and Be with Me somehow didn't succeed in that. But read it, I still really enjoyed it. J. Lynn wrote a compelling romance. She always does.

I have waited for this book since I read the preview of it! I knew it was going to be a gem, but I had no idea just how big of a gem it would be. I loved every little thing about this story! Don't expect any spoilers from me, because that isn't happening. The way these two help one another face the demons that haunt them is unbelievable. I wish I could give this more than five stars!!! Such a breathtakingly beautiful ride!! Great job, J Lynn!!

"Thank you." His spine lost some of its stiffness as he draped his arm over my shoulders. Tugging me against the shelter of his body, he rested his cheek against the top of my head and sighed. 
 "Thank you for being here with me." 
 Well that was difficult to read. 
 This was very different than Wait for You. While Wait for You was a passionate and a well-driven novel, Be with Me was so much more different. It shared less passionate romance, it shared way too much drama, and it didn't have any of the expectations I had after Wait for You. I don't do half stars with books, no matter how close it is to a .5 or how far it should be from the given rating, but I feel like this one deserves it? Even with that being said, I'm not rating this a 1.5, I'm leaving it as a 1. I had a lot of problems with it. I had problems with both of the characters, the side chararacters, and the plot itself. 
 Be with Me is about Teresa Hamilton and Jase Winstead, Cam's little sister and best friend from Wait for You. Teresa has been in love with Jase for a while now, especially after sharing a small yet passionate kiss with him. After that, Jase and Teresa stopped communicating with each other as the years went by, especially because Jase was afraid to start a relationship with his best friend's little sister. One year later, they are both sharing a class together in college since Teresa enrolled late after having to drop her dancing career. Like in Wait for You, both characters have a secret past that they are running away from. Teresa is trying to get over her abusive ex-boyfriend, Jeremy, while Jase is trying to make up his mind about life and whether he wants to be with Teresa or not. As the two start seeing each other more, they begin to learn more about each other as well. Teresa, still in love with Jase, knows he is attracted to her as well but can't seem the to find the reasoning for him acting the way he does. Jase, being Jase, can't seem to make up his mind because there is something behind the reasons he doesn't want to be with Teresa. As the two start rebuilding a friendship, the two start learning more about each other, understanding each other, and even sharing moments together. 
 This was difficult to read like I said. It was so different than Wait for You and I didn't enjoy it as much. As a matter of fact, I didn't enjoy it that much. There was too much drama, and it was the kind of drama I don't enjoy. It wasn't a second-chance love story, and it wasn't a romance novel where the two are trying to find a way to be together. No, not really. Instead, it was a story filled with drama involving the two main characters finding out ways to fix the way they can be together. They were both complicated characters, especially together, and they weren't the kind of couple I enjoyed reading about. 
 Teresa was very different than Cameron. I know she's been through a lot, especially now that she can to drop her dancing career because of her injury, but she was still quite annoying and stupid. She thought she could do a lot of things for her age but she really couldn't. She was also annoying with Cameron when it came to him being the protective brother he is. I mean, she really needed to chill at times. She's his baby sister and she's been abused, what does she expect to get from him? Does she expect him to not care at all, to not worry about her? Her attitude was plain ass boring and her personality as well, unlike Avery. Tess, as Jase calls her, didn't have a big sense of humor and that was a missing part. I was expecting to laugh at this and giggle when it came to her scene with Jase, but instead, I found myself skipping a few things and not caring what was about to happen. She was really different around Jase, which was something else I didn't like, and she was also easy to be controlled. Tess was also very stupid when it came to Jase's rejections. 
 Honestly, the girl needed to give up and find someone else. Like my friend Amber said, if I kept getting rejected by the same guy, I would've already punched him in the throat. She kept saying she would stay away from him and that she would punch him in the throat if he kept saying it was all "an accident" or "a mistake" or any of that bullshit, but every time he kissed her, she was all up on him and couldn't seem to control herself. Honestly, Tess, you should've given up on him. In my opinion, she should've been the one to walk away. She did, one time, and then she was with him again, but I wish she kept walking away. I wish she did a test on him, walking away and seeing if he would come back for her. 
 Jase wasn't different. He was also an asshole, especially because he kept rejecting Tess over and over again. I hated how he would always kiss her and then say "I'm sorry, that was a mistake." only repeating the process, only to say the same thing. He would bring up excuses, saying he was drunk or saying that was a bad idea, but then he would hate himself for what he did, regret it, and pretty much kiss Tess again. Tess, being the selfish person she is, was able to just relax and not care what was happening because she was so in love with Jase and couldn't think of a single thing that she didn't want from him. Jase, also, happens to be a dad which was surprising to me. Yes, I don't have predictions when it comes to books. I tend to ignore them because then they ruin the whole book. Especially if I'm right, then it just makes it worse. Honestly, like Tess said, I wish he would make up his mind about Tess and be straightforward about his feelings for her if he really did have them. 
 I know they're different characters, but Cam and Jase were so damn different whereas Cam didn't give up on Avery no matter what the hell was going on or what was happening and Jase didn't seem like the kind of guy that would try no matter what the situation was. He changed at least, as the book was coming to an end, but his character in the beginning and in the middle was just awful. I hated how he was able to "control" Tess by being able to stop her from doing what she was doing, only to break her heart again. 
 The romance wasn't there for me. There was no chemistry in any way, not even in the end where he was able to tell Cam the truth and tell Tess that he loves her. Even when Jase told Tess the truth, I couldn't seem to find a way where their romance was cute or sweet in a way because it just, wasn't. The whole novel was a lot heavier than the first one, but I wish it wasn't. If the series continues to be like this one, I won't end up enjoying them. To be honest, I'm glad Cam and Avery were still in this book because if it wasn't for them, Tess and Jase would've been fucked in their own way. To be honest, there was really nothing I enjoyed about this except for Cam and Avery being a part of it. Tess and Jase, their relationship was a mess; it was all over the place. One minute they were making out, the other they were fucking, and then they were arguing while one was saying "you don't understand" and the other was saying "I understand completely" when both were wrong; they didn't understand, but they didn't understand themselves either. Both characters carried their own issues but there were also issues involving side characters. What I hated about this were the problems the other characters brought to Tess and Jess. Erik and Debbie were a huge problem in this, and I wish they weren't. They weren't necessary for this book, and I wish they were never brought up. Debbie added much more problems to Tess, especially because of her death and Erik did too since he blamed her for Debbie's death, only beating her up and almost killing her which was just a mess for me. I didn't think that would be the problem of it all, but I guess it was. Like in Wait for Me, the story was mainly just focused on Cam and Avery. Even though Avery's friends was mentioned a lot, it all made sense. Avery was going through some tough times and her friends were there for her to support her in any way along with her boyfriend. In Be with Me, the friendships here were so different and difficult to understand. Debbie didn't even look like the good kind of friend since she always had to bring up her abusive boyfriend and get Tess worried. 
 I had issues with this one, and they were not the kind of issues that could get solved right away if I gave the book and characters another chance. I hope the third book makes up for it since I have heard it's the best one so far. Actually, I heard this one is the best one so far because of how different the relationship between Tess and Jase was/is compared to Cam and Avery. Despite my issues with this one, I am still looking forward for the rest of the series and hoping they get better and make up for this one. I know Cam and Avery won't be mentioned a lot anymore or brought up, but I'm okay with that. I love them together so much. I love Cam so much that I wish he was real or that someone with his kind of charms and personality would exist. I also love Avery and wish her the best with Cam. I'm really hoping this series builds up and just gets better. Well, the series is done and is either better or worse, but I hope I think differently. 
 Also, this isn't really a spoiler since it's actually a novella, but Cam is planning to propose to Avery and I am so ready to giggle and say "aw" to myself while reading that short 6-page novella.

The book is pretty good but I don't think I'm going to read the sequel to this one. The thing is, is that J. Lynn is repeating the same story as "Wait For You". Teresa was abused by her loser boyfriend, not a spoiler it was in the last book, then got a thing for her brother's best friend Jase. They go to college together blah-blah-blah Teresa has a life changing moment where she realizes she is not to blame for being abused and she lives happily ever after with Jase. Familiar mush? It's EXACTLY like "Wait for You"! When I open a book I want something exciting, not even new just something that makes me want to keep reading but with this book I only finished it because I'm a fan of Jennifer Armentrout and I thought she might turn it around! No such luck. It was dull through and through.

Just...raging hormones. I didn't like Jase (so sorry for those abs) and I kinda feel sorry for Tess. Ugh! You don't kiss a girl and regret it afterwards; say you care for her and dump her the next (which happened a lot of times in this book). Damn, Jase has nothing on Cam. -.- I never thought I could rate a JLA book like this but yeah...

As much as I loved cam and Avery's story I absolutely loved jase and Tess's story so much more. There is a lot of push and pull with the characters . Jase becomes so much more substantial in this book. He becomes this all around perfect American boy with deep seeded secrets. Although I knew what the secrets were well before they were revealed I absolutely couldn't put this book down! Looking forward to the third book in the series. If you want a tear jerker with fast paced writting and witty characters, this is the book for you!

book_b.title: Take a Chance (Rosemary Beach, #7; Chance, #1)
book_b.user_review: DNF

sample_reviews.review_text:
An endless annoying drag 
 I can't believe it's over 
 I loved the others in the series 
 But the whole thing got so irritating 
 Justification after justification 
 Yeah it's finally over !
Didn't get far... This really wasn't for me

I was eager to read Grant's story because I always liked him in Rush's but....I was not feeling him at all in this book & don't even get me started on his love interest. This book was very flawed but my biggest regret is Harlow. Grant and Harlow are not compatable at all in my opinion! They r boring and dont bring out the best in each other. Also can we get over Nan? I'm done with her. DONE!. I don't even care to read anymore of these Rosemary books...I'll just stick with the first 3 with Blair and Rush (in my opinion those were the best)
Stupid effing cliffhanger!!! BEWARE

** spoiler alert ** 
 Nan? NAN?! Are we still trying to muscle up sympathy for Nan? Send the evil broken bitch to an island somewhere and then never talk about her again. I about came UNGLUED when Rush ran off to rescue her (AGAIN!) and dragged Grant along with him. Are you kidding me? No way I would put up with that if I were Blair. I don't care if she's your sister, she's poison. Nan can't be saved. Soulless bitches from hell CANNOT BE SAVED. 
 OK, now that I got that out of my system. If you skip all the parts with Nan in it, you have a decent love story. Grant and Harlow were hot and sexy, but man I've never read two people who are less meant to be together. Sure there's chemistry, but very little else. Harlow will never trust Grant, nor should she. Grant will never get past his commitment issues because he's still hung up on Nan. Don't lie, yes he is. 
 Just UGH!

WOW! ABBI GLINES REALLY TOOK A CHANCE ON THIS ONE!!! 
 I already knew I was going to have a hard time with this story because of the reviews, but I have really enjoyed the Rosemary Beach series, so far, and simply needed to keep going. So I recruited the help of a reading buddy to read/listen along with me so we could be a support group to one another...lol, Crazy right? Well, let me tell you that I needed that support throughout this book because about 20 minutes into it, it was an almost DNF. In fact, it was an almost DNF up until about 60% of the book. 
 Glines really took a chance in writing Grant and Harlow's story because of Grant's tangled previous relationship with Harlow's half sister Nan (who is a bonafide biotch of the first degree). Harlow and Nan are half sisters and the daughters of rock star legend, Kiro, and along with that connection, there were so many relational aspects of this story that did not make sense to me. For instance....why would Kiro have Harlow (his favorite and beloved daughter) live with Nan (his venomous daughter who HATES Harlow) in Rosemary Beach, in the SAME house????? I NEVER understood that completely. But, the hardest part was how Grant got involved with Harlow after his relationship with Nan began to disintegrate. I know that he had an instant attraction to Harlow, and she made him feel things he had never experienced before but, Oh MY GOODNESS, really??? You're going to fall in love with your EVIL-BITCHY ex-girlfriend's half sister???? Now if that wasn't a doozy, the hardest part of the story between Grant and Harlow is HIS behavior after he was with Harlow. UGH, that infuriated me beyond belief!!!! Look, I really do like Man-Whores, but only after they STOP Man-whoring after they find the love of their life!!!! What the heck Grant???? His excuse was fear....wow...that dam fear..... 
 Anyway, I don't think I will ever get over how badly Grant messed up on Harlow after being with her!!!! UGh!!! And, I really liked Grant from previous books. He was the fun and very caring playboy of the group of gorgeous men in Rosemary Beach. 
 Well, the reason I finished this book was because of sweet Harlow. I mean, I needed to see the girl through this mess! Also, because of her cowboy, half-brother Mase who was so awesome and protective--Loved Him. Lastly, because of the the incredible story that was revealed about her mother, Emily and Kiro's amazing love. OMG, that took my breath away!!!!! 
 Even though this book does not end well, I'm pushing to the next book because I'm an optimist and hoping Grant redeems himself, especially in light of Harlow's secret coming out..... 
 Narrators: Shayna T. and Jack D. did a very nice job with this audiobook. It took me a while to get used to Shayna's voice, but overall, I believe she did a good job.

Same old, same old. Enserio, ya cansa. Estos libros parecen salir de una fabrica china, son todos iguales!!! 
 En los personajes masculinos no hay variacion alguna, y en los femeninos muy poca. No hay originalidad, todos siguen una misma estructura, los personajes por momentos actuan con incoherencia en orden de respetar el molde del libro. 
 En este caso, Grant. Cuando se lo conoce en Fallen too Far, se tiene una idea totalmente distinta a como resulta siendo en Take a Chance, lo que hace que se pierda la continuidad del personaje a traves de los libros. Es igual a Rush: playboy, posesivo, que se parte en 20, etc, etc. 
 Harlow, es cualquier cosa. Su personaje no tiene coherencia. Se la quiere mostrar como una bookworm, pero si leyo algun libro en Take a Chance, nunca me entere... 
 Esta pareja tenia bastante potencial en lo que se mostraba en Forever too Far, pero lo mandaron todo al tacho desde el momento en que Abbi Glines fue a su fabrica china y saco un manuscrito llenando los espacios en blanco con los nombres Grant y Harlow. 
 La trama no tiene nada de interesante, enserio, una enfermedad del corazon??!! Ni que estuviera viendo una telenovela mexicana!! 
 Para peor el libro parece empezado, ya te muestran a los personajes enganchados de una, no hay mayor elaboracion en como se conocen entre ellos...nada. 
 Y Nan....cortala!!! Hace como cuatro libros que venimos con ella como antagonista, cansa. 
 En resumidas cuentas, no creo que vuelva a leer algo de Abbi Glines...no pienso seguir perdiendo el tiempo en leer bazofias como esta.

Abbi, Abbi, Abbi,....You did not just leave me hanging.....UGGGGGHHHH!!! I am such a fan of this series. This is the story of Grant and Harlow. I always like Grant in the other books, but in this one it took me a while to really like him. Then, I didn't like him again. I absolutely despise Nan. Grant is such a fool for even thinking that he likes her. Harlow is so sweet. Thank goodness she is a forgiving person or this story would never work. Also, I am thankful that Rush is so heavily featured in this story. He is a great friend to both Grant and Harlow. He tells Grant like it is. What makes me so mad about this story is that Grant can treat Harlow like crap at times, but when she chooses not to share her secret with him, he acts like a dickhead. Now, I have to wait until the next book for the conclusion of their story. So yes, there is a cliffhanger!! Dual point of views, which I love. You wouldn't have to read the rest of the series before this one, but I highly recommend it.

I just started reading this and I dont think I can finish this book. There's too much going back and forth in the book that I find it hard to keep up. It just left me a whole lot confused on where the story is headed to. I dont mind reading books which switch between flashbacks and the present scenario as long as it is well written. From what I have read so far, this book lacks cohesion. I enjoyed most of Abbi Glines' books but the Rosemary Beach series have been disappointing.
This wasn't just my cup of tea. So sad to rate a book like this - aaaack I feel bad.

reference_books.title: Throne of Glass (Throne of Glass, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
I have a feeling this book is going to be the next Twilight or The Hunger Games. It hits all of the "big YA fantasy" points, and is an enjoyable fast paced read. That said, there are many issues. It's a shallow read - the world building is almost non-existent, the plot obvious, the love triangle by the books. In fact, the characters don't even seem to care about the plot all that much - did Chaol really not question the runes next to all the bodies? 
 One topic that will be much debated is whether Celaena is a Mary Sue. She is abnormally good at almost everything, but what was important to me is that she works at it. There was no handwaving, no blithe smoothing it over; to be that good, you need to work your ass off. Her arrogance was part of her charm for me. There was no good girl desire to hide her ambition and no false modesty. 
 What struck me about this book was the similarity to Patricia Briggs's When Demons Walk. Look at the comparison: 
 Set after a megalomaniac takes over a fantasy realm? 
 check 
 Blonde young female thief/assassin whose childhood was ripped apart after her parents died in the invasion? 
 check 
 The conquerors don't believe in magic and killed all who claimed to use it? 
 check 
 The remaining magic is used through runes? 
 check 
 Our hero (highly placed in the new regime) tracks down the heroine to bring her to the castle under a false identity? 
 check 
 Is a serial killer demon running amok ? 
 check 
 Is the heroine a girl who loves using clothing as costume? 
 check 
 I could go on, but that would get too spoilerific. For me the bottom line is I like Throne of Glass, and I'll look forward to reading the sequels, but I'm not going to be falling in love with this world. 
 And, you should read When Demons Walk.

reference_books.title: Doon (Doon, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
I really wanted to like this book. Scottish setting? Girls who are great best friends? These are things I love. The set up was fabulous, but the book didn't follow through. It's 368 pages of telling us why everyone is awesome and why the witch is so scary rather than actually letting the characters breathe and become real for the readers. 
 Everything was too much. There was no subtlety, no reality. Everyone is model gorgeous (as repeated CONSTANTLY) evil is EVIL, good people are totally pure. Vee's family life is disastrous, Kenna has the best internship ever, and they are the best dancer and actress. And Jamie and Duncan are awesome and strong and princes and kind and sweet. Well, when Jamie isn't being a jerk. But he's Vee's soulmate, so that's alright. 
 The soulmate aspect was what really damaged it for me. Rather than two characters meeting and falling in love because of mutual attraction and compatibility they're "meant to be" and thus we are told to cheer for them rather than growing to care for them. 
 Add to all this the 'if everyone just talked it would have been over in half time' conflict and you get a book I was very disappointed by.

reference_books.title: A School for Unusual Girls (Stranje House, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
I enjoyed reading this book, but I wanted to like it more than I did. The core story is good: girl is misunderstood by parents, girl finds place that appreciates her, girl uses science to save the world country, girl saves boy. There was just too much thrown in, though, leaving the side characters not fully fleshed out and the plot threads leading into the sequels distracting rather than intriguing. 
 One of my pet peeves in stories is when a character is talked up as so very smart, then the writer leads the audience to understand things long before the character figures it out. Georgie (and really, Georgiana Fitzwilliam as a character name in a regency book?) doesn't take that long in-universe to sort things out, but from the audience perspective she takes forever to understand what's happening around her. It left the pacing of the book feeling off and dragging for the first half. 
 Would I recommend? Probably not to buy, but maybe to take out from the library.

reference_books.title: Saga, Vol. 1 (Saga, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
I have heard such good things about this series and enjoyed Brian K. Vaughan's writing in the past, so I think that my expectations might have been slightly too high. While I enjoyed the story, I didn't feel any connection or concern about the characters. While there should be a strong narrative to the plot, it felt like it meandered off course to the point where it feels like it loses all of it's drive. 
 The main characters are Alana and Marko, as well as their newborn daughter, Hope, but we never really get to know them or where they come from. They loved each other enough to defy their own cultures, yet barely seemed to communicate. They seem to be learning each other's history at the same time we do, leaving me to wonder what they talked about during the time before Hope was born. There were bounty hunters, princes and all sorts of other characters, yet they seemed to be little more than pieces moving around the board for a game where the rules are never explained. 
 Some of this is the problem with sequential storytelling - you want to give people enough of a hook to start them off, but leave the big stuff for later in the run. Unfortunately, with the number of comics and books I'm trying to follow, this just wasn't capable of grabbing me.

reference_books.title: Letters from Skye
reference_books.review_text:
I think I'm about to damn this book with faint praise. And yes, it deserves a cliche. 
 Many of my favourite books are epistolary, so I was quite happy to find this one. What I found was a predictable plot that still maintained some charm. Elspeth, our lady on Skye, starts receiving letters from an American fan of her poetry, David. Will she fall in love? Will their correspondence cause issues with her husband? Will she get over her fear of boats to meet him on the mainland? I'm sure you can guess that answers to these questions. 
 Alternating chapters move from WWI to WWII, where Margaret exchanges letters with various people. Will she find out the truth about her mother? Will there be a series of convenient coincidences and tragic missed connections? Duh. 
 Despite the predictability I enjoyed the read. Sometimes what we look for in a book isn't excitement and new ways of thinking, but a comfortable enjoyable read. Letters from Skye delivers that.

book_a.title: The Darkest Minds (The Darkest Minds, #1)
book_a.user_review:
I loved the experience of reading this book. It has fast paced action, interesting characters, and a firm sense of world building. I confess, when I started reading I didn't realize it was the start of a trilogy. I'm now all excited and horrified about the wait until we get the next part of the story. I hope that the plan is for the later books to go into where the epidemic comes from and how on earth it stops at the American borders. 
 Ruby was a fascinating protagonist, both damaged by her years in the camp and working so hard to move past them. Liam's optimism, Chubs' distrust and Suz's enthusiasm tied together beautifully, and Clancy was a perfect mix of possibilities. I'm also delighted at the lack of a love triangle since they seem to have become such a mainstay of YA lit. 
 There are a few minor issues that I had, like why did they keep talking about trains and buses when they were on the run? Mass transit seems like it would be a bad idea when you need to hide. 
 Overall, I think this is a very solid dystopian story which I highly recommend.

I'll probably read the next book when it comes out, but hopefully I won't have forgotten too much by that point. 
 Overall, it was an enjoyable read. There was lots of action and I liked the different powers/abilities. They were constantly on the move and there were times when I was surprised by the brutality of Alexandra Bracken's descriptions. Unfortunately, the ending was a bit predictable and lessened the impact (at least for me).

I read all three books within three days and haven't stopped thinking about the characters since. The story is exciting, suspenseful, heart-breaking, and just overall amazing--and I didn't set it down once until it was over. 
 I gotta say, it's been a while since I've read a book this good. Right from the start, the story is fast-paced and I was dying to find out what would happen next. At every turn there is suspense and action and I could picture every scene clearly in my head, thanks to Bracken's excellent writing. I became so attached to Ruby and her friends that I find myself thinking about them 24/7. It is nearly impossible not to love the main characters. While they can be frustrating at times, they are so real and so good, despite all of the terrible things they've had to deal with at such a young age. I was also pleased with how diverse their personalities were. My heart physically ached for them and I will humbly admit that I cried several times throughout the series. When I came to the last page of the third book I actually felt as if there was a gaping hole in my chest where my heart had previously been. In order to fill said empty void, I immediately picked up the first book and read the series again, from start to finish. I love this book, and the two that follow it, and I hope everyone is as moved by Ruby's story as I was!

book_b.title: Andre the Giant: Life and Legend
book_b.user_review:
I was fascinated by this look into moments through Andre the Giant's life from the opening author's note. Rather than writing (and drawing) a full biography Brown chose to pick specific moments from throughout Andre's life, significant and average, to show the contradictions of his personality; both as a wonderful person and a rather self-centred alcoholic who only met his daughter a couple of times. 
 Sifting the truth from the stories is a difficult procedure for any biographer, and the over the top nature of wrestling makes the process even more difficult. Andre was larger than life in every way, standing out from the start due to his illness. Switching from being publicly insulted and revered in the ring he was in near constant pain towards the end. This was a great view into his life.

sample_reviews.review_text: Well researched but very boring

The life of Andre the Giants is truly the stuff of legends. He grew up near Samuel Beckett, spent his youth in Paris, and then proceeded to professionally wrestle around the world, ending his great career after an acting stint in the Princess Bride. This graphic novel, is interesting, but it does fail to reach far beneath the surface of who Andre the Giant was. While the author states that he wants to present an honest portrayal of Andre's life, he does little to look at motivation or what made Andre tick. The book ends up depicting amusing vignette's from Andre's life and wrestling, but shows the reader little else.

I picked up this book as a long time lover of The Princess Bride- it's a classic. The book itself was so interesting, diving into Andre's wrestling career in the 1970s-80s. I had no idea that before the days of MMA, wrestling fights were staged (who knows, maybe they still are?) And this theme of "put on the mask" is present throughout the book. Those who knew Andre knew him as the "gentle giant," but Andre was cruely mad fun of most of his life due to his 7 foot plus height. Did I mention it's a graphic novel? Bonus. 
 I would have given this book more stars but it has too many heavy swear words, racial slurs, explicit sexual themes, and lots of drinking. Yes, he was an alcoholic, but adding in all of that was so unnecessary to the plot of the book. disappointing. To make the book accessible for grade students I ripped out 8 pages and sharpied words. Great story and illustrations, not so great book.

Since James handled the main review, I didn't give this a complete read until very recently. It's every bit as good as everyone said, and deserves all positive comments it's already gotten. 
 Box levels up here as a creator, using his geometric style to great effect, lending visual complexity to a biographical tale, and making the scale of Andre's size really show, especially in contrast to the other wrestlers. His likenesses are great, and I love that he discusses the realities of pro wrestling with its images and myths. 
 He also is very honest--Andre's not always shown in the best light--but doesn't condemn him for heavy drinking or having a rough side because of always being stared at, no matter where he went. 
 A stunning graphic biography that's a must-read for anyone who had just a bit of wrestling in their soul, or who still quotes from Princess Bride.

It's probably closer to three or three and a half stars, but I enjoyed it quite a bit, so I'm rounding up.

I would recommend this to a true fan of wrestling and to those who'd like a quick and light background of everyone's favorite Frenchman.

 Isis continues to be her crazy self and that's putting lightly. However, we finally get to see what lays beyond the sarcasm, wit and random acts of craziness. She is old enough to sleep over with a guy and be the crutch her mother needs, but her personality is that of a twelve year old. I will never understand that.

Isis is annoying, plain and simple, but her witty comments and comebacks help to keep this twisted, confusing novel afloat. Each character play their roles well, but I still can't put together the pieces of the puzzles that is this story. 
 We finally spend some time with Sophia, but don't expect much on that front either. The chick is coo coo crazy and I don't see what every one else does in her. A part from her being the block between Jack and Isis, the girl is pure evil and quite the manipulator. Her act at the end of this book, I believe was strategically done, to make the rift even bigger between Isis and Jack. 
 This is a dark, twisted tale of high school kids who behave like 30 year olds with major Nancy Drew/Hardy Boys complexes. reference_books.title: In a Dark, Dark Wood
reference_books.review_text:
3.25 Stars 
 Wow, I must say for a debut novel, this was really good. I was surprised how fast I read it, and was also very delighted about the fact that for a thriller, I wasn't dissapointed. I sure more could have been done, but honestly I really liked it. It was an easy read, and yes the main character Nora was kind of annoying, and yet unreliable, but I think in a mystery, it's supposed to happen. 
 Okay, so let me break it down, Nora is a shut in writer who gets an email saying that a friend of hers from way back (10 years) is getting married. And she's been invited to the Hen party. She's at first very reluctant to go, but decides to go anyway. She meets Tom, Nina, Flo, Melonie and Claire (the bride) for a weekend getaway in this glass house. But strange things are happening, footprints found outside, a back door left unlocked, phone missing, and one night someone dies and now we're trying to piece it all together before its too late, I can't really say anymore, due to spoilers but it's a good fun read that had me guessing right up til the end.

book_a.user_review:

 Reading this book, I was easily transported back to Neptune, California, back to Mars Investigations. The witty banter and snappy comebacks were just as funny as before. 
 Veronica is one of my favorite female PIs. She's tough, smart, resourceful and charming. And the love she has for her father is beautiful. I love their teamwork. I can just go on and on. It was just like reading a new VM episode and it didn't dissapoint.

sample_reviews.review_text: Over all, this more like a 3.5 book. It's got the true-to-original feeling to it, but at the same time it's still missing something. No Logan beating people up? Not enough Weevil being a bad-ass? It's a solid read, an I'll be reading the next one for sure...but it doesn't quite add up to the experience of watching the show; so rarely do these things. But, for a fix it's worth the time.
An okay read, but nothing too special. Review to come.

Rob Thomas writes a story like it's a script from the Veronica Mars TV series of years ago. He should, he was the writer of the TV series for some seasons. But I digress. 
 A girl goes missing in Neptune, CA during spring break. Veronica is worried about her dad. Their investigation company is pulling in so little dough, not so much as a cookie will crumble in the crime-mystery biz. What to do? 
 A rich, snobby gal from Neptune's Chamber of Commerce walks in and challenges Veronica to take on the missing girl case. Lots of money to be had. 
 I did not like all the red herrings. The cousins that could be part of a Mexican drug cartel; the missing girl's necklace shows up; and another girl goes missing from the same party -- call come together and mean absolutely nothing. 
 At least not until the end, when a predictable ending (granted, it still had a twist of lemon in it) ends the book with lots of questions as to what happened to certain personnel (whom you won't really care about) as to their fate or whereabouts! 
 Last Word: 
 Overall a decent Young Adult novel that captures the feisty nature of Veronica Mars. No romance in this one, but a few tearjerker scenes that will have you reaching for the Kleenex in no time. A bit too much herring in this dish, however.
Fun, though still not really my genre. Which makes it fun - still a novelty for me to read detective stories.
A fun mystery plot but I have never watched any Veronica Mars & could tell so much important backstory was missing. The characters stayed strangers.
Never seen the TV series but this was a fun story, well read by Kristen Bell.
Not a Mars fan, so not utterly impressed. The mystery solved, as if there had been none.

For hardcore VM fans only. I liked the series well enough, but it didn't translate well to the printed page for me. I guess this is a Young Adult novel? Maybe that's why it felt so pat and artificial. Like Nancy Drew with a few swears sprinkled in.

I loved this book. Entertaining whodunnit and interesting characters made it so I resented real life interfering in my reading time. 
 If you've read the first two Robert Galbraith books you will be familiar with the central characters - Private Detective/ex military policeman Cormoran Strike and his assistant Robin Ellacott. Career of Evil follows directly on from The Silkworm, so if you haven't read The Cuckoo's Calling and The Silkworm, you won't necessarily understand a lot of the references. 
 There's a killer murdering and mutilating women and the evidence keeps leading back to Strike. The story follows Strike and Robin's efforts to identify and stop the killer, while keeping the business running, not putting the police offside and dealing with their personal relationships.

reference_books.title: Does the Noise in My Head Bother You?
reference_books.review_text: I love Aerosmith. I found this fun but occasionally incomprehensible. But that was kind of good in that he does his best to take us inside the Tyler head. Basically, Steven Tyler really loves music. And drugs. And sex. It'd have been fun to have heard more about some of the specific antics they got up to, the laddish pranks and the monster bonking that went down. But then again, how much of the 70's can the old boy remember? Oh, and for those of you who think he comes across as a bit egotistical and self-centered. Erm, he's a rock star. Still, saying that, it would have been nice to have heard a bit more about the musical dynamic in the band, rather than just "Here's all the ace shit I did." And, it'd have been perhaps more engaging if Mr. Tyler hadn't so obviously read all the other bios about him and Aerosmith and band members and decided to settle a few scores. But, you know, he's human, and he's a musician and a lyricist, not a writer of tomes. And this is mucho better than most bios, which - let's face it - are utter bilge.

sample_reviews.review_text: I think I hated this book. Oh, I know what he was trying to do with the satirical look at the war and I appreciate that to some extent. I will relent to an extent that some of the actual Dresden parts might have been somewhat interesting. I also understand that some authors like to put cute little catch phrases in their manuscripts to establish a unique voice, but what worked for Holden Caulfied did not work for Billy Pilgrim. "So it goes" and "and so on" were thrown onto almost every page--someone could easily count how many times--and it was just really tiresome.

For being such a classic piece of literature, I was surprisingly underwhelmed by the whole thing. There isn't much rising action or a climax, nothing important seems to happen. There were a few sentences that were fairly poignant, but they tended to be few and far between. There was also very little resolution. I'll give it credit for the literary classic it is, especially since it was a quick read.
If I had a different taste in books, I'd have probably enjoyed this. But it just wasn't my cup of tea although Vonnegut is actually a smart novelist.

I think I might have given up on this book,had it not been so short...it jumped about too much in time for me...and said the words "and so it goes" far more than I needed to read them. 
 I'm not sure why its such a famous book......
wow! This book continued to suprise me! The story follows a nonlinear plot, reveals some of the harsh realities of war and life after war and even includes alien encounters!

So, I'd read this one as a precocious 19-year-old in 1990 eager to read the counter-culture classics, and today I re-read it for the first time as an old fart with a couple of self-published novels under my belt and wanted to see if Vonnegut's most famous work was still as good as I remembered it. It wasn't. 
 It was much better. 
 Or, I've matured enough to appreciate there was more going on than a zany, ingenious, funny, sexy, one-liner-filled tale of time travel and the pointlessness of war. Somehow, what had completely passed my teenage self was that this was all of the above and also a touching portrait of a veteran with post traumatic stress disorder and as true a first-hand account of the destruction of Dresden as you are ever going to read. It's as relevant today as it was to 1945, 1968, 2001 or any other date before or since resonating with atrocities at our own hands. So it goes.

book_b.title: Notes from a Small Island
book_b.user_review: It's great writing, and sweet enough and he seems like a likeable bloke, but his England is a slightly overbearing compliment.

sample_reviews.review_text:
Another Bryson travel book that was a slog to get through. 
 There was very little that was fun or entertaining to read in this book. If I was his travel companion I would have had a very boring time (I know Bryson to be a fascinating writer from his other non-fiction works so I don't know why this journey was so average). 
 The basic gist of the book is that Bryson goes on a farewell tour of the UK. He stays at a lot of b&bs, eats a lot of curry, visits towns that offer little in the way of tourism and travels on many trains. 
 I am not arguing that this book isn't a realistic portrayal of what makes the UK the UK. If you were to undertake the same journey as Bryson I am sure your experience would be the same. In a way he does the reader a favour by warning them that if you try to find excitement or tourist opportunities in sleepy towns you are not going to find them. I wish though that some exciting, wonderful, interesting tourism experiences were peppered throughout the book to provide the reader with the idea of where to go.

I thought this would be a great read as an American having just spent the summer with my in-laws in Manchester, but I'm having a hard time getting into it. Seems very outdated and also specific to the southwest.

The book where it comes to light that Bill Bryson is a miserable middle aged American white guy who hates fat people, people in the service industry, and everything that came into existence after the Victorian era.

This was a bit of a mix for me, in places I really enjoyed it- it's very well researched and I liked the odd bits of info thrown in that I'd never have known about my own country if I hadn't read this however Bryson does seem to consider Britain one massive tourist attraction that should be preserved as is for the visitor to view rather than a country that has to change to meet the needs of a population and keep up with the changes in technology. 
 Bryson also comes across as fairly contemptuous of a lot of the people he meets and in a few places he's downright horrible to them. In general I found the tone of the book a bit smug and Bryson seems very impressed with his own writing and his own intelligence (vastly superior to most the people he meets if you were wondering) so I just didn't enjoy the style. I should say I listened to the audible audiobook so I might have enjoyed it more had I read it.

Wow. How boring was this book?? And why oh why does Bill Bryson have to torment me so?? 
 I discovered Bill Bryson shortly before I read Notes and seriously thought I had hit a goldmine; I thought he'd be my new favorite author, that I'd be reading his entire collection, that I wouldn't be able to get enough. Part travel writer, part humorist, part explorer-of-curiosities and part taker-of-challenges, Bryson writes things I want to read about: hiking the Appalachian Trail, returning to America after 20 years abroad, Australia...everything he wrote sounded interesting! I love Britain, so despite a "meh" experience with Bryson's A Walk in the Woods, I was willing to give Notes from a Small Island a chance. 
 This, it turns out, was a big mistake. Somehow, the book that I thought would be full of funny observations and charming details about jolly old England turned out to be, well, pretty much just that---but gone terribly wrong. As was the case with A Walk in the Woods, Bryson tells a funny story, full of keen observations, dark humor and interesting facts, but as a whole, the book didn't come together. All the pieces were there, so this was very disappointing indeed. 
 Essentially, this book is like sitting through a slide show (sans visuals) tour of Britain, and even though the host might be a funny guy who you'd really like to go grab a pint with, you're still like wait, seriously? There are how many more slides to go?? 
 Side note: Part of me still wants to read the rest of Bryson's books...it's as though I can't convince myself that no, I am not a Bill Bryson fan. Sad day.

You'd be excused for thinking Bryson despises Britain, despite his statements to the contrary, because he spends the majority of this book complaining about the architecture and making subtle unkind jabs at the people he meets. I assume he hates modern Britain and only loves picturesque old timey postcard Britain. 
 Not his best.

Pode dizer-se que detestei este livro. 
 Quando o vi a venda, em portugues, pensei que se tratava de um livro que eu precisava muito de ler, devido a minha anglofilia absoluta. Tratei, portanto, de o comprar no original e foi-me trazido, por uma mala amiga, da propria Inglaterra. 
 Estas cronicas, chamemos-lhe, foram escritas no inicio dos anos 90 quando Bill Bryson, americano de origem e morador no Reino Unido ha duas decadas, decide fazer uma viagem pela ilha em despedida, ja que pretende regressar ao seu pais com a familia. 
 Vai, portanto, de terra em terra, usando essencialmente o comboio e os seus proprios pes, falando um pouco de cada sitio, comparando as suas memorias antigas de outras visitas com as actuais, comentando isto, discutindo aquilo. 
 Parecia-me uma boa premissa. 
 Acontece que Bryson teve a infeliz ideia de banir quase por completo a utilizacao de um automovel e ir de viagem no pico do Inverno (sim, no Reino Unido). Portanto, e claro que debaixo de lencois de agua fica dificil gostar de alguma coisa, como alias parece ser o seu caso, que detesta tudo. Cada cidade, cada nova ladainha critica. 
 Alem disso, o gosto por dada cidade parece ser proporcional a quantidade e tipo de comida que o autor ingere durante a sua estadia. Em geral, o ciclo e o seguinte: 
 1. Ah eis-nos chegados a X, da qual tenho boas memorias. Vou ali ao restaurante Y que costumava ser tao bom. What. Que e isto? Que nojo. Odeio X. Nunca mais ca volto. 
 2. Ah eis-nos chegados a X, essa cidade atrofiada e palerma. So estou aqui porque, enfim, nem sei bem. Calhou, so havia comboios para aqui de onde estava antes. Que ranhosa de cidade. Que ridiculo. Olha, estes palermas tem aqui um restaurante mais ou menos decente. Vou entrar e comer, pronto. 
 Depois, grande parte das suas memorias sao pautadas por momentos de autentica ma-educacao em que Bryson descarrega em cima de um ingles a sua frustracao, cansaco, fome e mau-humor, as vezes tudo junto. Por exemplo, quando chega a Edimburgo esta todo encantado (e penso eu, claro, nem o teu mau-humor resiste a Edimburgo). Ate abre os cordoes a bolsa e decide ficar no hotel Caledonian (um dos melhores hoteis da cidade, basta verem uma foto dele para perceberem como deve ser caro). Nada mau, Bryson. Estas a redimir-te. Mas assim que percebe que o pequeno-almoco lhe vai custar 14 libras (a serio, achavas que no Caledonian te ia custar quanto, zero?), volta todo o mau espirito, cancela o pedido e sai disparado pelas ruas escocesas a dizer mal de tudo. 
 Nao aguentei. Passei metade do livro a revirar os olhos e outra metade a ler na diagonal, sem acreditar que alguem publicou esta compilacao ranhosa de critica. Aparentemente, os leitores acham alguma graca ao livro, diz quem la vive que se gosta mais da escrita dele quando se conhecem estes lugares. Ate pode ser, mas a mim parece-me que ele tira a vontade toda de conhecer seja o que for. 
 Esquecam isto e leiam outras coisas.

It took me forever to read this because I was constantly picking it up and putting it down, not because I wasn't enjoying it, but because it's one of those books where it works to read it in this way, and I read so many other books during the times I took breaks from reading this book. 
 Sometimes I just don't like Bill Bryson as a man. There's a smattering of things he writes that are cruel, crass, and otherwise makes him unappealing to me, and he sure drinks a lot of beer, but the nasty material is a tiny minority of the book's content. 
 He's basically a likeable and interesting guy who is an explorer, much of it done via walking, and he has a refreshing sense of what constitutes adventure. 
 He's a skilled writer. He's very, very funny; I laughed out loud and chuckled many times. 
 I've always wanted to go to Britain so for me this was a bit of armchair traveling. Unfortunately, much of this book made me wish I'd visited the place (and most other places) at least a few decades ago. Bryson makes clear the homogenization that's taken place at various British locales, and this book was written 15 years ago so who knows what he'd say now. I'd still love to go but I'd skip some of his destinations. He also writes much about the history of his destinations and I found most of the information fascinating. 
 One thing that tickled my funny bone is that when he was in one small English town, he saw the old "This is Cinerama" movie, a movie I remember from my childhood, and brought me right back to the United States of America. I hadn't realized the movie was already old the first time that I saw it, but I do remember loving that film and other Cinerama movies. 
 There's a glossary of English (vs. American English) words in the back of the book. Given that I'm a bit of an Anglophile, I already knew the definition of most of the words, but having it in the book was a fun touch.

Disclaimer: I only got through just more than half of this book, so it could have improved after that point, but I had already spent too much time trying to drudge through the book to wait for that possibility to come to fruition. 
 As much as I wanted to like this book, and believe me when I say I really wanted to, I just couldn't get through it. Perhaps someone more familiar with the United Kingdom would appreciate it more, but it was too much detail in all the wrong places. Yes, there were points when I laughed out loud, but these were offset with a much larger amount of boring text. :(

reference_books.title: Tangled (Tangled, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
Ok, firstly let me introduce you the main reason you should read this book. It is called Drew Evans!!! 
 Girls I am pretty sure that in your reading life you have met a lot of literature naughty, cynical, womanizer men but let me tell you that Drew Evans is the king of them. 
 Tangled is definitely of the most entertaining books I have read lately. Light and funny read with this great and easy writing style that sometimes almost makes you forget that you are actually reading and you start checking the doors in case Drew comes to ask advice about him and Kate. 
 The main storyline well known. The bad and cynical boy who finally falls in love well in case of Drew he gets the flu. So with such a typical story you will ask why to prefer this book. Did I mention it is Drew Evans? 
 Well actually now I am thinking Drew is not exactly the bad guy of the story a little playboy yes but not a bad guy. He is working really hard, he loves his family, he is a good man. He just has a thing with serious relationships and a very, very big mouth like every man. Girls forget the books with the girl's point of view. Forget tears, love, proderm and pink clouds because the book is written from Drew's point of view. Maybe I am still laughing out loud with him. Drew has a big mouth and has no problem let it sing jajaja 
 For those ladies out there who are listening, let me give you some free advice: If a guy who you just met at a club calls you baby, sweetheart, angel or any other generic endearment? Don't make the mistake of thinking he's so into you, he's already thinking up pet names. It's because he can't or doesn't care to remember your actual name. 
 I blame Adam. Now theres a guy who had the world by the balls. Walking around naked, a hot chick to satisfy his every whim. I sure hope that apple was tasty, 'cause he really fucked it up for the rest of us. 
 If I put down all Drew's quotes I think I could make a book. The encyclopedia of love by Drew Evans. What a brilliant find from the author writing the book from the male POV. So many quotes that I think that in my bad days I will return back to this book re-reading them and still laughing with them. This is probably how I spent the whole time reading this book 
 "For God's sake, don't let her watch Cinderella. What kind of example is that? A mindless twit who can't even remember where she left her damn shoe, so she has to wait for some douchebag in tights to bring it to her? Give me a frigging break!" 
 Which reminds me- Martha Stewart? She's my new idol. Seriously. I used to think her whole deal was a joke. Who becomes a billionaire by showing people how to fold goddamn dinner napkins correctly? But that was before. Before I actually tried to use my own oven or set a table. Now Martha's a fucking god. Like Buddha. And if her recipe helps me pulls this off? I'll worship at her pudgy sandaled feet every day for the rest of my life. 
 God I love male POV's Seriously I don't remember having so much fun reading a book 
 The true story begins after we find out Drew's main problem. Don't tell me you believed he has the flu? And what happens when the flu gets a name and it is called Kate? Well it means that you need to take medication. Not to mention that all his rules of women and dating in general fly out of the window 
 Women fall in love quicker than men. Easier and more often. But when guys fall? We go down harder. And when things go bad? When it's not us who ends it? We don't get to walk away. 
 We crawl. " 
 What I am trying to say all this time but I can't actually find the exact words is that there is one an simple reason why this book is so addictive and hilarious. Ok yes I told you that before. It is Drew Evans. But it is Drew because reading this book from his point of view it was actually like we were living ourselves the story. It is so big the connection with him that you think the whole time he was talking to you that you were sitting next to him like taking him an interview. There is no biggest success of a book than being so direct and refreshing like you are present.Let's be honest we as a women are more closed, sometimes no one can predict what it inside a woman mind. Men express more easily and this is what makes them so lovable in books 
 And besides of this you will have the opportunity to read a great story which was not only sex, it was actually more than that. God the man watched the notebook and beauty and the beast to win his girl's heart 
 "Edward Cullen can take his stupid heroine and OD on it. Kate is my own personal brand of Viagra." 
 Sssssss don't tell her he told that

3 stars from me. Ok don't get me wrong please I liked the book, I really liked. God I had missed so fucking much Drew Evan's sharp tongue, big spicy mouth and I really laughed out loud with all the funny scenes in the entire book but here is my problem. Oh please Drew I still love you don't look at me with this pissed look. I am blushing. I still love you I swear. 
 When I realized that in this 4th book of tangled series we would have the story written by drew's POV I felt like this 
 God I was dying being in this man head again even more now he was the big daddy. Drew Evans is definitely one of my favorite book characters. I loved him in tangle and just reading the first pages of tied reminded me why I loved him so much in first place. The man is a king when god made him the definitely broke the mold. Reading a book from drew evan's pov at least is a guarantee you will never get bored. The little God of love and life really knows how to offer to the readers hilarious, sexy and funny moments with just opening his mouth 
 But now it is time to explain what I felt it was wrong with the book. The book starts two years later after twisted. Now Drew Evans is a father and he is preparing for the big day, his wedding with Kate. Drew, and Kate have really grown up all these years. Ok, ok Drew still remains the same Drew we loved from tangled 
 "Prince William and Kate can kiss my ass. Amateurs. We've got this wedding-of-the-century thing in the bag." 
 "What do you want, James?" My voice has a frustrated edge. "You're dry, I'm holding you, I'm trying to feed you--what the hell do you want?" I walk back to the kitchen and grab the checkbook off the counter. 
 "Will money make you happy?" 
 Ridiculous--yes, I know. Don't judge me. 
 "I'll give you ten thousand dollars for four hours of sleep. I'll write the check out right now."

I like the after stories but in this case I don't I guess that I would prefer an extra chapter on the second book with only the wedding day included. This book reminded me how Hollywood works. If a movie has success we make the sequel no matter if we don't have a story. It is all about the money.  3,5 stars from me .Let me first tell you that I liked the book, I really did and I found it entertaining but I had some issues with it which prevent from characterize the book as a BIG and memorable book. 
 Bad Romeo tells the story of Cassie Taylor and Ethan Holt and alternates between the present and the past. In the first part that takes place in the present Cassie and Ethan are already famous and successful actors and former lovers too that find themselves having to work together for a Broadway show. Now 6 years after they first met both Cassie and Ethan have made their dreams to become respectable actors but the one sure thing is that Cassie wants nothing to do with him again after Ethan broke her heart 6 years ago. All this time we as a readers know that something really, really bad must have happened with them in the past but we have no idea of what that was except it must be bad and it was all Ethan's fault. 
 The other part of the book takes place in the past when they both auditioned to the Grove institute of arts. When they meet each other there is an instant attraction between them. Ethan Holt is auditioning for the third time and if we won't make it he won't able to audition again. He is passionate with acting but also mysterious, a loner and he has built his own walls and don't let anyone get in. Cassie is quite the opposite. She found her calling to acting coming from a small town of Washington and growing with over protective parents made her more pleasant. Even though in the begging Ethan is quite cold with her she finds her self really attracted to him. Even though he warns her that he is not good guy for her to hang out with she is still trying to change his mind and become his friend and something more actually. Cassie never actually had a boyfriend or being kissed and she has this obsession of people like her. Even though they are different Cassie manage to get under his skin. Their chemistry is so obvious and intense that even their teacher notices that and casts them for the leading roles of Romeo and Juliet. 
 Back in present we find Ethan desperate for a reconciliation when in past they put fire on the scene with their chemistry but when they are in public they pretend they don't like each other but behind doors they make their no label friendship stronger if you know what I mean. Because Ethan had warned her he is not the right guy for her he wants to keep secret their dating and he refuses to give her what she desperately wants from him to take her virginity. 
 Why? Is the world going to end if we hang out?" 
 He fixes me with an intense expression. "Yes The seas will boil, the skies will darken, and every volcano in the world will erupt, thus bringing an end to civilization as we know it. So for the sake of humanity...in fact, for the sake of everything you hold dear...stay away from me." He's so serious, it makes me think he isn't joking. 
 What is weird now that am thinking of it is that Ethan in the past put all his energy in order to make Cassie to stay away from him because he was the worst thing that could happen to her and now in present he desperately wants a reconciliation believing he is now the best thing for her. 
 So let me sum up what I liked and what I didn't in this book and explain the reasons why I enjoyed the book but I didn't love it 
 what I liked 
 1.	Even though I had serious problems with the plot line I loved the writing. It was refreshing and hilarious in many occasions. 
 2.	The incredible chemistry between the two main heroes. Even though I had many issues with them as individuals and especially with Cassie God when they were together . 
 3.	Ethan Holt. Ok his was jerk, and asshole and put any other adjective you want but I really, really loved him when he opened his mouth to make a point. your diary was my literature Viagra I loved his sarcasm and funny lines. 
 what I didn't like 
 1.	Cassie, Cassie and did I mention Cassie? Cassie's need for sex was so exaggerated to the point of annoyance. Her character can be summed up with this 
 For God's shake girl please we get it. Ethan is a hot guy, you want to lose your virginity but fuck you literally. God this horny virgin really pissed me off. I hated she acted like there is no other interest in life than sex and so what she was a virgin. She was only 19. Ok her little obsession might seemed funny in the beginning but after of 4568 times she said that

Ok I totally understand that she felt broken, that Ethan was bad with her but at least in the present time we see an improved image of him when she is turned into a bitch sleeping with every man. So matured. Not to mention her insecurity problems and her obsession to make people like her. As you understand when you have issues with the main heroine it is difficult to bond with the book. With Ethan I had also a few issues. To be honest I liked him more. He maybe was a jerk and a complete asshole but he was also intense, knowing what to want most of the time

sample_reviews.review_text:
Llega Maldito Romeo a demostrarnos que Fifty Shades of Grey parece seguir inspirando historias acerca de un chico malo -porque esta "traumado"- y una chica virgen -que aunque es guapisima y sexy, nadie se explica por que sigue virgen- que se enamoran y viven un "torrido" romance. 
 Cassandra (Cassie) es una chica modelo, que no bebe, no fuma, saca brillantes calificaciones, y no desobedece en lo minimo a sus padres -y ademas es virgen-. Ella suena con ser actriz e irse lo mas lejos posible de su casa (cosa que dice, pero que no nos queda del todo claro por que). Asi que al audicionar y ser aceptada The Grove -universidad especializada en artes escenicas-, su vida cambia; sobre todo despues de conocer a Ethan -nuestro protagonista muy a la "soy malo porque estoy traumado"- y literalmente OBSESIONARSE con su pene. Y es que, por favor, todas las virgenes de 19 anos de obsesionan con el pene del chico que acaban de conocer, ?no? 
 El desarrollo comenzo bien. Me gusto la voz que Leisa le dio a Cassie. Directa y comica en tonos sexuales sin caer en la vulgaridad. Apenas estaba comenzando el libro y ya la queria para cotillear. Daba la apariencia de ser una mujer abierta y madura. Eso hasta el primer 30% del libro, porque despues, la historia y el mismo personaje comienzan a caer y caer y caer. 
 La autora nos narra la historia entre el presente y el pasado -seis anos atras-, nos lleva a su encuentro a raiz de su reencuentro, y hay que decir que la estructura de la anacronia deja mucho que desear, bueno en otros terminos, es horrible. El presente, a veces esta narrado en fragmentos muy cortos y el pasado en dos o mas capitulos enteros, y viceversa. Las entradas del diario de Cassey son inutiles, no aportan absolutamente nada a la trama. Incluso si Ethan -Spoiler Alert- no hubiera leido este, la historia se hubiera mantenido igual: leeeeenta y tediosa. Debo de reconocer su pluma, eso si, excelentes descripciones y con una narrativa que te mantiene pegada al libro y que te arrancan carcajadas en muchas ocasiones. Todos los personajes secundarios estan bien definidos y causan empatia con el lector, aunque hubiera estado padre que profundizaran mas en ellos. Me hubiera gustado conocer mas de Tristan y Ruby, por ejemplo. Y es que todo fue tocado tan superficial, tan rapido, restandole importancia para darle lugar a los repetitivos encuentros de los protagonistas. La novela se mantuvo, hasta sus 472 paginas, con escenas en las que Cassandra le pedia literalmente a Ethan que la desprendiera de su virginidad, y el negandose. Al principio se maneja excelentemente bien la tension sexual de los personajes, se puede incluso palpar y arrancarle sensaciones al lector, pero es que tras ochocientos encuentros del mismo tipo, termina siendo repetitiva y hasta molesto. 
 - Te quiero, Christian Ethan. Y a tu pene, 
 - Alejate de mi, Anastasia Cassie. Yo y mi pene no te convenimos. 
 El final... !Vaya, el final! Ya sabia que este era la primera entrega de una serie de tres pero es que el cliffhanger es el peor que he leido y que he vivido y que he... Es muy malo, punto. 
 La historia ya la vivi. Solo que a diferencia de esta historia, el tipo tenia millones de dolares, ella no estudiaba teatro sino letras, y a el le gustaba amarrarla a la cama. El tambien fue adoptado a los tres anos -creo-, y en el fondo era un tipo debil e inseguro, y solo con ella puso abrirse al mundo. Me costo mucho trabajo llegar al final despues del 30% del libro, lo dejaba y francamente no tenia la necesidad de iniciarlo de nuevo. 
 Creo que la historia es ciertamente mala, el contexto es malo, el personaje de Ethan es muy malo. Pero el acierto es que Leisa sabe contar historias con humor -por mas malas que estas sean-. Y que a pesar de todo hay obviedades. Podemos adivinar que Ethan dejo a Cassie luego de desprenderla de su molesta virginidad, y que esta fue la primera vez que le rompio el corazon. Que los papeles estaran cambiados, ahora sera Ethan el que ruegue por Cassie, y que ahora ella sera la herida, la desconfiada, la que no se entrega. La traumada, pues. Pero al final, como siempre, el amor triunfara. Porque si fuera el amor propio entonces si me sorprenderia. 
 Me gustan las historias en las que el nino es malo porque ha sufrido y en la que ella, inocente y virginal, lo cambia con dulzura y amor -y humillandose a veces un poco, si no hay mas remedio-. La prueba esta en que le tengo un desmesurado carino al senor Grey. Pero esta historia, sencillamente no. No porque ya la vi antes, y no porque Ethan ni siquiera tiene un buen argumento para ser el monumental patan. No porque la voz de la protagonista (que es la voz de toda la historia) te abandona en menos de la mitad de la historia, y dejas de disfrutarla. No porque las escenas entre ellos muchas veces se sienten forzadas. No, porque hay recursos inecesarios. Y no porque me senti defraudada.

This was pretty much my face expression during the 62% I read 
 I really wasn't impressed by this book. The cover and the title of the book is probably the best things about it. Note to myself: Stop reading books based on their pretty covers. 
 Anyway, at first I really thought it would be an interesting story with pretty unique setting, two persons with intense chemistry cast for the leading roles in Romeo and Juliet and sparks fly. Although, that was the case, I really did not enjoy it. 
 For one, the heroine. I can't even express in words how much I disliked her. She was a girl without an opinion, always saying whatever people wanted to hear and doing whatever was necessary to be liked. I felt like her whole persona was fake. I can forgive her for being young and maybe she hasn't found herself yet, but when we see Cassie after 6 years, it's the same bloody girl just a bit bitter. Another things about her I hated was how horny she was all the time, and when I say all the time, I really mean ALL THE FREAKING TIME. Her vagina was constantly aroused and she was turned on the moment she woke up all day every day. 
 Another thing, the hero. I usually find a lot of redeeming qualities in book heroes, even when I don't like the heroines, but in this case Ethan was almost as unlikable as Cassie. His mixed signals, his jerk attitude towards Cassie, his daddy issues, his 'awful past' and his 'i'm cancer' really didn't work for me. Plus he was almost as horny as Cassie. 
 Third, there wasn't any connection. They talked about the intense connection between them all the time, but I really didn't see it because all they did was talk about how badly they want to rip each others clothes off and all they did was try to do just that, with kissing and humping each other on stage. There is a difference between chemistry and connection. Chemistry is more of a physical attraction while connection is something deeper such as trust and understand of each other. They were definitely missing that, because I didn't see why would they love each other if not for the lust. 
 Fourth, I like second chance romances and I don't mind jumping from past to present and back, but when it happens I expect to feel different emotions reading the past and the present. Please give me pain, regret and heartache. No, that wasn't the case here, those six years didn't change either of them much, and it really didn't feel like any time had passed. Yeah, Ethan asks for forgiveness and Cassie is hurt and angry, but all they still want to do is jump each other. Also, the switching from past to present was exhausting here. Past - Cassie chases Ethan, present Ethan chases Cassie. I can't even say if I disliked their past or present more. 
 Another new adult novel which is a utterly disappointing. This really wasn't for me.
