BOOKS WITH SUMMER VIBES = YES PLEASE. This book makes me want to make my own list because lists are the best things in the world, let's be honest. I loved the adventures and all the characters. I especially liked Frank because his best trait wasn't his looks; it was for his knowledge and success. Which is awesome!! I love when characters are defined by traits such as these :) 
 "All the stuff you can't wait to get away from, until it's not there anymore, and then you miss it like crazy."

Since You've Been Gone was my first read by Morgan Matson and I can say with certainty that it won't be my last. 
 The story stars quite suddenly, with Emily finding that her best friend, Sloane, is gone. There was no notice, no goodbye message, and no note explaining her sudden departure. But things take a turn when one day Emily receives a to-do list from Sloane. After weeks of worry, she finally receives something from Sloane. Emily believes that by completing all the items on the list she will somehow get her best friend back. And so begins Emily's most epic summer, filled with new friends, self-discovery, and adventure. 
 Morgan Matson has developed great characters that were very genuine and memorable. I found most of the characters to be very relatable, Emily in particular. She was very shy and socially clumsy. I am quite shy and tend to be quite awkward in social situations, so I found her very endearing and was able to instantly connect with her. 
 The novel is filled with flashbacks on Emily and Sloane's friendship, how they met, and how their relationship evolved over the years. In the flashbacks, we get a sense that Emily is quite dependent on Sloane. She appears to live vicariously through Sloane. She is more confident when Sloane is around because she allows Sloane to take the lead; but when Sloane disappears, she finds herself quite lost. People don't seem to really know her in school except as the girl who is always with Sloane. Additionally, the flashbacks provide an insight into what kind of person Sloane is; she is portrayed as very outgoing, friendly, and thirsty for adventure and mischief. While reading, at first I was convinced that Emily relied too much on Sloane, but as the story developed I understood just how much Sloane relied on Emily as well. 
 As Emily starts completing tasks from the list, with the much unexpected help from Frank Porter, she manages to make new friends. At first the friends she makes are almost by accident because she doesn't know how to handle or avoid certain situations. However, throughout the book we get to see Emily find her own voice, grow more confident, make new friends, make mistakes and learn from them, build new relationships, and most importantly find her own identity. 
 The book was a great journey of self-growth and self-discovery. I really liked that while the book did have some romance, it was not the main focus. I loved the relationship Emily had with her parents and her brother, and all the relationships and friendships she built over the summer. The book expressed how important it is to surround ourselves with worthy people, because the people in our live have a huge effect on us. The book starts with Emily being completely lost, and in a slight state of depression, but with each page she finds herself and becomes a much stronger person; she does so with the help of the people she has around her. 
 The items on the list that Emily had to complete were very funny. There were many times I found myself laughing out loud, earning me quite a few curious glances from those around me. 
 Since You've Been Gone was the perfect start to my summer reading; it was a fun and easy read. It is one of the best books featuring friendships that I have ever read. I found Morgan Matson's writing style to be just wonderful; she is an incredible storyteller and I cannot wait to read her other works, as I am convinced that they are equally amazing.

I enjoyed this book way more than I anticipated. Refreshingly, Matson did NOT follow the typical boy meets girl and they instantly fall in love pattern found in many YA contemporaries. Instead, themes of friendship and inner confidence and courage ran deep throughout the story. Overall 4/5 stars; this novel far exceeded my expectations!

Frank and Emily end up getting married, no one fight me on this. This book was absolutely amazing. Too bad I was in the middle of a reading slump and it took me weeks to finish, but by the end of it, I was close to tears, which is a rare thing. It's currently 12:26 and I'm still freaking out over the ending. I highly recommend.

Man, this book was good and so hard to put down!! I loved both Amy & Roger's Epic Detour and Second Chance Summer so there was no surprise that I would love this too! I'm still processing my thoughts and will be working on a review, just know this book was amazing and I highly recommend it!! <3

In a well ordered universe, I still find myself reading this book. 
 Yaaaay! Loved it, even though I feel like there's something missing. Gideon, Dawn, and Collins' story arcs were left hanging. And I wanted more of Frank and Emily! Haha.

 tension and action. Keeps you off the street.

reference_books.title: Red Country (First Law World, #6)

reference_books.title: The Whistler
reference_books.review_text: A good read, better than the last two. Plenty of twists and turns, action and interesting characters. Back in the groove

reference_books.title: Make Me (Jack Reacher, #20)
reference_books.review_text: I really enjoyed this novel. The new Reacher book has become a date in the diary. Could not resist, had to buy it and I was not disappointed. Excellent plot and plenty of action. Reacher is more fleshed out and that along with a few other points might surprise many Reacher fans.

book_a.title: The Overlook (Harry Bosch, #13; Harry Bosch Universe, #16)
book_a.user_review: Another page runner from Harry Bosch. Really enjoyed it. Well worth a read. Sort and snappy, it's got an excellent pace.

sample_reviews.review_text: This is one of the thinnest Bosch books but that doesn't stop it from being a good read. Someone who handles radioactive materials for a living is killed and the feds jump right in on the case. Harry focuses on the murder while the feds hunt the radioactive materials. The usual friction comes up and it is complicated by the fact that Harry is working with someone he knows from the FBI. This is a nice tight quick read. Excellent storytelling as usual.

Not sure why this one didn't appeal as much as previous Bosch's. Moved along, actually taking only about 12 hours 
 The usual tension with the FBI and Rachel Walling. An MD is murdered, ostensibly by some terrorists who want the radioactive cesium he has access to in his practice. And Harry is the only one who wants to pursue it as a murder. 
 I guess there were too many leaps of logic toward the end for me to really buy. But I will persist in this series. Don't know how many more there are in the series.
I like Harry Bosch.
Very suspenseful and hard to put down. I can't say much without spoilers, so I'll just say it's another good Bosch investigation.
Love Harry B books usually, but this one? Meh
A quick read. Good beach book.
Another fun book. Closer to just cop drama, no Sad Harry drama. Good change of pace.
Someone is murdered and the investigation turns up a terrorist angle, but thanks to Bosch the real story comes to light.
Read this mainly because I previously had Michael Connelly and John Connolly confused with each other. Having read a crime/thriller from each, I can now tell them apart.

The Overlook is in my opinion the weakest of the series. I read somewhere the novel first appeared as a series of weekly installments in some magazine or newspaper, then someone said, 'pad it out and we'll stick a cover on it.' It has the pacing of such an endeavor. I just didn't care for it. 
 Reviewed by, David Feeney, author; Terror on the high seas

book_b.title: The Way of Shadows (Night Angel, #1)
book_b.user_review: I can't make my mind upo on this book. In many ways it was good. There were strong characters and an exciting, well paced story but I flet a bit "meh" about it and was not really bothered whether i finished it or not.

sample_reviews.review_text: Eh, just not that into it.

I'm roughly 25% into this book, and it hasn't grabbed me yet. I keep hearing good things about this, so I'm begging you guys to maybe motivate me or confirm my initial thoughts. 
 So far, the writing is fine. There's nothing good or bad about it, which is just fine with me for a funtasy book. One minor quirk: Durzo is a badass, I get it, no need to keep repeating that Durzo is the greatest-most-bestest-awesomest assassin. It cheapens the character. I swear at one point the narration actually points out that he's the best assassin, as if "best assassin" is some plaque Durzo received. 
 Okay, that rant aside, the rest of it is fine. That's kind of the problem. There's nothing GREAT about it. The characters don't stand out at all. You get the baddestass assassin and a protege who's lived a really harsh life, but 25% into it, and I've yet to gain any sense of motivation from these characters. I don't know why Durzo does what he does, and that's fine, but shouldn't I WANT to know why he's doing what he's doing? Where's the intrigue, or foreshadowing, or hints of characteristics that will make me want to know more about this uber assassin? 
 With Kylar, at least I'm interested enough to root for him to survive. His relationship with the girl is downright heart-breaking, and it definitely makes me want to know more about him. 
 Anyway, I'm not sure I can keep reading this. If any of you LOVE this or HATE this, please comment. I hope I'm not missing out on an amazing book just because I decided to stop. 
 Side note: I forced myself to finish book 1 of the Mistborn trilogy, and I'm glad I did. I was bored of that book in a somewhat similar manner as this one.
DNF at 120 pages. I feel like I've seen this story before countless times, and better written as well.

The friend who recommended it to me called it the Mary Sue Assassin novel. It totally is, but not necessarily in a way that diminishes the book. A bit cliche and melodramatic, but the author gets some things right, namely his depictions of nobility and street rat life. The villains are still totally mwa-ha-ha evil but his women seem to have sense and intellect. Total trashy plane reading in the best way.

I liked the book, there were some pretty brutal parts to the story but was a ok read. This book is sort of the book series you read when your in between series and you can't decide what to read next. Definetly not for children to read, there are some pretty graphic things in this novel. I really like the world he created and have bought the remaining two books in the series, not something I will probably read again but don't think I have wasted my time in doing so. One interesting this in this novel was how children are treated. I have NEVER read a novel that contained that sort of content, except from possibly George R. Martin. Which is what made me this novel stand out for me. Anyways, not something I recommend other people read, but if you do you won't regret it but your life won't be changed for reading it.
Took me a while to finish, parts felt liked it dragged. The pacing was just too slow for my liking.

My biggest complaint with this book was I was not invested at all in the world. Big things seemed to be happening, but I didn't really care beyond the main character. A bit of humor might have been nice too. Overall I was intrigued by the magic system, I'm a fan of the assassin set-up, and I'm interested to see what will happen in the next books.

I got quite a few chapters into this book--far more than I was really comfortable with--when I found myself sitting there and watching this character doing horrible, immoral stuff with absolute callousness (and I'm not even talking about the assassination gig!). And I pulled away and sat there watching myself watching him, and I thought, "What am doing? Is there any way in which I can justify what I am exposing myself to right now?" And I realized I couldn't. So I left it unfinished. 
 Rating: Extra R. Also, I didn't even get to the worst stuff. Violence, deviant sexual attitudes, yada yada yada. Did I mention I couldn't finish it?

Unfortunately not my thing. I stopped reading at the 9% mark. 
 Street Corner Bookers' Pile Reduction Challenge, #17 (challenger: Teccc)

Whats not to love about this novel? 
 A orphan raised in the gutter as a thief and scavenger, who triumphs over adversity to become an assassins apprentice. And add a touch of magic near the end of the book (that's the essence to the next two) Okay that the simplistic view, and a lot more's happening here than solely that. 
 Azoth who is an orphan who lives in the Warrens of Cenaria City. He has two friends, Jarl and Doll Girl. Then there's Rat who rises to be the leader of the guild and hates Azoth and his friends to the point of murder and buggery. We see his life in the warrens and his struggles to over come that life. He wants become Durzo Blint's apprentice but has to prove himself. - okay any more here adds spoilers. 
 Meanwhile the cities ruler is Duke Gyre and his heir Logan Gyre. Duke Gyre leaves the city to fight invaders leaving his son behind. Add to this a travelling mage Solon Tofusin who seems to be following a prophesy involving Lord Gyre but isn't sure if its the Duke or his son. 
 Once Azoth, now known as Kylar Stern has become Blints apprentice we get to witness some training and grooming that's addictive in the telling. He becomes a blade master and we learn he has a wealth of magical mojo, but the connection to it is broken. However a "kakari" would bridge the connection but is a very powerful weapon and only 7 are in existence. 
 Kylar eventually gets the black kakari which has some unusual qualities including defying death at a dire cost to Kylar. 
 The book then goes into overdrive with a fight between Kylar and Blint and Khalidorans invasion arrives by sea with vurdmeisters (powerful mages) and amongst the chaos Logan Gyre becomes King and hides in a most unusual place. This end part of the book had me on tender hooks the entire time, and I refused to put the book down until I had finished it. 
 Its an old story of waif to assassin but it has a whole new feel here. The Black kakiri and the vurdmeisters magic are a new twist on magic as we normally perceive it in these books. Told in a new and ruthless manner this book is simply addictive. The characters are endearing. And the ending climatic.

reference_books.title: The Queen of the Night
reference_books.review_text: The writing in this was so elegant and I was pleased that this totally lived up to the hype. It stretched a bit long in places but overall, was very compelling.

reference_books.title: What is Not Yours is Not Yours
reference_books.review_text: Beautiful writing but I'm just not a short story person. I did really enjoy a few of them but for the most part, not for me.

reference_books.title: Lab Girl
reference_books.review_text: While I didn't like this, I appreciated it. I thought the structure of the personal chapters alternating with the scientific chapters was really smart. However, the science chapters weren't for me, it's just not where my interests lie. The writing is wonderful and I think this is a book that would be excellent reading for any young woman interested in science.

reference_books.title: Turbo Twenty-Three (Stephanie Plum, #23)
reference_books.review_text: Oh, was this Book 3 or Book 23? I can't tell because the exact same things are still going on in Stephanie's life. I get that the Morelli/Stephanie/Ranger triangle is what the series is built on but enough already - one can only handle reading the same book over and over. Time to stop blowing up cars, time to stop being "torn" between Morelli & Ranger, time to stop catching your bad guys through pure dumb luck - it's time for some new tropes. Or at least, time for me to move on to a new series.

reference_books.title: Pride and Prejudice and Zombies (Pride and Prejudice and Zombies, #1)
reference_books.review_text: Did a grade 6 boy write this? There is no wit or sophistication in the so-called comedy of this book. And don't get me started on beating the servants who "deserved" it. I only finished because First Impressions (a Jane Austen fan podcast) has an episode that is a "smackdown with cutting critical analysis" of the movie & I always read the book before watching the movie. The only good thing about it was snuggle time with my dog.

book_a.title: Tricky Twenty-Two (Stephanie Plum, #22)
book_a.user_review:
Okay, this gravy train has to be stopping soon, right? Each time I read one of these, I think it'll be the last one I read but then it never is. But I think I'm getting to my breaking point, soon. I'll give Evanovich to 25 but if the Stephanie/Morelli/Ranger thing is still going on, I'll be peacing out, for sure. 
 These are just so repetitive now. The formula doesn't change at all, there's been no character development over the 22 books at all, and the overarching storyline (the Morelli/Ranger debate) hasn't moved forward AT ALL. 
 But, it's a light-hearted quick read for when you need to just put your feet up and smile at the (albeit, expected) antics of Stephanie and crew.

sample_reviews.review_text: Here's the thing: This is a light, fun series. Some things are repetitive from book to book but I actually like that and I think it works. This is my go-to series when I want to read something that I can get through quick and will make me smile. I've found the last few have tried too hard to be funny but this one didn't and because of that I found it really funny at parts.

Stephanie Plum has to be one of my all time favorite book heroines, not because she is so special or does amazing things, it's because of the fact that in every book she ends up being so relatable. I am 21 books prior invested into this series, so I can't turn it down now. This book was one of the best installments in a long time. I went into this installment totally blind. Honestly I was a little scared reading this book which is a major feat within itself because this is book number 21. The villain had a way of being evil that was not done before. Plus some of the other side villains were scary as well. I loved every character in this book this time around and some that I knew before I fell in love with even more. Plus there was some progress with the overall storyline (which is a freakin miracle!) I plowed through this installment and for once did not have that horrible feeling of lacking that I have had in the last few installments. I still stand by my 3 star review of the last book but I have to say when Lula threw the dildo at the rapist's head I went from being scared to laughing literally out loud. At that point I knew that this was going to be a 5 star review. Also the ending was fan freakin tastic and I loved every bit of it. I just wish it was a tad bit longer.

Not sure why I'm even reading these books anymore, beyond the fact that I'm on #22 and I've lasted this long. What is this author even doing?? Just end it and put these characters out of their misery, please?!

Loved this one Janet, thank you for the good laughs! I thought I would die laughing when (spoiler alert) Stephanie's Mom chased down, tackled and then pummeled the bad guy!! I love these books because it is always like visiting family, sometimes funny and fun and sometimes not lol. Keep up the good work Janet!!
Slightly funny

Janet Evanovich is one of my favorite authors who has the habit of dishing best-selling novels a few years ago. For reasons best known only to her, she has turned seemingly impressive novels into lacklustre ones, turning hopeful readers into doubters for the past several years. And I'm sure most readers will approach Stephanie Plum's twenty-second outing, Tricky Twenty-Two, with sense of trepidation and lots of scepticism. 
 Contrary to my expectation, Tricky Twenty-Two by Janet Evanovich, the twenty-second instalment in the Stephanie Plum is a fast paced mystery with a lot of sarcastic humor scattered all over. And the characters have really come alive, and the plot is one of the best in the series. Though I love to hate Stephanie Plum, this one is really entertaining, and one of the best in the long-running series.

hmmm... not sure what to say but i think this is the end of the road for me and Stephanie. I love these books because they are quick reads but i'm just not sure if i can read another one of these unless i'm rereading an older one. I think it was Lula that finally did it in for me. I just don't like her in the books at all, at least when she is "helping" Stephanie catch the bad guys.

This was a library book, so I didn't pay for it directly. It was also light fluffy fun, but it could have possibly been cut and pasted from several of her previous books. Same old same old. I enjoyed it, and I'll probably read the next Stephanie Plum book, however, there just isn't anything new here and can't imagine someone paying 15 or even 5 for it. Get it at the library book sale.

You like her. Or you don't. If you do, you read every book in the series. 
 That's the category I'm in. I'm catching up. My third Plum this year. All perfect mindless reads.
Can't believe I just finished my almost 3 Mong Stephanie Plum marathon. Bring on November!!

book_b.title: The Stupidest Angel: A Heartwarming Tale of Christmas Terror (Pine Cove, #3)
book_b.user_review: WHERE DOES HE COME UP WITH THIS STUFF?!?!

sample_reviews.review_text:
I'm in a grinchy, grumbly, bah humbug mood today. Ordering Christmas presents on-line is easier than fighting through the mall, but it is hard enough to get the Christmas spirit in So Cal, so that doesn't help. It feels kind of stupid. 
 As did this book, read for one of my reading groups. At least it wasn't as stupid as the stupid Christmas mysteries we have read in years past. But it felt like reading a TV show. Since I don't watch TV anymore, I guess I shouldn't complain, but the guy humor did not make me laugh. 
 There are zombies in this "Heartwarming Tale of Christmas Terror." They are gross but not as scary as the characters in The Graveyard Book. As far as the other dysfunctional, heavy drinking, stupid characters go, my heart somehow never warmed. 
 Most of the readers in the group found it hilarious. Now I know the difference between Christopher Moore and Michael Moore. I could only recommend this "book" to people who are going to have a monumentally sucky Christmas in the hopes that it might cheer them up a little.

A laugh-out-loud ridiculous Christmas story that showcases a small town during the holiday season. The characters flaws are over the top and each has a distinct delivery of expressing holiday joy. The comedic timing is wonderful and refreshing, as well as, easy to follow. If you enjoy sarcastic humor topped with a harmless zest of spite cooked in a fun story, than you will quickly become a fan of Christopher Moore. 
 This is not a literary work (traditionally speaking). The story is a story told merely for entertainment purposes. It's bathroom humor at best and the reckless and absurd events skate along on the surface. Although I enjoyed the sarcasm and comedic dialogue, I teetered back and forth as to whether it was 'too much.' At times, I felt like I wanted less humor and more story to make my reading and time worth while. And... since this did not happen, it was more like reading one long ridiculous joke with no real punch line or hilarious moral. It left me thinking, 'that was cute and funny, but so what?' I was just as detached to the characters and the town as I was on the first page. 
 Although the style of writing is unique, the common stereotype of small town mentality is not. Every character is a fuddling idiot, even those who are suppose to have degrees, which puts them all in the same category -- a big group of socially stunted and mostly twisted anti-heros. The only person given a hint of brains is the narrator. This is fine, but nothing really changes as a result, no epiphany is ever revealed or even hinted at, which leaves all the ridiculousness, just that, a silly, hilarious story that ends like a bad night out and fizzles.
Only got half way thru. Loved his other books but NOT this one.

This is the first, and last, Christopher Moore book I will ever read. With zombies, talking fruit bats and a cop with his own pot plants it was all too much for me . The talking fruit bat was kinda funny though.
Fun B-movie-type story with goofy characters. Great read.
Not one of Christopher Moore's best stories but still entertaining. A super easy read with a few parts that had me laughing out loud. It is quite the Christmas horror tale.
This makes more sense after reading the lust lizard book. Really enjoyed it!
Good book, but not one of Christopher Moore's best. I listened to this on a drive home from Fairbanks to Anchorage.
not Moore's best but festive, clever & funny. Added bonus he does a fabulous job integrating old characters into a new story. enjoyed it & just in time for Christmas too!!
Not that funny. I had to push myself to finish it. I picked this up because I wanted to see why everyone was talking about this author. If this is his best, I'm not impressed.

reference_books.title: Inbetween (Kissed by Death, #1)
reference_books.review_text: The concept within this book was very interesting. Hell, heaven, and everything that is the in-between. I never would have thought of the possibility of something that makes so much sense. Souls having a waiting room before they are judged is so unique. What happened to Allison/Emma is the work of love and Mauve has every reason to be upset, however, she went above and beyond being upset. She got what she deserved. I can't help but wonder what is going on with Cash? I hope we get his story along with Anaya's! Great book!

reference_books.title: New Moon (Twilight, #2)
reference_books.review_text:
Only reason this one got 3 stars is because I don't like first person narritive. I didn't like that almost every sentence began with You. "You need to leave", "You can feel the fury building", "You leave her alone", "You run to the hospital", "You call, and she answers". This was all within 9 sentences, barely even 2 paragraphs. 
 Other than that - story was pretty decent. 
 Update: Okay so I guess since the title is called Being Jacob, it makes slightly more sense. I still think it should have been told in 3rd person rather than trying to make it seem like you are Jacob.

reference_books.title: Pure (Covenant, #2)
reference_books.review_text:
In the words of Mrs. Armentrout: 
 This was the good kind of insanity--dangerous, but oh-so fun. 
 Merged review: 
 Someone come and put out this fire. This book is hot. I love the relationship building between Alex and Seth. To catch my interest, a book HAS to have characters that you just fall in love with - and Jennifer Armentrout has done that plenty of times. It bothers me to no end that I have to wait oh so long for Deity. Oh what ever will I do without Seth?? :(

reference_books.title: Price of a Kiss (Forbidden Men, #1)

reference_books.title: Easy (Contours of the Heart, #1)

Lucas is amazing and I want to have his babies. The storyline is also amazing. He saves J from something very close to his heart. He couldn't save his mother and that was a heavy weight on his shoulders. Just everything about this book makes me melt. If you didn't read this book yet, what are you doing with yourself??

book_a.title: Silver Shadows (Bloodlines, #5)
book_a.user_review: What a freaking ending!

sample_reviews.review_text: Alchemists are evil. At least in Richelle Mead's universe. The first half of this book is fairly angsty with Andrian off the wagon and Sydney playing Mara Dyer (The Evolution of Mara Dyer) all locked up in her ward and barfing everywhere. Things get a bit Twilighty with the romance in Las Vegas at one point and meanwhile I'm all, "Wait, I forgot we were talking about vampires..where's the blood?!?" But, fun! It was fun reading about the Death Valley adventures as I read this a week after being there myself. Not locked up. Also, I love that Sydney's magic is just there now, no big thing. Crazy witch.

** spoiler alert ** 
 I felt so much reading this! I can't believe it took me so long! During Adrian's period of hopelessness, I was mad at him for giving up but I understood so I couldn't hate him! Ahh there's just so much going on in this book I literally am not looking forward to the next one! It can't end! I love Adrian and Sydney!

Solid 4 stars. *Update* Nevermind, I'm changing this rating to 5 stars because it really was one of the most enjoyable books I've read in a while. 
 I LOVE THIS SERIES. Dare I say I've gone to enjoy it even more than the Vampire Academy series? It's close. I can't say for sure. (I'm also very sad that there is only 1 book left in the series.) I did really enjoy this book though. Sydney is great. Adrian is great. The treatment facility was intriguing (and a tiny nod to the de-gaying camps in the US), and I thought it was well done. This was probably going to be a 5 star rated book, but then the last 1/5th of the book happened and I just can't handle that extreme amount of lovey-dovey stuff. It was just too "cute" for such a severe situation. And then the last 2 pages. Ugh. Cliffhanger to the extreme. I need the next book in my life NOW.

When I first started reading the Bloodlines series I often found myself quite annoyed by Sydney's ridiculous reaction to the Moroi, the Moroi magic and her own magic. As the story progresses we learn why she is the way she is, just what sort of indoctrination she went through as an alchemist and growing up in the Sage household. I was really interested in hearing about what made Sydney turn to Abe. Sydney is very much a different kind of badass then Rose. She's a bit like the Q to Rose's Bond so it was really great to see her use all her alchemist, and then magic, skills. 
 I was a little disappointed we Rose didn't take part in the break out, I understand why, but I really missed my badass Sydney and Rose duo. Don't get me wrong, I love Lissa and Rose but Sydney and Rose have a bit more in common. They're both part of the, sort of, working class and both know a lot about sacrificing personal wishes for the job. Lissa does as well but it's a little different for her. Just as we learn and see how Rose's skills develop VA we see the same for Sydney in Bloodlines. I was also a little disappointed that Rose didn't give Sydney a little thumbs up for making such an entrance to Court at the end, it was a very Rose entrance and I wished we had seen her in the background applauding. I hoping now that Sydney's at Court we'll get to see them team up again. 
 I was really glad we have Sydney actively taking part in her escape. Sydney isn't one to take things lying down so I'm glad we got to see her work on her side of the prison break. Eddie's comment about breaking people out of prison was great and I loved the little throw back reminding us just how much shit that kid was done/been involved in. I knew Emma wasn't as she appeared since she was a little too convincing, I'd love to see more of her she seems clever. Originally I thought they might call on Abe to help break Sydney out so I was little sad they didn't. He's such a character so I'm always up for more Abe. 
 As for after the break out the wedding scene was pretty cute and right in line with Sydney's story, she's got all these plans and ideas for her life and it just never works out the way she thinks it will. I knew as soon as they mention Adrian still having the cuff links that they'd come back into the picture but I was expecting as a wedding ring. Jill's little comments via text were great since I was missing her this book but I knew that was going to get her in trouble as soon as Jill said she'd set something up to help Sydney and Adrian I just knew it was going to get her exposed. Though a little over the top and cliche the chase scene was a fun read. I am however disappointed Sydney pull a Danny and get Hopper to go full on Drogon but hey, maybe next time. 
 One of the things I didn't like was the Nina storyline, it was unnecessary and felt like drama for the sake of drama. I have a feeling it's going to come back and I'm just not looking forward to it. I liked Danielle's storyline, her stuff was great. The woman doesn't always make the best decisions but she sticks to them. She's a great character and could be a very formidable opponent. Go Mama Ivashkov. I feel like this might be unpopular but I totally understood and standby Lissa's decision. She's not just your average Moroi, her decisions have massive political impact and she's being heavily scrutinized. She's trying to make life better for her people and yea that sucks for Sydney but it's what you have to do sometimes as a leader. 
 Loved that we got to see Carly, more Sage sisters! Marcus grabbing for Carly's number was great, smooth Marcus, smooth. It was really nice to see the story from Carly's point of view a little and how's she's dealing with her trauma. I'd be curious if Carly knows what Sydney did to Keith, and if so, what her reaction to it would be. I wasn't a big fan of Zoe but I understood where she was coming from, she's pretty much Sydney when she was younger so I was a little sad we didn't get hear her thoughts after handing Sydney over. Also, Ian, get a hobby that doesn't involve one of the Sage sisters, seriously, it's creepy. 
 I have a few thoughts about the next book, I mean for one thing we now know why it's called the Ruby Circle, but beyond that here's what was kicking around in my head. For one thing I think Sydney will be working with Sonya on the cure. Whether this will happen the next book or just be mentioned as part of her future I'm not sure but Sonya mentioned needing someone with a science background and if Sydney's is stuck there, well why not? As for who took Jill I'm not sure, it sounds a bit like magic was used but I can't understand why witches would want Jill. Unless Ms. T. took Jill to protect her, I could see Ms. T. doing that. I also wonder if it might have been the Alchemists in retaliation, it'd be a really stupid move but who knows. The most obvious is the Moroi rebels which is very likely but I have a feeling they weren't working alone. I really want Ms. T to come to Court I think that would be a hilarious experience, she can bring Trey as her assistant cause he'll have some hilarious reactions to Court. I hope if he goes he runs into Rose. 
 Overall if you like the previous Bloodlines books you'll like this one. It's a little slow in the beginning but really takes off closer to the end. Looking forward to The Ruby Circle!

She got real cool real quick. She was such an annoying character at first now she's awesome and she owns it. I love them two together. Also poor Eddie. His life sucks. How can he keep being all positive when things like this keep happening on his watch?!
I'm very upset at this book and the author right now so I'm probably just not fit to write a review just yet. Later on.

book_b.title: Fallen Too Far (Rosemary Beach, #1; Too Far, #1)
book_b.user_review: Now, first off I would like to put on record that I love Abbi Glines' writing. Big, big fan. I enjoyed reading this book. I love that she has steered into more adult type novels. I was reminded a lot of the Sea Breeze series within this book though. Sadie with Jax. Her life was hard and the rock star background. Then the twist in the story reminded me of Marcus Hardy's. Still, all in all, I loved reading about the ever sexy Rush and the very strong Blaire. I didn't like the ending, but at least Abbi can say that she didn't make that typical happy ending (not within this book anyway). I can only hope that the next book in the series isn't as heartbreaking. Bravo Abbi, you never seem to disappoint.

sample_reviews.review_text: Abbi Glines does it again! This book had me hooked from the moment I picked it up and started reading it. I don't want to give away too much of this story all I am going to say is if you want real emotion and a struggling love story than you need to read this book. It took me about 4 hours to read it, I couldn't put it done. I fell in love with Blaire and her strength to move forward in her life after her mother dies and she loses everything she has. Rush was an ass but slowly he starts to win Blaire over, deep down he is a sweet guy but he has a dark secret, one he doesn't want Blaire to know. Great story looking forward to March 12, 2013 so I can finish Blaire's story in Never too Far. Hurry up March!!
Good story and Rush what can I say? Sexy and cute
My favourite romance novel so far! I couldn't put it down and found myself thinking about the characters weeks later.
It should be illegal to end a book in a way that you MUST get to the next one ASAP if the next one isn't immediately published!! Great read!! We can all use a Rush!

Gawd, I need to stop reading this crap. It's awful. Apparently editors are the only reason why commas exist in books, because none of these smutty indie books have them. Didn't anyone teach grammar in the 80s? 
 Seriously, these books are terrible - like crack, The Kardashians, or cheap potato chips. You know you're going to regret it but you go for it anyways. 
 The story sucked, the guy was horrendous, and not at all appealing, the main character shallow, there was no chemistry, and the sex scenes were boring. And the big scandal/secret? Just dumb. As I said in my review for Collide by Megan Hart, it's really sad when 50 Shades becomes good literature compared to this trash. 
 I honestly do not understand how books like these get a higher rating than Percy Jackson or Unwind. Apparent YA readers tastes are more discerning. And to think that I used to complain about the teenage fan girls that drove up the YA wannabe books! The writing for those are exponentially better than these "new adult" romances. At least this one cost me less than $1. 
 Sorry Abbi Glines - I'm sure you're a nice woman. Just invest in an editor - you can find them on craigslist.

Exact rating: 2.75 
 It felt as if the author was writing to a bunch of 13 year olds. The plot was very unstable and very much immature. The setting wasn't strong and the characters, I don't see any character developments going on at all. 
 Blaire was tough, yes, and I adore her very, very much. However she doesn't seem to be able to make choices very well. What was the gun for anyway? Was it just an extra part to make people love her more? That was not necessary. Rush's character was just, I don't know. There was nothing going on, he didn't interest me as much as Wood did. I thought that Wood would be a much interesting main character instead of Rush. Summarizing his character would be mysterious and nothing and else. He was not that special people would fall for, they just want him for his pretty face. Awful, really. 
 Call me sadistic, but I liked how the book ended. Long live Blaire the Queen!

STORY: 4.5 stars 
 PERFORMANCE: 3.5-4 stars 
 OVERALL: 4 stars 
 STORY: 
 This was my 1st Abbi Glines book. It was a pleasant surprise with its' clever storyline and super hot sex scenes. I struggled with how fast some of the relationships became as deep as they did and how this occurred so quickly; for example, the relationship between the two main characters developed very, very quickly . While I was grateful that there was not an excessive amount of angst and tension-filled drama between them before they finally acknowledged their feelings, the magnitude of some of the feelings felt a bit rushed in my opinion. And though the ending was interesting, unexpected and made sense from a business perspective, I hated the cliffhanger ending! It did make me want to keep reading though... 
 PERFORMANCE: 
 Jennifer Lynn Bronstein is not a bad narrator yet because I have listened to so many other narrators, I kept wishing someone else had been chosen to read this particular series. I could be completely wrong but for me, Bronstein's Southern accent didn't not feel authentic. It was not absolutely atrocious though... What bothers me most about her performance was that she made little or no attempt to alter her voice between characters. I would have appreciated it if she'd at least attempted to speak with a more masculine voice while reading the male dialogue but she did not. Aside from the sex scenes, she did not put a lot of emotion into the dialogue, using the same tone of voice consistently which in my opinion was somewhat needy and whiny. And thought she did put emotion in her voice while recording the sex scenes, occasionally I felt that she put too much effort. Basically, if I hadn't listened to other, better narrators prior to hearing this audiobook, I don't think I would have had as many issues with Ms. Bronstein's performance but since that's not the case, it was hard for me not to compare.
I absolutely loved Blaire and Rush story. Couldn't get enough of those two. Can't wait to read more and see where there story will go.
Pretty much awful :-)

I love Rush and Blaire's story - not that happy with how it ended in this book, but I guess that just means I need to keep reading this series. :) The last third of the book was full of twists, and I don't feel like everything was finished by the end. On to the next one!

reference_books.title: The Walking Dead, Vol. 01: Days Gone Bye
reference_books.review_text:
Bad points of this book: 
 1) It is highly derivative of every other work of zombie fiction ever. 
 2) The art isn't that good. 
 3) The writing ain't anything to write home about. 
 However, it was amusing.

reference_books.title: Ender's Game (Ender's Saga, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
This is my favorite book of all time, and it has endured as such since I was 12. 
 Even people who don't like science fiction can appreciate this story. This book is really a story of children growing up and having to negotiate their relationships with adults and their peers. Told through the ideas of a child who is smart enough to recognize that the adults in his life are using him for their own ends and identify the insecurity of his bullies. He nonetheless responds with the emotional maturity of a child, reacting with the gravity, certainty, and determination that only a child can muster. 
 The speculative fiction aspects like the prediction of the internet and video games are also pretty impressive.

reference_books.title: The Walking Dead, Vol. 04: The Heart's Desire
reference_books.review_text:
Read this to continue the story from the first books. 
 The art and writing haven't improved, however while still highly derivative the execution of the story is getting better and more original.

reference_books.title: Startide Rising (The Uplift Saga, #2)
reference_books.review_text:
This book is about a galactic civilization where only ones species has ever traveled to the stars without being "uplifted," or genetically engineered by another more advanced species. The one that wasn't uplifted were the progenitors, the first race to make it to the stars. The galaxy has an interesting political make up, as each race is valued on who uplifted them and how many races they have uplifted. And then there are the humans, who seem to have reached the stars without being uplifted. And before reaching the galactic civilization they have a uplifted two other races from earth: dolphins and chimpanzees. 
 The basis for this story is very interesting. However, the plot is meandering and hard to follow. There are many threads which are unsatisfactorily tied up at the end. The book is a a good example of great idea which falls short of its potential.

reference_books.title: Pride of Baghdad
reference_books.review_text:
This is a graphic novel rendition of a true story of a pride of lions who escaped from the Baghdad Zoo during the 2003 American Shock and Awe air campaign against Iraq. 
 This is an excellent graphic novel. It is well drawn and well written. I found it very moving. The story is definitely an allegory for the American involvement in the Iraq war. In this capacity, it is somewhat ham fisted. But still this is the best example of political allegory in graphic novel form that I have seen heretofore. 
 The animals in this book are anthropomorphised and could talk. This was kind of weird, and I wasn't expecting it, but it wasn't bad. 
 I read this book because it looked good and my mom gave me a copy for Hanukkah.

book_a.title: Empire (Empire, #1)
book_a.user_review:
This is the story of a group of left wing militants who try to take of the US with high tech weaponry. 
 This book was not very good. Card is a good writer, but this is not his best writing. The characters are static and unbelievable. It reads like a script to an action movie: it is fast paced and there is a lot of action. 
 Also, this book is fair and balanced like fox news. The left wing extreme in this book holds beliefs that only a small, unmobilized percentage of the population of America holds. The right wing extreme of this book is also, some what exaggerated, however they never take any action in the book. The war/uprising is entirely started and perpetrated by left wing militants. Also, the book openly states that the present administration are moderates who are widely supported. I am not going to claim that the present administration are right wing extremists, but they are hardly moderate, and they are also not widely supported, not now and not when this book was written and published. 
 This book makes excellent points about the political dialog in America today: people need to stop characterizing the other side as stupid or crazy just because they don't agree. There has been very little party cooperation lately, and that needs to improve. However, to deny that this book has a right leaning bias would be irresponsible. 
 I read this book because I like Orson Scott Card and thought this book looked interesting. Also, my Mom got it for me for Hanukkah.

sample_reviews.review_text:
This is Card's worst novel by such a large margin that it's almost difficult to describe. It resembles the unpersuasive hyperbole from the political rants on his website far more than it does any of his other novels. He has a blind spot for his political views that is utterly staggering. He is one of my favorite writers, and it seems strange that political writing is such a vastly different skill than fiction, but here he seems singularly untalented and tone deaf. It's like watching Charles Barkley play golf. It seems impossible that someone with that level of body control could look so ungraceful in a semi-athletic endeavor. 
 If you love listening uncritically to right-wing radio, you'll probably enjoy this. If you like good novels, you probably won't.
some interesting ideas in here, but also some glaring holes in the storyline. not recommended for further consumption.
I... I'm stunned at how terrible this book is.

Although not realy a civil war, this is a book about a major uprising of a organization that i hope americans would never allow but. This oranization has many hightech 2-legged wallers (that Rube and Cole call Mechs)these space-like armor-suit, and hover-bikes that have anti-tank weapons. All of these together make up a pretty good fighting force. This is a pretty good book but, I'll admit, it could have been better.
really surprised this was the same orson scott card that brought me ender. this is descolada.

This book was so bad I cried myself to sleep the night I finished it. It was especially painful because I had really enjoyed most of Card's work I had read earlier and found some of it quite brilliant. 
 This book is unimaginative, shallow and stupid and I don't mean the political bias here. You want to be a right wing propagandist - be one! There is surely plenty enough of propaganda on the left to balance you out. But at least be a good one, especially if you are an experienced author, who proven his talent and distinction many times over. 
 Empire's story is weak, the whole premise of it is ridiculous enough and the bad plot only adds to the overall preposterousness of the book, which makes it seem like a piece of a very cheap rightwing propaganda. I wouldn't mind if Bill O'Reilly wrote it but it is so below what I expect from writers such as O. S. Card.

Oh, Orson, how far you have fallen. Instead of the brilliance that was Ender's Game, you now write a Tea Partier's political doomsday fantasy/sub-par action movie. A shame. Hopefully you'll recover from this.

I really didn't like this book, but I think it presented some interesting ideas. I just wish that those ideas were packaged into a better form. Empire reads like a shoot 'em up video game, which leads to a lot of mundane action scenes and not enough character development and discussion of real ideas and perspectives. 
 The story is about a modern civil war that occurs in America. The war is sort of between the political left and the political right, but there's this whole plot about there being a conspiracy deeper than that. The main characters are two military guys who are trying to stop the civil war before it spreads. 
 There's a ton of potential in this book. There is a really strong political polarization in America that's led to not just disagreements but outright demonization. That schism is concerning - at least, to me. The afterword of this book was probably my favorite part because the author, Orson Scott Card, actually discussed that. The rest of the book presents the danger of polarization, but then gets completely wrapped up in a really silly action story. 
 The action itself is boring and, at times, even laughable. There's a scene at the very beginning where the main character literally tears off his clothes and shouts "noo!!!!" when someone dies during a military operation. It's just cliched and over-the-top and is not at all out of place with the rest of the novel. 
 Further, despite a lot of crazy and potentially emotionally jarring incidents, the prose and the emotional reactions of the characters is stunningly flat. A minor spoiler: the president is assassinated early in the book. But there is so little reaction to this huge event that I wasn't sure for quite a while whether it was a simulation or something. 
 Because of the flatness and cliches, reading Empire was a real slog. I wish that Card had been able to spend more time and effort on it, because I think a story like Empire could have a lot of potential as an eye-opening discussion of the dangers of our political polarization. But, as it is, Empire sucks. Don't waste your time on it. At most, read the afterword, then chuck it.

This book is about the events leading to a present day civil war in United States. I think it was originally written as a book in the near future, but now I think of it almost as a alternative past (mostly because the reference the show "24" and it finished up this last year, lol). 
 It was interesting, but for some reason I wasn't able to get into this book as well as his other books. Some of the events that should have had more of an emotional impact on me, just didn't.

In all honesty, I couldn't read this one all the way through. I just thought the whole basis was too perfect and annoying. It is a story of an attack on Washington DC, a setup of the good guy, and (I have to presume) his fight to redeem himself. I did get to the main character's redemption. I couldn't get past how perfect everything was falling into place or how perfect everything else had been pre-arranged. If you liked all of Dan Brown's novels, this might appeal. As I noted elsewhere, I think once you have read one, you don't need to read any more. This has that feel.

book_b.title: The Subtle Knife (His Dark Materials, #2)
book_b.user_review: Really more of a 3.5 stars than a 4. I didn't like it nearly as much as the first book, but it kept me turning the pages.

sample_reviews.review_text: You know, I don't know why everyone is hating on this book. I mean it was no Harry Potter by far... but I still enjoyed it. I am a little confused as to where the plot is going and slightly disappointed I have to read yet another book to figure it out... but I want to know the end! Plus I have always wanted to finish this series since I was little. Overall, an entertaining and quick read.

This book starts off exactly where Northern Lights (or The Golden Compass if you're reading the movie tie-in edition) left off. This time Lyra journeys to our dimension where she meets Will, who has the gift of wielding a very special knife in such a way that he can cut holes into other dimensions. I couldn't help but wonder if this might have been a better place to start this trilogy. If this had been book one instead of two, maybe more people would have related to characters and followed them when they suddenly started dimension-hopping. 
 This book really focuses on Will's introduction and discovery of his place in the grand plan. There are long stretches where we don't see Lyra at all, or she's asleep! Her duplicitous mother is still around and seemingly playing both sides against each other. We're never really sure what her true intentions are. 
 This book is the shortest of the three and so skips along at a good pace until its climatic battle. Probably less action oriented than book one but still engrossing enough to keep you turning those pages into the wee small hours.

Very interesting read. I enjoyed it very much. 
 I think I'm becoming a fan of Pullman's works. 
 Took a while to get adjusted to the new timeline of the story. 
 A bit different from the premise of the first story. Took one thirds of the story to start weaving in the happenings of the first one into this. 
 And darker (is that the correct word? ) than the first one. 
 I think I see the religious implications that everyone was referring to when the movie came out. These are clearer in this one than the first. 
 Still, worth a read. And maybe a re-read for the series. So giving it a four.

Nice continuation from second book,much preferred Lyra in the company of Will than as the lone annoying child in book one. But clearly all the action and tying of loose ends is in book three. 
 More death than I expected and the overhanging idea (loose metaphor to reality) of religion and the church vs God is a little heavy for what would otherwise be a nice adventure story.

It's been a few years since I read The Golden Compass, I book I enjoyed quite a bit. At that time I went into the series with a fresh mind; I hadn't heard of the book, it's author, or any controversy that may have come along with them. After reading the book and forming my own thoughts and opinions on the subjects brought up, I found out that the series was seen as an anti-religion story, something I didn't fully see. It obviously takes shots at certain ideas that come from religion including the church itself, but it never went as far as saying religion was evil itself and, in my mind, took just as much time taking shots at science. I felt the book was attacking power grabbers and dogma however those things manifest themselves. Of course there was always the chance of that point of view changing over the course of three books. Now that I am two books into the series, I still see it as an even attack on the extremes of both religion and science. To say after two books that Pullman is only attacking religion is reading his work looking for those attacks. There are characters who are just as evil in the world of science, who commit deeds just as horrible as those in the church. Criticizing the story as anti-religion is limiting the scope of the novel that Pullman has created and not giving him credit for creating a fully flushed out world. 
 As far as Pullman's writing goes, this is very much a young adult novel. In the years since reading The Golden Compass, I must have become more critical of writing styles, because I found The Subtle Knife much more juvenile in it's language and style then I remember The Golden Compass being. Pullman is not writing anywhere near the depth of character and story that Suzanne Collins did in her Hunger Games novels. This is very much the type of novel I would normally stay away from because it just wasn't written for me, it was clearly written for young teens. 
 Now that I have read two of three books in the series, I'm sure that I will finish it at some point, but I wouldn't recommend these books to adults. This is a young adult fantasy series written for young adults. Many of the themes are more mature then you would expect, but the language and style is much more suitable to younger readers. Pullman has created a wonderful world with fabulous characters, but I would leave these books for the kids.

When I first read this right after it was published, I enjoyed it even more than the first book in the series. I loved how it opened up the world and introduced new elements and characters. Reading it a second time, without the thrill of the new dimensions, it's less impressive. Still a good read, it feels like the middle book in the series it is - more about setting up the final book than creating a satisfying story in its own right.

If I can give this book 20 million stars I would give this book 20 million stars. 
 That's just how good I think it is. 
 The subtle Knife,the second book of the trilogy,expands more into the ideas first introduced in the Golden Compass. I know a lot of people are prejudice about this series because Mr. Pullman's agnostic atheist beliefs were openly expressed in this series.But in my opinion,whether you believe in god or not, read this series without personal biases, and you'll find how imaginative and refreshing this series is. This book explores ideas of parallel universe,magic,religion,war,good and evil all in an exciting adventure of this little girl Lyra in such a well thought manner. The last time I've read a series so additively was Harry Potter,although no one doubts J.K Rowling's imagination and creativity, I find Mr. Pullman's creativity even more dimensional and sophisticated. 
 Not only that,Lyra's adventure was plotted so perfectly. Unlike the Hobbit,where admittedly I got bored at times(sorry Tolkien fans), this series was able to keep you interested through out. Not a moment of dullness. 
 In conclusion, I STRONGLY urge everyone to give this series a try.

I liked most of this book better than the first one, mostly because it focuses on a new character, Will, who I like much better than Lyra. Lyra and Will dash between worlds trying to collect allies and information about Dust. As before, the writing style is uneven--very believable and engaging when speaking about the children's feelings, less so when dealing with adults or dialog. This book would recieve more stars from me if the ending wasn't so sloppy, rushed and needlessly bloody. It felt like Pulman suddenly realized he needed to ramp up the tension and create a cliffhanger, so he basically killed off every character and support he could think of. Violent shocks in a children's book can work very well, but this just felt artificial and calculated.
I think this trilogy can only get dumber from here. It's lie when I started watching Pretty Little Liars though- I just couldn't stop.
this book was offputting you open it up and basically the first sentence is about murder, darkness and depression!

reference_books.title: Mirror Mirror
reference_books.review_text: I have loved everything Maguire has written up until this point. Gosh... this book was so dull, so disjointed... I almost didn't finish it (and I finish every book I start!) Just an absolutely worthless read.
The only thing gripping about this novel was the medical side of it. Otherwise it was a bore and a drag.

reference_books.title: Ring (Ring, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
This was an odd book. The translation made the writing pretty clunky, so it was sort of difficult to get completely submerged into at first. 
 The story is interesting and different from the movie, so it kept me wondering what was going to happen next. 
 It's an interesting glimpse into a different culture as well. The husband and main character is really distant from his family who are barely mentioned in the book at all, but that seems to be slightly acceptable and typical even. 
 The character development is greatly lacking and there are a few details that are just innocuous and bizarre.

reference_books.title: Jaws
reference_books.review_text:
This book sort of redeemed itself a bit at the last minute. I really disliked the way marriage was portrayed throughout the book. It seemed as if every single couple in the book was dissatisfied in some way with their relationship and was seeking or wishing for a relationship with someone else. 
 However, one of the main characters did end up figuring out how valuable her marriage was to her within the last few chapter of the book, but she did continue to treat her husband like crap. She belittled him, gave him the silent treatment, and was painfully passive aggressive. 
 As for the main plot- which I guess is the shark...??? The action was good- it was creepy and ominous, but the scenes with the actual shark in them were few and far between. The book was more of a drama between all of the characters in the town and how they were going to recover from the economic toll the shark attacks had on the town as a whole. 
 Not one of my favorite reads, but decent enough.

reference_books.title: Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter
reference_books.review_text: So boring!! Had a rough time finishing this one.

book_a.title: Enchantment
book_a.user_review:
I had read several negative comments before reading this book, and I was all set to disagree with all of them, but wound up, instead, agreeing with nearly every single one. 
 The story starts off sweet and fun enough. But by the time the Princess is woken up, things take a turn for the weird and disjointed. At a few points I felt like I had picked up one of those super cheezy romance novels- completely unrealistic sex scene included (gross). 
 The religious aspect of the book was really random as well. She's Christian, he's a Jew, but neither one is REALLY practicing their faith- it's pretty much a cultural thing. And, between all the witchcraft and unanswered questions on God's existence, I didn't see the reason why the author should of bothered to include any Christian or Jewish aspect into the plot at all. 
 It's one thing to have an unbelievable plot, but when you can't believe in the characters either- well, then you've got a recipe for a bad book on your hands.

sample_reviews.review_text: I loved this new spin on Sleeping Beauty. I want some of it to be true!

This book is best described as "interesting." It was definitely a page turner, but not so much for the characters and storytelling as for Card's unique take on history, fairy tales and the melding of modern and ancient worlds. I also enjoyed learning a little about Slavic history and legend that I never knew before. 
 Part history, part legend, part fantasy, minus truly compelling characters and plot. Worth reading, especially if you like Card. Warning: it takes a little while for the book to become interesting.

This book I pondered for many days after reading it. There were some things I didn't like about it that I thought the author could have left out (if you've read it you understand what I mean) but overall I liked it. It was original and interesting.

I enjoyed this book well enough, it had good characters and decent world building. The more I read of Orson Scott Card the more I see his tendency to narrate the story and simply deliver in plain text what the reader needs to know about the history. I am beginning to realize that I prefer writers who leave some things to the readers imagination, and allow the history and story to unfold throughout the book.

It was ok. I found it entertaining merely because it was so different from what I normally would choose to read. I grabbed it out of desperation and it being the only thing I had on hand at the time. 
 The romantic relationship was tiring in it. Frustrating and to me not so believable. I didn't know enough Russian history to make that part interesting. The main character was without clothes a lot. Couldn't figure out why the author wanted him that way so much. Mostly pointless I thought. I don't get Mr. Card's humor the way he probably intends, so it wasn't as funny to me.
Retelling of Sleeping Beauty.
It had a bit of a slow start and there were parts where I felt it dragged on unnecessarily but I did enjoy the expansion of and twist on the Sleeping Beauty story.

Ancient tales twisted with romance creates a great story in Enchantment. Card writes romance like no one else can - making true love appear before every reader's eyes. And the best part is that his plot doesn't suffer for the love theme.

This was a very mediocre book. There were times when I thought it was going to be really good, but that never actually materialized. Perhaps Card was looking for a very simply story style since it's a retelling of a fairy tale. But either way, he ended up with a fairly weak plot that involved some leaps of faith to maintain any sort of believability (which is saying something in a fantasy novel!). It was certainly an interesting take on Sleeping Beauty - but that didn't really add enough to make it a winner.

I picked up this book because I enjoy modern retellings of fairy tales. The story managed to hold my interest about halfway through. However, it seemed to shift into a completely different book later on, when the characters became talking heads and seemed to be lecturing the reader instead of telling a story. I'm not even sure what the point of the lecture was--that Jewish people had the only true magic? I couldn't make it out. Regardless, I was very disappointed.

book_b.title: Dark Places
book_b.user_review:
I really enjoyed this one! It wasn't quite as good as Gone Girl- but it kept me going, kept me on the edge for the most part. 
 *** SPOILER WARNING *** 
 The only thing I thought was super annoying was the fact that Diondra was actually able to carry her baby all the way to term and that she was born relatively healthy (at least physically) from the descriptions in the book. I'm sorry, but after all the alcohol and drugs that girl consumed during pregnancy- there is no way that baby would be okay! 
 Aside from that contrived bit of nonsense... it was a gripping read!

sample_reviews.review_text: I liked this book from the start. It is a very dark and mysterious book. There was something about the main character Libby that I loved reading- I think it was her no nonsense/sarcastic attitude. I enjoyed reading the books from the various perspectives of Libby, her brother Ben, her mom Patty, etc. I also liked how it went back and forth in time. It made things interesting. It kept my interest also because the entire book is talking about the night Libby's family was murdered except she and Ben and who did it and what the town thought, etc. It kept me guessing. It was a bit weird all the talk of devil worshipping and drug use - a little scary. I also didn't love how quickly the ending wrapped up- I always feel like books I read lately end too abruptly or easily. Maybe it's just me.... Overall good and interesting book and I'm excited to see the movie.
It's hard when there is not one character to remotely like. Dark, violent.

What a dark but delightful read. I picked up this book on vacation, thinking it was a new release, and then realizing this was published before the oh so popular, Gone Girl. Really had no expectations when I opened the cover. The story was engaging - dark, yes - and exciting to go back and forth between now and 1985 as the story unfolded from three perspectives. The ending was good...not fantastic...but good and it wrapped it all up with no loose ends. Definitely worth the read!

I'm working Gillian Flynn in reverse - first Gone Girl, sensational bestelling movie-adapted third novel; then Dark Places, second coming of a newly-started author, apparently living up to the expectation of her debut, Sharp Objects - which I'm planning on reading ASAP, because few authors get me like Flynn can. 
 I think it's all about the characters and points of view, to be honest. Flynn has the best kind of writing style - one that doesn't pressure the reader, doesn't make the narrator a looming presence impossible to ignore. She also writes about horrible people in a sympathetic way, but without putting them on a pedestal. I love this. There's way to many authors (and readers, sic!) excusing and/or romantizing terrible behaviours just because of some sappy backstories. Which, nope. I'm sorry for your loss, but they don't excuse you being an abusive person, or a murder, or ehi! even an ordinary bastard. 
 Gillian Flynn doens't make heroes out of ordinary bastards. She leads you into their minds and makes you understand what made them the monsters they are, but she never forgets to showcase them for what they are - monsters. Gone Girl is a great example of what I mean: you can't escape the twisted magic of that book, the one that makes you symphatize with both Nick and Amy. But never once the book stops from showing you how toxic and sick and 100% NOT-TO-DO their love is. 
 It works the same in Dark Places. You've got the main girl, Libby Day, only survivor of domestic massacre. When she was seven, her older brother Ben murdered their mother and two sisters, then was condamed to life sentence thanks to Libby's shaky witnessing. Grown-up Libby is a mean, selfish, weak young woman with not will to either live or die, who gets roped back in the murderous mess that was her past by young, lost causes obsessed Lyle and his little club of Murders Solvers. 
 Libby is a bad person, and her family is made out of some hugely messed-up persons - and I loved each one of them. I loved twisted, scared Ben and his surrander to a mean world. I loved mama Patty and her desperate love for her children. I loved Libby, messy, mean Libby, a survivor with no sugar coating her emotional scars. It was hard to take in all their emotions, because Flynn is a merciless writer, when it comes to emotions. But that's her charm; and the raw, intense, yet never over-the-top way she describes her characters' journies leads the reader in some of the most compelling, twisted and terryfing plots I've ever read, with just the right amount of tension and details to never make it too much.

Just have to fair, because she wrote this book before Gone Girl, Gone Girl was much better in style and writing, sometimes I need to stop a bit before I can continue to read. Good thriller, but the plot and the story background was not my cup of tea (don't want to include spoiler here). Can't wait to see the movie adaptation to see if I like it better or not.

Very twisty. Gillian Flynn is a masterful writer, she made me care about a character I didn't like and felt absolutely no personal connection to. The twists she made along the way were fascinating and the ending was unexpected. There were a few spots that didn't sit right with me just a tiny bit, but not enough to dislike the book. She more than made up for it. Next, Sharp Objects.

Definitely 3.5 stars. I like Flynns books, but at the same time they are so creepy and intense. Not always an easy book to just pick up and read in a day. I do love how you never truly know the truth until she's ready to reveal it though!
I did not enjoy this nearly as much as Gone Girl. It was too gruesome for my taste and somewhat of a predictable mystery. This one was just "meh" for me...

No. Just...no. 
 It's been months since this series ended. But every time I pass by the bookstore and see this book sitting on the shelf, I silently fume inside. Honestly, I want nothing more than this book to just not exist. It's worse than Fallen and more unlikable than Shatter Me. At least those books were a let-down from the very beginning. This series had so much potential to be great, and it just went down the drain in this last book. Think Allegiant. 
 The Unbecoming of Mara Dyer was great, albeit a little flawed. There were some elements in that book that made it your typical paranormal YA story, but there were other elements that made me like it enough to be attached to it. The Evolution of Mara Dyer was--and still is--one of the best books and one of the best sequels I've ever read. It started out strong, built up into such a complex and goosebump-inducing plot, and ended with so much potential. It ended with Noah's fate in question and with Mara's morals in question. Filled with so much hate and vengeance, Mara had the potential to become the villain that the past two books were predicting her to become. 
 Then what did this book do? Throw it all away. What did it do to Jude's character? Throw that away, too. And the plot and pacing was terrible. Wait...what plot? Ha! It was as if the author said, "Screw it, let's just write anything and then slap a price tag on it. The readers will buy it anyway!" 
 I have so much anger for this book because it had the potential to be the best darn conclusion that YA paranormal books have ever seen, but it fell short in the end. More than short. Like, it didn't even reach my bracket of standards. Reading this was like reading a poorly-constructed draft of another story. 
 Literally, nothing made sense in this book, and I wouldn't recommend anyone to buy it. Save yourself the heartbreak and the frustration.

So I finished the books.... 
 This is going to be very short. Some of you may have read my review to the first book. This is an extension to that. 
 The second book was good, not as good as the first but still enjoyable. 
 The twists and turns did catch me off guard, but some you could just see coming and I was not that impressed. 
 I did not enjoy the ending of the third book. The cliffhanger in the second book did not leave me as distressed as I usually would be, since I knew I had the last book. 
 I felt as though the series just ended without giving any explanation into what happened next. In some cases it is okay. For example, the last book in the Breathing Series did have somewhat of an abrupt ending, but we knew that everything would be okay. With this book that did not happen. We were told bad things would happen, but that was never explored. 
 Overall, I did enjoy the story and the writing was very good. However, I feel as though the story was unfinished, therefore, making my experience less enjoyable. I would recommend these books, as I did like the series as a whole. 
 3.5/5 stars for the series as a whole.
What a great way to end a series. I'm going to miss Mara but I'll be missing Noah a lot more.
