This is my sixth Scott Turow book but my first in a while. I had a few Turow books on my bookshelf when I began to have problems visually tracking the lines in printed books and ultimately switch to audible books. So this is my first Turow audible. 
 I like Scott Turow a lot and I'm not going to spend much time retelling the story here. He is not a mystery writer with a lot of action or violence or gun powder. His stories are mostly dialogs and interior conversations. This book has a father and son aspect and his ability to write about long time relationships is superb. His ability to write about what people are thinking and feeling and experiencing is excellent. He can draw complex characters in a most understandable way. 
 This book has one of those traditional mystery aspects. It's not quite a whodunit. But it is a how did the woman die? The courtroom scenes are pretty extensive. You pretty much get to know what everybody in a courtroom is thinking. All very well done.
Agonizingly slow read - was not able to capture my attention at all. Therefore, had to chock it up as a loss. Did not finish, sorry to say.

I used to love Turow's legal thrillers -- but either my taste has changed or Turow's writing has. I just got bored. Of course, it doesn't help that I've got seven or eight other books sitting on the bedside table and I'm thinking about the trip I'm about to leave on... 
 Did Turow's characters spend so much time in his earlier books staring into their navels and thinking about themselves? The lead character here gets all of his chapters written in the first person, and he has an incredibly dull inner monologue running. Me, me, me. 
 The chapters centering on other characters are written in the third person, and they seem to be better. Still to much moaning and bitching about their lives -- everyone here is pretty dysfunctional -- but there seems to be a bit more action. 
 I remember Turow as writing -- essentially -- the courtroom attorney's version of a police procedural. Instead of casting some overweight and emotionally broken cop and watching how he thinks and obsesses about solving some puzzling crime, you'd have an assistant DA doing the work. 
 The chapters that focus on that part of the story were the best part, and the only reason it kept two stars. But I couldn't skip the boring parts, or I'd spend too much time backtracking to fill in the missing pieces. 
 So I ended it. Too bad; I used to have great memories of Turow's novels, and now I wonder if I re-read them whether I'd re-like 'em.

Innocent is not the first Turow book you should read. I know. I have read all his novels about "Kindle County." The first book has to be "Presumed Innocent" since that book concerns Rusty Sabich and many of the same characters 20 years earlier. 
 Turow is a brilliant writer whose style is a joy to experience. Though this book is not about happy topics -It is about affairs of the heart. It is about how the police and the prosecutors think about crime and their jobs. It is about the dark side of growing older and less optimistic about the way life works out. 
 The story is played out in court and around lawyers in a way that shows how intimately Turow understands all he has assembled. And, I guess, I agree with some other reviewers that it reflects on Turow's own aging process and what he has gleaned from it.
Rusty returns for more extra marital fun and games, trial for murder, this time of his wife--but even more secrets. Still the book isn't quite the page turner of its predecessor.

reference_books.title: Burn for Me (Hidden Legacy, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
I love Ilona Andrews. That said, at first I wasn't too sure about this book as I thought it was slow to get going. And it finished with a sequel set up which is not one of my favourite devices, as even in series I prefer each book to be completely stand alone. But with those two provisos I ripped through this book and was sorry it was over. I nearly went back and read all their previous books just so I didn't have to say goodbye. 
 It's a great story of young woman who is the stalwart of her family. They are just getting it together after tragedy and she made one wrong decision by taking out a mortgage to get them through. That decision comes back to haunt her when the mortgagor takes advantage to send her and her family Private Investigation company on a suicide mission to bring in a renegade Prime magic user. 
 In the process she comes up against, and then partners with, (sometimes hard to tell the difference in practice), another Prime magic user. Keeping the upper hand when she is insanely attracted to him and he knows it, keeps her on her toes and him plotting. 
 Clever, funny, imaginative and suspenseful. Enjoy.

reference_books.title: The Enemy (Jack Reacher, #8)
reference_books.review_text:
Reacher finds himself posted back to the US from an important operation in South America and in charge of the MPs on base. He gets dragged out, early on New Year's morning, to a natural death of a two star general. The officer has apparently died while in bed with a prostitute. All would be well but something important goes missing... At the same time, he realises there are a whole group of his colleagues who have mysteriously been reposted over the world. What is going on and is everything connected? Plus his mother becomes seriously unwell and he has to juggle all the balls. 
 This is my second Reacher book. I wasn't that impressed with the first one I read but, to my surprise, I loved this one. I could hardly put it down. This book has one of the best discussions of death I have ever seen in a murder mystery. It also has an excellent explication of who is Reacher and how did he develop into the character he is? The characterisations are very well done. 
 I also enjoyed the time setting which was at the fall of the Berlin wall. There appeared to be no anachronisms and Child captured the times well as far as I remember them. 
 A good mystery, well written with good timing and suspense. Enjoy.

reference_books.title: Violets Are Blue (Alex Cross, #7)
reference_books.review_text:
Alex Cross is being stalked by the Mastermind who has killed his partner and is threatening him and his family. At the same time, he has been drawn into a serial murder case where bodies are appearing across the country, apparently killed and drained by vampires or maybe a tiger. Alex is dragged into the case almost against his will as he is reviewing his commitment to his family versus his committment to his work. 
 This is only the second James Patterson that I have read. I was not impressed with the first and read this one as it was on my book club list and they are so popular I was sure the problem must have been me the first time around. I'm still not impressed. 
 The writing is poor, the story line is hackneyed and makes little sense. The outcomes are telegraphed. I couldn't wait for the end so that I could put it down. I'm very disappointed.

reference_books.title: Broken (Will Trent, #4)
reference_books.review_text:
This is the fourth in the Will Trent series. I've not read most of the preceding books. I found this an interesting mixture. Is this a murder mystery or is it the ongoing story of Sara - Jeffery - Lena with Will being thrown in? 
 Sara goes back to Grant County reluctantly. It is where she grew up, fell in love, was happily married to the police chief and then traumatically widowed. Lena, the detective she blames for her husband's death is still there. It seems like she has been there 5 minutes when she is called to the police station to help with a prisoner and finds him dead in the cells. To top it off the prisoner has been accused of murder but Sara knew him and is sure he could not have committed the type of murder described. She seeks outside assistance and Will Trent arrives to investigate. 
 He finds himself highly unpopular as he investigates both the local cops and the murder of a young girl. Sara finds herself drawn in to assist. We find that almost everyone involved is Broken in some way. 
 3.5 stars Enjoyable

reference_books.title: Sweep in Peace (Innkeeper Chronicles, #2)
reference_books.review_text:
Sweep in Peace is the second in this series about Dina the Innkeeper. Dina is offered a peace conference at the Inn. The chances of this turning out well are very poor but the Inn desperately needs guests. With three different races who have been warring for generations, the Galactic Arbitrators and a temperamental chef all challenging Dina's capacity for hospitality, the future of Gertrude Hunt Inn could be on the line. 
 The book was written on line as a serial before being taken away for tidying up and publishing. Fans will enjoy it and it has the added bonus of a well done tie in to a previous series. It's also something of a drawback though though as, to me, this book, felt like a way station in two ongoing story lines. 
 I enjoyed it, and I'll definitely read the next, but I'm not sure that this is a starter book.

book_a.title: Sabriel (Abhorsen,  #1)
book_a.user_review:
Sabriel, at eighteen, is from a long line of Abhorsens, who have power over the Dead. Sabriel's father is missing and she must leave the safety of her school with the little Charter Magic she knows, and brave the dangers of Free Magic and the chaos of the Old Kingdom, to save him. 
 This has a strong flavor of WWI and the fantasy world is well imagined and beautifully detailed. The action is also well done. The characters are not particularly sophisticated but this is the first book in a trilogy and they may be more fleshed out as the story continues. 
 I enjoyed it and will read the second book.

sample_reviews.review_text:
I really liked this book, almost one star more but>>> 
 The only real issue I had was that it had a slow start for me to get interested enough and keep reading.. 
 It had a lot of action which was brilliantly described and sucked you in after biting through, but im a big fantasy & romance lover and it didnt quite do it for me in the Romance field.. 
 However, the story & action made up for that fact in the end and even though I was really looking forward to more character development from both leads and was kind of let down with an unsatisfying feeling when I had finished... 
 So, I gave in and actually started reading Book No. 2, Lirael.. 
 And Even though I foolishly thought It was about a completely different perona and side of the story, I was pleasantly surprised it finally gave me the ending to Sabriel I was longing for and more ;)

Many fantasy stories fall into 2 categories; either they are a twist on The Lord of the Rings (like Eragon or Robert Jordan's Wheel of Time series), or they are part of today's popular paranormal romance genre. This was a refreshingly original fantasy story featuring a strong girl protagonist. Sabriel is the daughter of the currently reigning Abhorsen, which gives her the legacy responsibility of making sure that the Dead, really stay dead. She is armed with necromancy and a set of magical bells with different attributes to help control the Dead. Life seems pretty normal, or at least normal for someone who lives in a magical world, until her father the Abhorsen goes missing and the likely culprit is Kerrigor, a powerful member of the Dead who not only won't stay undead, but is wreaking havoc in the world of the living. What makes this an easy series to recommend is the strong character of Sabriel, a fiesty and resourceful young woman, and her sidekick Moggett, a magical creature who has the physical body, as well as the quirky personality traits, of a cat. 
 One of the best parts of this audiobook is the narration by Tim Curry of Rocky Horror fame. He does a fantastic job with the various voices, and really does an over the top performance for some of the more challenging aspects, like Moggett throwing up a hairball. Fun read!

I'm hesitant to rate this one, and I may have to revisit it in print because while I'm usually fine with audiobooks, something either about the density of Nix's prose or the narrator's style made me feel like I was gliding over a lot of passages. I really enjoyed the story, though and I want to read more. Maybe in print next time, though.

Wish I had read this when I was younger. You have no idea how much I want to kick myself that I didn't. Especially because I did love all of Garth Nix's other series when I was younger. 
 But then again, who am I kidding, this is an excellent book, it's just not quite as in depth as I wanted it to be. 
 Sabriel is part of the Abhorsen line, the family that controls the dead. Her father brought her from the Archensljtire. 
 Then she rescues a boy from the mast of a wood. They inevitably fall in love within a few days, which always bothers me, but I guess this is a fantasy.... 
 Otherwise it was a lovely fantasy.

I recently reread it. I had forgotten/never noticed how feminist it. It's a pretty solid YA book with cool world building and a strong female main character. It has several other competent female background characters as well. I'd recommend it to girls who like adventure and boys whose parents raised them right(who also like adventure).

This was extraordinarily boring. 3 stars is being generous, but there was a good story in there somewhere. I thought Tim curry would have been an narrator. Although I question the choice of having a male narrator for a story about a young woman. 
 With the subject matter, there should have been fear and thrills. But I was bored. The "love story " was nonexistent. No romance or teasing. No chemistry 
 Since many reviews have said the series gets better, I may try reading the next one

** spoiler alert ** 
 This book is amazing..so amazing that I read both of the sequels before writing any reviews. I'm now experiencing a sad state of withdrawal since I've reached the end for these characters. 
 But Sabriel is only the beginning. Nix has created a world split in two by a wall. To the North is the Old Kingdom, where the dead don't stay dead and magic forces prevent technological based equipment from functioning. Ancelstierre, the southern kingdom, is a more modern country with automobiles, electric power, airplanes, telephones - like the early to mid twentieth century. I don't remember any cell phones or computers, so not entirely modern. 
 Sabriel is the daughter of Abhorsen. She has spent most of her life at a boarding school in Ancelstierre but is now graduating and at a crossroads. Should she continue her studies with her friends in Ancelstierre? Or should she return to the old kingdom to join her father (the Abhorson) in his efforts to help the dead to permanent rest? When she discovers that her father has died, she realizes she has no choice - she must return to the old kingdom to find him. For as the new Abhorsen, she has the magic and the tools to travel through the gates of death. She only hopes that her father has not traveled beyond her ability to find him. She also must beware of the necromancers who also use magic to travel in death; they are working to bring the dead back to the world of the living. 
 Early on, Sabriel is very much alone. While I think this highlights her resourcefulness and strength of character, it was harder for me to relate. I became more engrossed when she met her traveling companions later in the story. My personal preference is for stories with a lot of dialogue and interaction between characters; when I was younger, I used to skip to the descriptions for the conversations. 
 I thought the idea of a wall splitting the two kingdoms, with a modern military guard on one side, was very interesting. It reminded me of the Demilitarized Zone splitting North Korea and South Korea. That's probably because I've been to the DMZ and so have firm impressions in my mind of that situation. South Korea is definitely more technologically advanced than North Korea, but I'm pretty sure that no magic forces act in North Korea. 
 Maybe it's a common idea for magic to cause technology to malfunction; I haven't read very many books that combine modern technology with magic. The Dresden file books by Jim Butcher use this same idea. 
 Although this book made me want to read more right away, it was only because I became absorbed in the characters. The story had a satisfying ending and would work well as a stand alone novel.

I dont think this was the story for me. It was interesting mixing medieval with current but I found some things confusing. I still didn't quite understand charter marks or charter mages but I'm going to give book 2 a shot.
I take awhile to get into fantasy but once I'm there, I'm there. Unfortunately, I never get 'there' and by the time the book is finished I don't want to go back.
Hated hated hated this. It moved so slowly I couldn't hardly drag myself through it. And I had already bought the second and the third in the series, which well never be read.

book_b.title: Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter
book_b.user_review: I read 32% of this book and then put it down. It is meant to be humorous. I definitely see the humour in the contrast between Abe and vampires. I could even see the cleverness and the depth of research. It just did not work for me. I struggled to get that far and did not get a skerrick of connection so I gave up. Hunour is so subjective.

sample_reviews.review_text:
This doesn't hold my attention. The writing style is what i don't like. I suppose it had to be that way because it is a journey, but it was off putting. But i will watch the movie,because i am curious what they managed to make out of this book. 
 ** 
 I admit i hardly finished the book by skipping a lot of pages which i usualy never do to a book.. 
 so it was a bad and boring experience for me. 
 Thx god it is over.
Interesting concept. Book is peppered with Lincoln quotes. Whole vampire motif seems a bit forced though, doesn't really add up at times.
Well written, but weird.
More like 3.5 - loved the first 3/4 of the book and then it seemed to have a different feel towards the end. It does really make it plausible to believe in vampires though!

I much prefer this one to Pride and Prejudice and Zombies (which, bizarrely suffered from not enough zombies). It's a clever, if silly, take on the civil war done in a pseudo historical fashion with narrative intersperced with Lincoln's lost journal. A triffle don't get me wrong, but it's a truly enjoyable read.

I thoroughly enjoyed this book. I don't really care if he got some of the history wrong (I hear history buffs have that complaint), it was a fun read that got me more interested in the actual history than probably anything else would. I don't care for certain vampire stories (the romance ones), but this, I can enjoy. I'm not into violence, though, so I had to skim past a few gruesome paragraphs, but overall it wasn't too bad. I know I wouldn't want to see the movie, though.
It started off strong, but the longer he stayed with Abe's historical life the more tortured the idea became.

This was a fun book to read. I learned alot about the history of Abraham Lincoln along with the fun twist of the vampire hunter. Definitely worth picking up. 
 Enjoy!!!!!!!
Very interesting and thought provoking. It's a pleasure to read something like nothing I've ever read.
Better than i thought it would be. Fun, it even included a bit of emotional weight here and there. Not played for camp (which was what I expected) but rather presented as alternative history.

reference_books.title: Isla and the Happily Ever After (Anna and the French Kiss, #3)
Angelfall (Penryn & the End of Days, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
4.5 stars 
 Good story and writing. Loved Penryn's character. Interesting dark elements. Predictable romance, though.

reference_books.title: Em and The Big Hoom
reference_books.review_text:
"A well-told lie can heal. Otherwise, what's fiction?" 
 This was short, sweet and sad. 
 It was the perfect book to read after 'The Gene'.

reference_books.title: A Court of Wings and Ruin (A Court of Thorns and Roses, #3)
reference_books.review_text:
It may not have delivered all its promise, but this is still a good book. I savored it. I found it, especially the second part of it, quite similar to Archangel series by Nalini Singh though this is like an epic fantasy while the latter is an urban fantasy and more inclined toward romance. 
 The end is sweet and not bittersweet and disappoints a little, after raising the expectation high with all the twists and the nested twists. I'm not sure why there are more books in the series.

reference_books.title: The God of Small Things
reference_books.review_text: It's a tragic, old and well-known story told in a disjoint way. A nostalgic way. You feel disconnected to the characters at times, and the story seems fractured. But not so much that you abandon it. It holds its shape and leaves you with its imprint.

book_a.title: Seventh Grave and No Body (Charley Davidson, #7)
book_a.user_review:
3.5/5 
 Better than the last book in the series, but not all that great. I wish it were more about Charley's P.I. stuff. This one didn't have much story in that angle. She seems to be just running around to different places all the time, and the hellhounds may be terrifying, but they're incredibly annoying - just showing up everywhere. And what's with the 'Twelve' business. Hope the author clarifies those prophecies soon.

sample_reviews.review_text: I can never get enough of Charley Davidson. Darynda Jones has given her another knock out performance. I can't wait for the next round.
Love these books!

Wow, this is by far the best one yet in this series! So much happens, but I'm not one to give any spoilers. Let's just say that this book moves the storyline along in a BIG way. Hellhounds, murders, missing corpses, a missing father, and BEEP (you will understand when you read it). But there is no rest for the saviour of humanity right? I'm exhausted from just reading all that went on in this book. Secrets, lies, and hellhounds make everything that much more tense. We get a lot of answers, but those answers just create more questions. How is this all going to play out? Will there be a final battle? Is everyone really on Dutch's side? And Reyes, well, he seems to be just as insecure as the rest of us when it comes to Charley. Is was nice to see this side of him. Absolutely one of my favorites in this series, can't wait for the next one. 
 P.S. If you are reading the print addition, the bonus chapter is SOOO worth the price of the hardback!!! (And I hate the word affianced now....lol)
NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!!!!! So awesome! Where the fudgicles is book 8. *devastated by not having the next book in my hands right now*
Wow, this book was amazing!!!! I read it in one day!
Awesome as previous books...

I'm giving this a two even though it's clearly a four star read. I'm just still super pissed at the stereotype that was put in the book. Just because someone is black doesn't mean every black person comes from the hood. And to have to read that crap clearly threw me for a loop, but alas even good authors can be ignorant.

"I caused more trouble than gonorrhoea." 
 If you liked all the previous Charley Davidson books, then you will like this too, especially when you are a fan of the series and can't wait to gobble up whatever Charley Davidson throws in your way. 
 Seventh Grave and No Body pretty much follows the same formulaic structure its previous instalments had - Charley receiving a new case from her self-owned PI company and landing herself into trouble, discovering more about her Myserious Grim Reaper Identity, flirting with the son of Satan and delivering her snarky and quirky lines while at it. 
 Seventh Grave isn't revolutionary or anything. While there is a respectable amount of plot progression mashed in the chaos of Charley's life, it kinda just blends in with the previous six books, bringing nothing new to the table. I, however, appreciate how things took a sinister turn towards the end of the book, promising a darker and more dangerous sequel. A short chapter of Reyes' POV at the end also proved to be a refreshing touch from Charley's usual nonchalance. 
 "Since meeting me, his life had been turned upside down. I was like a small but devastating plague upon humanity. It was weird."

3.5 stars. Good (but not great) installment. I really wanted to like this one more especially given the surprise in the last book. The plot lacked cohesion and I found myself losing interest in the middle. Reyes was wonderful as well as the minor characters. Charley was tough for me to stomach in this book. I usually like her flighty goofiness, but she continually put herself and the Beep in danger for stupid reasons. She left Reyes out of the loop several times for NO REASON. It was frustrating. Still looking forward to the next installment though.

About half way through, this needed to split into a couple books. Too much going on, none of it well served. I do enjoy the mystery parts of these books, her talking to the dead, etc. But when it gets to the mythology part, it is too frenetic. Then there is the whole - the hottest guy in the whole world (and some others) wants little ole plain me. A plot device, I have never liked.

book_b.title: The BFG
book_b.user_review:
The BFG is the most scrumdiddlyumptious story ritten for nice little chiddlers, left or right? 
 More right. 
 I is wishing I red the book when I is little human bean like Sophie.

sample_reviews.review_text: Probably my favorite book by Dahl.

While my children absolutely loved this book, I hated it. The language the giant uses was annoying and I just couldn't get into this book at all. It seems that the very things I did not like about this book, were the very things my children adored...I grew up :(

I picked up this book as a light read in between a lot of heavy books I was trying to finish. This was the second Dahl book that I wasn't a huge fan of. It was cute in its way, but I found the humor a bit repetitious. The way the BFG talked, sort of mashed up and confused with his vocabulary, was cute at first, but the longer the story went the more this running gag just irritated me. I was also a little put off by the bathroom humor in it, which I've grown beyond at this point in my life.

wow... terjemahannya... sangat wow!!! Salut sama penerjemahnya *kasih jempol* 
 Suatu malam, ketika mengintip dari balik jendela kamarnya, Sophie kecil yang yatim piatu menemukan dirinya menyaksikan pemandangan yang tidak biasa: seorang raksasa sedang meniupkan terompet ke kamar tidur anak-anak. 
 Celakanya, raksasa itu melihat Sophie dan menculik gadis kecil itu, dan membawanya ke negeri raksasa. 
 Cukup lumayanlah ceritanya, penuh fantasi liar yang pastinya sangat cocok untuk konsumsi pembaca cilik.

This is the story of the orphan girl Sophie who accidentally happens to see a Giant one night. Not wanting to be known by "human beans", the Giant decides to take Sophie with him to the Giant country. He is a very nice Giant, a Big Friendly Giant, but the other Giants are not... they gobble up humans every single night of their lives. 
 As the BFG is able to mix dreams and make people dream them, Sophie forms a plan to get the most powerful woman on the planet on the case: the Queen. With the help of a dream, she convinces her to act and act fast, and very soon, the army is helping the BFG to arrest all the murderous Giants. 
 The BFG and Sophie receive luxurious living quarters close to the Queen, and with the help of his new human daughter, the BFG even manages to become a writer, starting his career with a novel about himself and Sophie... 
 A nice little story. A bit brutal for younger readers, but entertaining and especially funny for everyone who likes word-plays.

This was one of my favourite books as a child :) 
 My poor parents have probably read it to me a thousand times heehee 
 If you have a child, read it to them :)
This was not one of my favorites. I didn't care for the reader. I'm also not a fan of "made up" words and this book has plenty of them.

Definitely not my favorite Roald Dahl, but I am very glad that I reread it. I remember feeling apathetic towards it as a tween, and the feeling still holds true. 
 Recommend For: Children/Fantasy/Tween

Quite possibly the worst book I've ever read. I had to force-feed it to myself to get it finished, reading about 5 pages at a time every week. The smallest event is written out in excruciating detail, and it's also written in the baby-babble language of the giant. I'd rather stub my toe than read this book again.

This was the most influential book of my childhood in getting me to read at all. I swear I thought the librarian had screwed up, and that this book was available only because no adult had bothered to read it. It was just that awesome to an 8 year old boy. 
 I mean, flying via fart power? It simply doesn't get any better. Roald Dahl was a gift to childrens' books. Few like him exist anymore--writers who don't dumb things down or rob children of wonder and mischief. 
 Harry Potter? No thanks. I'll keep my BFG.

reference_books.title: Of Poseidon (The Syrena Legacy, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
An exquisitely unique new YA that explores the realm below the ocean and brings readers on a journey they will never forget. 
 The story was very well written and the beautiful descriptions and attention to detail really captured my imagination. The romance was paced nicely without having any kind of instant love thing like some YA romances do. The characters had time to get to know each other and in the process allow readers to really get to know and become attached to these great characters. 
 The world of the Syrena was really intriguing and I enjoyed learning about it more and more throughout the book. 
 Emma is a sweet and sometimes quirky girl who I would love to have as a friend. She is a fun character to get to know and I really like her spunkiness especially around Galen. 
 Galen is a Syrena prince who is really dedicated to his job and his people. I really liked his character and seeing how he got along with Emma, although he could get a little arrogant. He could be so funny at times and then so serious at others. 
 Another character that I really enjoyed was Galen's sister Rayna. She did come across as a little abrasive in the beginning, but was fiercely protective of her friends and family. She was a fun character to get to know. I also enjoyed her relationship with Toraf because their interactions with each other were just so cute and I couldn't help, but laugh at some of their antics. 
 This story was spellbinding and I can't wait to see what else this author comes up with!

reference_books.title: The Demon Lover (Fairwick Chronicles, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
An enchanting read that will take your breath away. 
 The hauntingly beautiful imagery set the stage for this imaginative new story. The setting helped to add to the enchanting storyline. It was an interesting read and had an air of mystery about it that I really liked. There were some twists and turns that kept me guessing a bit throughout the story and kept it exciting. 
 Callie as a character was interesting and fun, but a tad naive. I enjoyed her as a character and liked seeing the mystery through her eyes. She was no pushover that's for sure and that was a good thing since she needed to be strong in order to overcome this monster. 
 I liked the premise for this book and enjoyed getting to know some unique characters, but I wouldn't really call this a romance. There were some romantic elements though that really brought out some intrigue in the story. Overall this was a fun fantasy mystery that I enjoyed reading.

reference_books.title: Ink (Paper Gods, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
A whole new world of adventure! 
 Ok there are so many things about this book that I loved, but the first thing that caught my attention was the location, Japan! I love Japan and everything about it, but there aren't that many YA books set in this place and the books that are tend to be based mainly in the past. The author gives us a glimpse into the contemporary Japan and using imagery and humor shows us many of the places and things that I would love to see for myself one day. I also loved how she was able to interweave a lot of the culture and mythology of Japan without making it seem like a history lesson. 
 Then there was the paranormal aspect to the story. I really liked the unusual powers the characters had with Ink and trying to figure out exactly what it was and how it worked. There was a lot we learned about it, but just as many questions arose from it as well and I can't wait to find out more in the next book. 
 Katie is a really strong willed character and I really admired her spirit. I liked that although she made mistakes she still kept trying. Just like when she was trying to learn the language. At first she wasn't that great at it and even though her friends didn't mind speaking to her in English she chose to keep on trying and perfect her Japanese instead of just giving up. She is a fun character to get to know and a bit quirky at times too. 
 Tomohiro was an interesting character and although I was a bit leery of him at first I really came to like him right along with Katie. He keeps to himself and for good reason, but once you get past that hard outer shell he really is a sweety and really funny. I love how he interacts with Katie and the way he sometimes teases her. It is so much fun to see them together. It was also great that he could also be so lighthearted and have a sense of humor about things given the situation he is in. I think he and Katie make a great team and I can't wait to see more of them. 
 I also loved Katie's two friends Yuki and Tanaka. Yuki is one of her first friends and she is one of my favorites. She is always cheerful and a lot of fun to be around kind of likes Tanaka who is a bit of a goofball. I liked how supportive they were of Katie even when things got really weird. They are definitely the kind of people I would love to be friends with. 
 Overall this is an exciting read with an imaginative new world that I am dying to read more of!

reference_books.title: Taste
reference_books.review_text:
Love has never been more dangerous. 
 This is a thrilling new romance that will leave you breathless. The impeccable writing and unforgettable characters kept me hooked from page 1. I couldn't have asked for a better paranormal romance than this. The storyline is unique and was filled with plenty of twists and turns along the way that kept me on the edge of my seat. 
 I was so immersed in this story that I pulled an all nighter just to finish it. I had lots of fun figuring out the mystery of the flesh eaters along with Pheonix. There were plenty of times that had me really worried about Phoenix's fate as well as times where I was mentally kicking Phoenix for some of her decisions. All in all it was a roller coaster ride of emotions and I loved every minute of it. 
 I couldn't help, but love these characters. Phoenix was a brave and kindhearted girl who I could definitely see myself being best friends with. 
 Demitri was my personal favorite character. He was a bit gruff at first, but after getting to know more about him it was plain to see he had a kind heart. He was a compelling character that I loved getting to know. 
 Luka was the more flirtatious and playful type and definitely an interesting character. He was fun and I had a great time reading about his interactions with Pheonix. 
 This is a dark and compelling new romance that paranormal fans won't want to miss out on.

reference_books.title: Cress (The Lunar Chronicles, #3)
reference_books.review_text:
The adventure continues in Cress! 
 The amount of action in this series just keeps getting bigger and better with every book. Things continue to heat up in this third installment and now the gang is getting ready to launch their first strikes against Levana. The first being to Save Cress! As Cinder digs deeper and more and more secrets are being revealed it is soon clear that it will take all that they have and as many allies as they can get to take down Levana. There was so many new mysteries cleared up in this book that I was constantly jumping up and down in excitement with each page turn. With more action unfortunately comes more danger and a few sacrifices. There was definitely some tear jerking moments in this book, but there were also plenty of just plain hilarious moments. 
 We meet Cress first in Cinder very briefly and I was intrigued, but not completely sure what to expect from her. After getting to know her in this book I was so excited. She is so adorable! Cress is also brilliant when it comes to programming which is why she is being forced to work for the lunar queen. I loved her courage and determination. She is trapped and betrayal could cost her her life, but she still does what she can to help the people of earth. I also loved her banter with Thorne. It was some of the best parts of the book! 
 Thorne was always the secondary wise cracker of the group and I liked that in this book he got some more time to shine. We definitely get to see A LOT more of his usual humor in this book, but I feel that we also get to see a softer side to him. It was kind of nice to see him caring so much for someone. Although his relationship with Cress has a long way to go I think there really is a small spark there. 
 So for all you lunar fans out there I highly recommend you go get your copy of Cress right now if you haven't already. Be warned it will put you on a roller coaster ride of emotions that will leave you screaming for the next book!

book_a.title: Intangible (Intangible, #1)
book_a.user_review:
Some may think being able to see the future or having the ability to heal with a touch is a gift and so did the twins Sera and Luke. That is until Luke had a premonition that will change their lives forever. 
 A well written fantasy that explores the relationship between siblings and what they would do to protect the ones they love. The imagery was beautiful and descriptive so that it really made you feel as if you were a part of their world. 
 The characters were relatable and I enjoyed getting to know all of them especially the twins. Sera and Luke have a great sibling relationship and it really shows how much they care for one another. They don't always get along which is to be expected, but they know how to work together to help those in need. Their emotional turmoil over Luke's vision and how they handled everything from then on out really brought out their true character. Sera was very brave and I think she handled the situation very well under their current circumstances (certainly better than I would). 
 This was a great read that I would recommend to fans of adventure with a bit of fantasy.

sample_reviews.review_text:
Intangible is one of those books where you find yourself loving every character. Needing to know what happens next. And, hoping that there will be a happy ending and not a dreadful one. Plus look at that pretty cover!! Intangible is exciting, dangerous, and full of magical moments. 
 We start off with Twins Sera, who can heal, and Luke, who can see the future. Then one freighting vision later, Luke sees Sera killed and his visions are never wrong. It becomes a race against time for Luke to figure out a way to save Sera. All the while, creatures are coming out that they never knew existed. Vampires, Fae, and well they might know something that Sera and Luke don't. 
 First off, I'm in love with twins. Any kind of twins is a huge win in my book and I absolutely adored Luke and Sera's story. Even though they both depend on each other so much, they each have their own strength. Watching them discover the world around them, figure out that they're apart of something bigger, and then do anything to save each other is true sibling love. Also, with Sera I really enjoyed her relationship with Mark. Mark is one of the sexy boys with the dark past that I find myself clinging to so I can give him a big hug. I thought he and Sera were good for each other, and I really hope to see more of him in the future. 
 Overall, the lore J. Meyers created was fascinating. Not only did she make Fae, and vampires, but she threw in special powers as well and that really captured my attention. Another thing J. Meyers did, was that she told the book from many different view points, and yet they were all perfectly in line with the story and easy to follow. I was very impressed with it and also loved it because I adore being inside different character's heads. Intangible is completely original and has loads of thrills to keep you turning the pages. I'll definitely be looking for the next one!

I was excited about this book going into it, but was left feeling a bit disappointed. 
 The highlight of the story was the romance. It was sweet and cute, and very warm and fuzzy. There was a bit of a triangle developing near the end, and I must admit that I am rooting for the "bad" guy. I found him to be much more intriguing and likable. 
 The actual plotline seemed a bit flat. I don't appreciate when parents keep huge secrets from their children for no apparent reason, and this is the main reason the book fell flat for me. There was never a good explanation given for why the parents didn't tell Sera and Luke anything about their abilities. If they had shared, I bet everyone's lives would have been much better, without the need to sneak around and get into trouble. 
 I was impressed at the varied amount of paranormal creatures in the story, however I don't think enough information was given about them. It almost seemed taken for granted that the reader was familiar with them, or something like that. I felt a bit out in left field about the behaviour of and reasoning behind a few of the characters. 
 Overall, this was a sweet romance that didn't quite deliver on the story. I enjoyed the characters, but never really connected with them. In a twist from ususal, I was left appreciating the romance, but not the plotline.

Intangible is a compelling, fast paced, read with rich characters that jump off the page into the reader's mind and heart. I found myself wishing I'd had friends like Fey, Luke and Sera when I was in high school. Fey is protective, witty, mysterious and beautiful, yet she doesn't let it go to her head. Luke is good looking, loyal, smart, and caring. Sera is kind, smart, couragous and compassionate. I enjoyed the unfolding of their secrets and personalities as the story progressed. The three of them are the heart of Intangible, but that doesn't mean the other characters we meet aren't crucial to the story as well. 
 Intangible is set in a world where vampires, elves and magic exsist, but are unknown to most humans. Luke and Sera are 17 year old twins who have special talents that they've kept secret their entire lives until events unfold that expose what they can do. They experience heartbreak, loss and betrayal while trying to figure our how they figure into the supernatural world they've discovered. I loved the author's take on the paranormal. The story was at times heart wrenching, but never without hope.

Intangible has everything that supernatural fans would want in a book! Vampires, elves, prophecy, and magic. 
 Intangible is about twins, Sera and Luke, who are believed to be the Children of the Prophecy, children born with special abilities to heal (Sera) and to see into the future (Luke). It is believed that these children will bring a change into the world, whether it be good or bad. That's a lot of information for a set of teens to absorb right? 
 In her true nature, Sera is unable to turn away from anyone who needs some sort of healing (body, mind, and soul). And it is because of her gift that she is sought out by the most fearsome creatures that walk the night. Some want her to help them change what they have become, and others like Lilith, the mother of all vampires....the head honcho...want to see her dead. 
 Luke is the ever faithful brother. With the gift to see things that have not yet come to pass, Luke is all too aware that all of his visions always happen, and can't do anything to change the outcome. When he has a vision of seeing the death of his sister, Sera, he will do anything he can to change the fates and save his twin from her demise. 
 With the help of friends like Fey, Jonas, and Marc, the twins do what they can to survive in a new world that they did not know existed, and where danger and threat is ever present. 
 Intangible by J. Meyers was a wickedly awesome ride! Chock full of action and sexy brooding characters by the name of sexy Jonas. When I started reading about Jonas, only one other character came to mind that reminded me of this hot vamp. I'm sure we all know who Angel aka Angelus from Buffy the Vampire Slayer is. Yah, Jonas reminded me so much of him. With his lurking in the shadows ways. 
 I loved the writing in this book, but most of all I loved the interaction between the characters. Meyers has put in so much humour in the book, especially with the words that come out of both Sera and Luke. Their jabs at each other, as well as towards their friends was so fun to read! It's what made me love these two characters so much. I felt as though they were my own friends come to life! 
 The action weaved throughout Intangible was plentiful, and when it came to the final showdown...it was non-stop. Once you think that all has been dealt with and nothing more could happen, Meyer's throws in another twist which will leave you up late at night to find out what the outcome will be, and to anxiously await the next thrill. I personally would love to see Sera and Jonas together, and perhaps see if there are any deeper feelings between Luke and Fey. 
 I recommend this book to fans of anything supernatural, who are looking for characters to fall in love with and claim as friends, and are looking for a ride that will leave you crying out for the next book!

First off, let me start by saying that there are elves and fae in these here pages -- neither of which am I a fan of -- but I still managed to enjoy this book. I honestly don't know what my aversion to either..umm..species(?) is, I just don't care for them. Anyway...I digress... 
 I'm kind of glad that I didn't know that the book centers around aforementioned creatures (oh - there's also a vampire), because I probably would have turned down the book, and I would have missed out on an entertaining read. 
 Despite the familiar merging of paranormal creatures that I feel has been done to death, the book still managed to feel fresh and it did hold my attention. What I liked most about the story was the dynamic, familial relationship between Sera and Luke. Despite their "powers", both of them are deeply human and relatable. They were close and always there for one another which I found really sweet. The other characters in the book are just as engaging, and I felt that almost all of them served a real purpose in driving the story forward. 
 While it did take me a while to get into the book, once I settled in I enjoyed the ride. It did drag in a few places, but not bad enough that I wanted to stop reading. There are some really good twists along the way and Ms. Meyers handles them nicely. They didn't seem forced at all. I also liked how she managed to believably balance a realistic high school existence and the supernatural elements that took place. 
 All in all, I thought this was a descent read. It will definitely appeal to all of the paranormal/fantasy/urban fantasy lovers out there.

Also found at: www.areadersdevotion.blogspot.co.uk 
 Thank you to J.Meyers for the review galley. 
 This book was a decent enough read and it had the potential. Unfortunately, it lacked in areas to make it a stand out amazing book. 
 " "Shall she be the first to die, Seer?" 
 Luke head whipped up and he froze with the realization - the woman, the voice, she was addressing him directly. That had never happened before. 
 She spoke again, a taunt. "Yes, I think so. Her healing makes her the more dangerous." 
 No. A chill tingled u hi neck, settled on his scalp. Not his sister. This one couldn't be about Sera." 
 What I found surprising about this book was that it was not just about Sera and Luke. No, we got introduced to many others and followed their stories. Each character had a different personality. There were no characters that I didn't like. There is usually at least one in a book. 
 While I liked all of the characters, my favourite had to be Marc. I have a soft spot for tragic characters. While Marc isn't the most tragic I have seen, he is still a guy finding himself in a bad situation and is trying to get out of it. I was drawn to him straight away and I was just willing for things to be alright for him. 
 The mythology is a lot more rounded than the synopsis made out to be as well. Not only do we have gifted humans but also faeries and vampires. I was really interested to see how all these different societies interacted with one another. While I really enjoyed the idea, I don't think each group was fully developed and it left me with a lot more questions. I don't know how intentional that was, if more was going to be revealed in later novels, but I guess I would of liked a bit more in this book. Especially the vampire hierarchy; I always like a good hierarchy in paranormal novels. 
 The plot was interesting, definitely generating the correct number of questions to keep me reading; wanting to find out what happens next. I mainly wanted to find out how each of the characters ended up being so heavily involved around these prophesied twins. I was also interested to know what the prophecy was and how that came to be. The climax was well done, with a good amount of tension; had me on the edge of my seat there. 
 Unfortunately, the overall story was a little slow. It took a while for the plot to warm up. While I like jumping back and forth between points of view, if it is at detriment to the pace then it is better without. The pace picked up after halfway which kept me reading until the end but that doesn't change the fact about the first half. 
 The characters were what I liked the most. Unfortunately the pacing and lack of development, in plot and mythology, brought this book down for me.

I loved this book! It was adorable. It really was. The world that J Meyers has created is exciting, heart breaking, scary, magical all rolled up into a beautiful and fun package. Intangible was a page turner for sure. 
 Twins Luke and Sera has special abilities that they keep to themselves. Luke is a Seer..he has visions of the future. Sera is a healer. She can heal anyone by putting her hands on them creating a warm light that no one else can see but Sera and Luke...or so they think! When Luke Sees Sera laying dead in a cave in one of his visions, he is hyper aware of everything. He is determined to make this the ONE vision he will change before it happens. He will not lose his sister. 
 Through a series of crazy events. Luke and Sera find themselves in the hands of vamps, fey...*SHHHH SPOILER FREE* The characters are so easy to love and get attached to. 
 AND this cover is GOREGOUS! I love this cover!!!

Intangible is about twins Sera and Luke, they both have special powers but due to their past when someone found out about their powers they keep them a secret. 
 I must admit I did get a little bored at the beginning of the book. It was fairly slow at starting although I know this was mainly because the book was introducing the characters and their lives. 
 I really liked both Sera and Luke they were kind and caring teenagers which is unique in itself. ( I have teenagers!) 
 I am not going to give away any spoilers because the book is great and you really do have to read it. It was very well written and after the first few pages of slowness the book started to flow and I was hooked.

I'd actually say it's 4.5 stars but that wasn't an option... 
 Intangible follows twins, Luke and Sera, who have special powers: Luke is a seer and Sera is a healer. They are the twins who have been prophesied long ago and everyone is looking for them because they can either make or break their future. Throughout this book the twins are tested and pulled through the ringer. Luke sees something that he desperately wants to change and Sera finds herself in trouble after healing somebody that a lot of people didn't want healed. Will the twins survive? Or will one of the many forces hunting them down win? 
 I could not put this book down. It was a quick read with a lot of action and excitement. I loved how tight knit the brother and sister pair were and that they would and will do anything for each other. I was able to relate to them because it reminded me of my sister and I. There are a lot of likable characters in this book, some you are drawn to quickly, and some take a while to warm up to. The book pulls you in from the very first page that leaves Luke fighting to save his sister's life. 
 This book is full of deception, intrigue, and excitement. Give it a try, you will love it!

Intangible was an awesome story with some really accomplished and out of this world characters!! The world of reality and the world of mystical creatures were creatively interwoven in a successful story that equally blended both worlds. Once you get to the climax of the story the thrills definitely do not stop there, in fact they spin you out of control up until the final page!

book_b.title: Need (Need, #1)
book_b.user_review: Loved it! In the beginning it really reminds me of a setup for a horror movie. When she moves to the new town to live with her grandmother and everyone seems to know something she doesn't. Anyways it is a very good book with a lot of comedy mixed among the mystery and suspense of the book. My favorite character is her friend Izzy who is just full of laughs and cuteness! Once you finish it will leave you needing more.

sample_reviews.review_text: I really enjoyed this book. The story was compelling and interesting.

Need has a very good story line, but it gets rather slow sometimes. However, I like the change of mythology on Pixies. It was nice to read about evil, normal sized, walking, talking pixies rather than say Tinker Bell.

Obviously, I enjoy fantasy books. Ones that include vampires, werewolves (shifters), fae (fairies, pixies, etc) and so forth...this is another one. And I loved it. (Again, why can't we do half stars?) I absolutely love the relationships between our group of friends, Devyn, Issie, Nick and Zara. 
 And the mention of all these different phobias makes me thankful I don't have that many fears! It was just a very interesting story; great plot and characters. I definitely am glad that I had Captivate ready and waiting for me to read. Patience is not a strong suit ;)

Need follows the story of Zara White who is send to live with her grandmother after the death of her step-father. In a lot of ways, the plot was very typical of a Young Adult Fantasy book. Girl moves to a new town where something strange is going on. Girl is attracted to boy who is clearly hiding something ... basically, it sounds like it should be interesting but it's been done so many times before. Okay, so the pixie thing is a bit unusual but not really enough to make this book exciting. 
 However, with good writing and great characters, books like this can be a fun read. After all, there's a reason why a lot of the plot devices are used in so many books. Sadly, there were too many of my pet hates in the writing style. The thing that bugged me most was that there was too much description of pretty much everything. It might be just me but I don't need to know what band is on someone's t-shirt unless it's relevant to the plot. I also found that the plot 'twists' were too predictable and didn't have any impact of surprise when they were revealed.. 
 The characters also annoyed me. Firstly because Zara made a bunch of new friends almost as soon as she arrived in town and not just people who were friendly to her but they acted like they'd known each other for years right from the start. The second thing that I disliked about Zara and her new best friends were that they were all too nice. 
 All of the issues I had with this book were down to personal preference though and I'm sure there are loads of people who'll read this book and enjoy it. If you like Twilight and the House of Night books then there's a good chance you'll like the Need series as well.

I kind of liked the story in Need, it was intriguing and a well-thought-out idea. But I didn't like how generic and dull the characters were, nor did I like the greeting card type writing style. It was too poetic and melodramatic in my opinion.

"Need! Indeed! I NEED the plots to have substance. I NEED the characters to be defined. I NEED some back story! Why are most YA books flat, lacks depth and details? It seems as though some YA authors feel that YA readers do not care! Stephanie Meyers appeal to women of all ages because she doesn't dumb down her readers and clearly this is another Twilight rip off. Girl sent to a remote wooded, cold and dreary town in Maine to live with grandmother. Love interest turns out to be a shape shifter who happens to be a werewolf. Pixies instead of vampires are natural enemies to Were's, were-wolfs, were-tigers, were-eagles, were-bears, and gold dusts, what? As far as romance is concerned it lacked Edward and Bella's chemistry. So the parallels were way too much. The only aspect of the book that I thought was original and had potential was Zara's obsession with phobia's. It was good for a light easy read. I just wished that there were so much more.
I won this book from a book blog and absolutely LOVE it!!! cannot wait to get my hands on Captivate!

One of those books what I should have never picked up in first place. 
 "He nearly killed me with his reckless driving, but when I saw how huge and handsome he was I just could not do anything else than stare him" 
 This misquote sums prety much what kind book this is and what is level of it's plot.

I couldn't finish this book. I plan on trying again, of course, but I got irritated when Zara quickly believed in pixies but somehow couldn't figure out that her crush was a werewolf, even after being told of their existence, tons of hints, seeing him in front of her, etc.
This book was awesome I just could not put it down and as soon as it was done I had to have the next book that day. Awesome is all I can say

sample_reviews.review_text: I feel like every book I have read the past few weeks have been about cheaters. The characters were good I suppose. However if I were 'sort of' dating someone I would totally not be cool with them 'checking out' potential loves (dating other people). The end was great but I feel like that was about it. I'm not normally a 2 star person. I feel like most books I read are amazing but please just don't waste your time with this one.

Had potential but I found I never got invested in the main character. I also never fell in love with the love interest. To me a good book snags you and drags you deep into the heart of it, where you are no longer reading a story but living another life. All I did was read this one. My life still went on around it and I was very much present in that part of my world, I never was able to get lost. I think it needs a little more depth... more build up and backstory in the beginning and more character development. It was close but just fell short.
Way too wordy and it lacked a good plot. It had a good enough premise but lacked force and kind felt all over the place. I was really hoping for better from the reviews, but was very disappointed.

I didn't really enjoy this novel. I love contemporary romances and I was looking forward to reading some hot and heavy teacher drama in this one... but I got something completely amateurish and just not very good. 
 All of our characters are teachers in a high school and you would expect them to behave in a moderately adult manner, but instead they all act like randy immature 15-year-olds themselves. Shelly Gelson (I don't know why, but I hate her name) is our heroine who has recently been dumped by her high school sweetheart, Chase, for one of their buxom co-workers. Shelly's friend Matt, another teacher, has always carried a torch for her and he starts pursuing her. 
 I just couldn't get past the uneducated way all of the teachers spoke and the completely juvenile way they all acted. The dialogue is stilted and the attempts at humor fell completely flat for me. I also was surprised at how often Shelly was out drinking. It seemed like she was at the bar almost every night. She had some weird obsession with beer and was a complete beer snob, which turned me off of her character. 
 The premise was good, but the execution here is just awful. There are great self published novels out there, but this is not one of them. I don't plan on reading anything else by this author, I just don't see the talent for storytelling here.
Great summer read!

What in the world did I just read?> 
 Before I begin my rant about how horrible this book was, I need to clarify a few things first. I was scrolling through Amazon looking for something interesting to read when I came across Against The Wall. I had put into the search bar that I wanted YA romance.. this book popped up. I read the blurb and, deciding that it looked interesting, downloaded it to my Kindle. 
 Big Mistake. 
 It did not take me long to figure out that this was not a YA novel. In fact, it wasn't even in the same ball park. Now, I have no problem with romance novels but I DO Not enjoy trashy, horribly-written, and pathetic excuses for books that fit into the romance genre. In fact, this book should be buried, never to be seen again. 
 For one thing, I didn't want to read an adult romance novel. Frankly, I do like how graphic things tend to get in those kinds of books, and that was something I was trying to stay clear of. Hence why I typed in YA romance! Another thing, when I looked at the blurb, this book was not tagged in adult romance and gave no hint to it being that. Well, it sure showed me. 
 I knew a chapter into the book that it was, unfortunately, an adult romance novel, but I gave it a try. My thoughts were: Give it a try, Kalla, you've read adult romance novels that were really good." And so I did. 
 I'm not even sure where to start on how terrible this book was. To be honest, this is one of the worst I've ever read. Ever. 
 The main protagonist, Shell, is a teacher. She's supposed to be setting a good example for her students. One would think that high school drama is the worse, but noooooo, Shell's is worse. Her life might as well be the center for drama. And how does she handle said drama? By cussing every sentence, degrading herself, and getting drunk. 
 I cannot even begin to tell you how much Shell and her friend Mell obsess over men. It was pathetic and I was solely embarrassed to see that the author embodies women in her book as this. Both women were shallow and "sex crazed". It was so bad that I was waiting on the chapter where they would find out they had an STD. I just wanted to scream, "Helloooo, do you not have anything better with your time! You're both adults- quit acting like hormone-crazed teenagers!" I understand that adults have physical relationships and that doesn't bother me. But when you put together 200+ pages of women acting like they can't live without some action in the bed, that's just plain annoying and ridiculous. 
 Every character in this boot annoyed me. I didn't like a single one. Matty, the guy Shell falls in love with is made out to be the perfect guy by the author and frankly, I just don't see it. He annoyed me. Both of them annoyed me. They decide to "see where things go" with each other and the next thing you know, he's practically living in her house! I don't know if it's just me, but I think revealing you're attracted to someone and then practically living together in less than 24 hours, that's fast. Toooo fast. 
 Another thing. The language in this book was crude and I found myself at times wanting to delete the book, but I almost always try to finish a book once I start it, regardless of how terrible it is. But the cursing and crude sayings was just too much. It didn't make the characters seem like adults/high school teachers. It made them look like teenagers! There was one part towards the beginning of the book where Shell was talking about another teacher at the school and said something along the lines of: "...and punch her each in the tits" or something of that nature. How very immature. I let it slide, though, thinking that it was a one time thing. Nope, it wasn't. Immature things like that were constantly said in the book. It really wasn't needed and it took away from the book and the characters, making them look shallow and nothing like adults. 
 The sex scenes. Well, it was like walking through the desert. So dry and with no end in sight. It was BORING and there was no chemistry. The writing was poor and every time a sex scene came up (which was a lot) I just skipped it. For this to be a "romance novel" it was a letdown for sure. Everything about this book was a letdown. A utter, massive catastrophe. Yep, a sloppy mess of words. 
 I should get a gold medal for even finishing this book. It was like being tortured, but I think I would have enjoyed being tortured more.

 I don't think I'll continue the series, this one just wasn't for me.

So I totally love the book after this one more. 
 I loved the idea of this book, how it started with the writing back and forth....and then the hero drops off the face of the planet for the heroine without a word. This is how it starts out. With out heroine missing our hero's contact..thinking she'd feel in love with him over 4 years of writing to each other every month and then he just "boom" disappears on her. 
 It was really sweet. But see, that was my problem. This book was just sweet...and very tame. It had it's moment's sure, but the fact that he's a fighter (literally) in this book, makes me want my Alpha to be more...more AGGRESSIVE! 
 He was very patient with the heroine's forgiveness of him disappearing on her for 2 years. That was really sweet <----again, there's that word.

 And he was...sort of...just in a really sweet way. 
 So, yeah, it was just okay. I liked Noah and Grace, they were just both really sweet.
