sample_reviews.review_text:
i love reading a good fluffy friends to lovers romance to procrastinate but the this was boring and the girl was really annoying and shallow. 
 maybe I'm getting too old for this kind of story?

Boys Next Door: Lori loves Sean. Sean loves himself and Rachel. Adam loves Lori but is dating Rachel. Until Sean and Adam, brothers, have a party and Sean and Rachel make out. Lori is devastated and concots a plan for Adam to get Rachel back and for her to get Sean: she and Adam will pretend to date. But, as one plan leads into another we learn 1. Adam is doing this for real and 2. Lori's plans always backfire. 
 After a few more schemes and misunderstandings, Lori finally gets a clue and Adam gets Lori. 
 Endless Summer: On the first night of officially dating Adam takes Lori to secret make out spot and they both fall asleep. The rents of both kids are NOT happy. Lori's father forbids her to see Adam, Adam is forbidden to see Lori or ever talk to her per his parents. 
 But they suck at staying apart and get into further trouble by being caught together. More misunderstandings courtesy of Lori's terrible plans, that, of course, ends in a happily ever after. 
 Or is it? 
 Echols did something interesting here. She had an adult character, former nanny of Lori, tell Lori how her relationship with Adam is destined to be, well, a bit volatile. They will have a rocky road and that one day Lori might get sick of it and leave. I thought that was interesting because while reading Adam flipping out every time Lori talked to a boy that was not him I thought - crap, that would annoy the hell out of me! 
 Lori and Adam seemed perfect for each other in every other way - they got each other in ways no one else had ever done. If Adam and Lori managed to do some serious growing up I could see them working out. 
 And right here is where I can't believe I've given this much thought to fictional characters in a teen romance.

I didn't hate it but I didn't love it either. I felt like the book was written as a reaction to people wanting a sequel to the much better first book The Boys Next Door. The characters were not developed enough to get a second book out of them. A lot of the time I had to remind myself that the main characters were 16 because I wanted to tell them to grow-up. All in all not bad for what it was, but not a favorite either.
The second half (so Endless Summer #2) was by far my least favourite book by Echols.

Endless Summer by Jennifer Echols stars clueless Lori McGuillicudy who gets in romantic entanglements with the boys next door. The cool thing about Endless Summer is that it is two books in one. The first book is The Boys Next Door, and the second book is the sequel, Endless Summer. 
 Read the rest of my review here
My bad. I relive enough of my embarrassing youth in my head to take on Lori's. 16 year olds are really stupid, turns out.

Perfect summer read. It's a cute, sweet, funny story. Adam is totally adorable. For a boy with ADHD, I don't know how he put up with Lori. She could drive a sane person nuts with all of her plans to make things right again. I felt bad for Adam. His brother Sean was horrible to him. 
 The things that Adam does to get Lori back are so sweet. He's the sweetest ever. Love how the boys don't think of Lori as a girl but just one of the guys. Lori is hilarious when she's making herself over. She's been a tomboy all her life and suddenly is changing and trying to make herself sexy, beautiful and a girly girl. Don't know what she saw in Sean and wanted him. Sean is a pain. Sean and Adam are always fighting and Cameron and McGillicuddy are always tearing them apart. 
 This is a light, funny story. I would recommend to anyone.

** spoiler alert ** 
 I liked the characters and I wanted to give it more than 2 stars,but couldn't.There was too much time spent on Lori making out with all the Vader boys while claiming her love for Adam.Reading about Adam was like riding a roller coaster.I really wanted to like it more,but oh well.

Endless summer? More like endless book! This is BY FAR the WORST book I have read in my whole LIFETIME! I agreed to read this book because a friend of mine absolutely adores these kinds of love stories. Of course, I agreed, because we usually have the same taste in books. NOT THIS TIME. I was extremely disappointed in the quality of the author's writing. Not only was it a very cliche plot, but it was written like a 16 year old was texting it! I get that a 16 year old was narrating it, but, come on, do you really have to abbreviate 'conversation' into 'convo' every single time the word is said? Just to get an idea on how cliche this book really is, when you look up 'endless summer' in the goodreads search box, you have to scroll down the page to find it because there are so many book called THE SAME EXACT THING. Also, was it really necessary to make this book 587 pages long? This story could have been told on less than half the pages because of all the nonsense that goes on in this book. Also, technically, this is two books smushed together into one book. I'm guessing the only reason the author decided to do this was because they knew no one would dare to buy the sequel after reading the atrocious first book, so, to solve the problem, they put the second book in the same purchase so the reader is practically forced to read it. There were many times I wanted to stop reading the book, but it is my unwritten rule that I must finish every book that I start, no matter the quality(and I wanted to write this snarky review). I mean, this book doesn't even deserve one star! Is it possible to give a half star? An eighth? A sixty-fourth? 
 So, being the generous person I am, I am going to give you a basic summary of this book so you won't have to go through the terrors of reading 587 looooong pages of nothing. 
 Lori likes Sean but he doesn't know or care and Sean's younger brother, Adam, is Lori's best friend. Adam has feelings for Lori and Lori is too blinded by her puppy love for Sean to notice. Lori decides that to get attention from Sean, she should show off her body by wearing itty bitty bikinis, low cut tops, and short skirts. Wait. Stop. This is already too much. Lori thinks that dressing up like a slut is going to help her?! Great message, author, really. We should all just parade around in minimal clothing so boys can make out with us because that is what all girls want in life: a steady boyfriend who uses us because we (un)dress like a glorified tramp. Okay... It is too painful for me to give a summary because I'll just stop every sentence to hate on it. In short, this is the book summary: Lori fantasizes about boys. Adam broods. Lori wears trampy clothes. Adam broods. Adam gets in a fist fight with Sean. Adam broods. Lori falls for Adam. Adam broods. Lori and Adam make out. Adam and Lori make out. Lori fantasizes about making out with Adam. Adam and Sean get into a fistfight. Adam broods. Happy ever after... Until the next book where not only is it narrated by Lori, its narrated by Adam too! Yay. 
 So you see? I needn't go any further. But I must. Time for the second book! 
 Because Adam narrated every other chapter in the *sarcastic voice* thrilling second, and last(hallelujah)installment of whatever the heck this joke of a series is called, I will focus all of my evil self on him. Here is a backstory on Adam: he has ADHD which makes him stupid and prone to punch people to get his feelings across(come on kid, use your words). He is hopelessly in love with Lori, which makes him really sweet to her, but he is still a stupid guy. I know this because not one chapter goes by when he doesn't mention her... body... For example, he mentions how GREAT she looks in her bikini MULTIPLE times and how she looks in her bikini bottoms and other stuff that made me want to puke. 
 So there you have it everybody, I know I totally attacked the author but in my opinion, she deserved it. I hope you never have to cross paths with this book again other than to read this review.

Why did I give it two 2 stars? Easy. I'm a big Jennifer Echols fan (absolutely loved Going Too Far)but did'nt feel this book is up to par. I found Lori too immature for a 16 year old girl, who grew up without a Mom and has a part-time job. Adam, I liked. But the second part of the book makes him looks like a fool. 
 Despite it all, I will still continue reading Echols novels.

This book is a crazy sci-fi romp that I would have eaten with a spoon when I was 13. It's not great literature, but it is unputdownable and thrilling. Reminded me of my childhood favorite, Christopher Pike.

Oh my god what. 
 I think maybe this was actually written by an alien rather than a Norwegian. At first I just assumed the peculiarly flavorless dialogue was a result of the translation process, but the way that no character at any time behaves the way an actual human would--there's just no other explanation. 
 Alien wrote this. 
 The end. 
 (the end, by the way, I did enjoy since everyone dies . Yay!)

To celebrate the anniversary of the moon landing, NASA decides on a major publicity stunt to win back the world's waning interest. They're going to send teens to the moon. Chosen at random, three teens from around the world win a special trip into outer space, but there's something darker going on with in the walls of NASA. There is another reason for this trip, a more sinister reason, one that may just cost them their lives. 
 The premise of this book was interesting, and the mystery of the moon had potential, but nothing comes of it. Things just happen. There were so many points where this story could have been great, but whenever it came time to take action, it felt like the characters had taken a lethal dose of stupid. 
 At one point, a pair of astronauts had to fix a malfunctioning generator and were running low on oxygen, one of them wanted to stay behind and keep working on it but they were out of time, and then they find themselves trapped with no escape. So, what did they do? Work on the generator until their dying breathe? No. They took off their helmets and just gave in. It's moments like that that really grate on me and made this book hard to finish. It happened so often that by the end I just didn't care anymore. 
 The number of plot holes and irrelevant info dumps really just hurt this book. It's clear that the author had done plenty of research, unfortunately it wasn't on any of the areas that actually count. In one chapter, there is an unnecessarily detailed account of the Kuchisake-Onna myth that had very little payoff and even less relevance. 
 The ending itself seemed to go out of its way to avoid making sense. There were several times when the story could have taken a turn and ended with some actual meaning, instead it finished with evil!Mia strangling a homeless man and taking over a New York hotel . 
 The story tries to be too many things at once; at some points it wants to be a scifi thriller like Alien, at others a ghastly horror story like Blair Witch, elsewhere a teen drama or an action adventure, and just ends up feeling like a mess. While it wasn't so bad as to make me stop reading, it did end up feeling like a waste of a perfectly good premise. 
 I begrudgingly give this book 2 stars.
Terrifying!

I have to start out by saying I was reading The Martian and Horrorstor at the same time as this book so I may be a bit bias towards it. The Martian gave me better space and science. Horrorstor gave me much better creep. That being said, it takes a lot for me to give a book a one star rating especially when a lot of people around me absolutely loved it. The thought, "What am I missing?" pops into my head a lot. But, well, these are my opinions. I found the whole story really blah, a bit boring and not really scary. The beginning was super slow and I understand we needed to build up the suspense but it was more, "Are we there yet?" then "OMG what's going to happen next?" I found the three teenagers boring and I had a hard time relating to any of their lifestyles. Also, having different perspectives is great when it actually makes sense and helps the story along. A random chapter with Simone just felt like filler. And that ending...it was such a twist, right? Well, that's because we have no idea how to even begin to understand what happened or how we got there. And maybe reading this in a hard copy would be better than an ereader but the random pictures of the moon sprinkled throughout the story again felt like we were trying to reach a minimum page requirement or something. The fact that once we got to the moon and it felt like people just gave up made me think that the book was a waste of my time because it felt unrealistic. Half the time I was thinking, "Mark Watney could have fixed it! (The Martian), the other half I was thinking why were the teenagers smarter than the astronauts.... Anyway, I wouldn't recommend this book but I wouldn't try to stop someone from reading it. Like I said, I'm still wondering if I was missing something or it just might be me. :)

book_a.user_review:
Kemunculan buku terakhir ini sepertinya lumayan melengkapi. Kenapa? Menurut gue, sebenernya sampe buku 3 udah cukup, asal dia udah berubah jadi vampir. Apalagi di akhir Eclipse ketahuan banget dia bakal nikah sama Edward.

sample_reviews.review_text: I liked the idea of a cross-breed human/vampire child but for the most part it is 700 pages of nothing. A bland conclusion for a series that started with great promise.

Seriously, what kind of story is this. 
 I read the first book because I was curious. I read the second book because I didn't want to judge a series by the first book. I read the third because I wanted to see how bad it could get. I read the fourth because the mindfuck had officially drawn me in and I couldn't help myself. It's like a car accident, you know you shouldn't look, but you can't help it. I don't even want to remember the things I've read.

I loved Twilight, New Moon and Eclipse but this last book of the saga I didn't like very much. There were moments when I felt disgusted while reading it, like at the moment of Renesmee's birth. There was something that I didn't enjoy at all that was when the narrator changed. I was too used to be like inside Bella's mind and when I read Jacob's side of the story... It was really weird for me. Despite that, I think it went ok.

** spoiler alert ** 
 It appeared as though the first three books had some conflict. Some actual conflict. Sacrifices were going to have to be made. In the end, Bella wouldn't be able to have everything she wanted, nor would Edward, nor would Jacob. And with the added peril of the Volturi coming, it seemed as though someone we cared about might actually die. 
 But, in the end... everyone gets everything they'd ever wanted and nobody we care about dies. What is this, Disney? The intended audience is not the problem - I'm sure we can all think of a well known series for young adults that deals with conflict, sacrifice, and death, and deals with these things for real. 
 It seems the drama of the entire series centers around characters being afraid of what might happen, even though none of it ever does. I think the final "battle" scene sums it all up (I accidentally just typed "scums it all up," which would be apt as well). They've been anticipating all possible outcomes of this battle for a good chunk of the book. They're prepared for casualties. They're prepared for orphans. They're making a stand against oppression with their very lives. 
 And then... nothing happens! All conversations go according to plan. They convince the right people of the right things. The bad guys leave without a fight! The Cullens' extended "family" all survive with nary a scratch. 
 Happily ever after blah blah blah. If it weren't such a quick read, I'd say it was a waste of my time. Maybe it still is.
I enjoyed it.
The redemption for this book that honestly has the weakest plot of anything I've ever seen published was the snippets from Jacob's point of view. I think he's a really funny narrator.

** spoiler alert ** 
 And done. The ending was happy. Not that i don't enjoy happy endings but it was almost too happy. 
 Someone from book club (Cathi maybe?) totally predicted what was going to happen in regards to the Bella, Edward, Jacob situation. we even discussed how they were going to have a baby... Meyer's explanation made sense as soon as i read it. 
 I liked how Edward and Bella's relationship matured a little when they got married. I was so glad she stopped flipping out about getting married in the first place even if it was while she was walking down the aisle. that was my single biggest irritaion with the books, that she wanted to spend the rest of time with edward by becoming a vampire but had reservations about marrying him *slaps forehead repeatedly* gah! 
 i never believed that Alice had actually abandoned them. 
 i continue to be appalled by the bad editiing. Little and Brown you are about to go on my list if you can't get some better editors. 
 Jacob is slightly more tolerable bonded to Renesme (hate that name).

Zero stars! Zero f***ing stars!! This is seriously must be the worst thing ever written. Meyer's prose hasn't improved even a little since the first book, she contradicts her own mythology, the plot is filled with logical holes, and it all culminates in a giant epic battle that never actually happens. Really, its a thousand pages of nothing. Crappily written nothing. I won't even get in to the disturbing, violent implied sex and the equally disturbing, violent pregnancy. Not to mention the horrendous mangling of basic human reproductive biology.

** spoiler alert ** 
 Good lord...talk about your lame ass everything wrapped up in a neat little package ending...She should have died...then she could have stopped boring the world with her plain obsessive BORING whinyness.

Although I sort of enjoyed the first book, as the series went on, I became less and less happy with the content. Although I did like the character of Jacob Black, I did not like the way the books were heading, and by the middle of the 4th book, Breaking Dawn, I quit. Things were a little too personal for me, although I was glad that they did get married, and the language was hard to ignore any more. I'm sorry it had to be this way, but I couldn't really continue.

Delightful to be immersed in a very different culture with such different idioms and resonances and nuances and the whole flavour of life. The plot development is excellent; very strong characterisations but fantastic detail which enlightens rather than immerses.

After a long time i came across a book I liked so much ! This is a fascinating book with a very intriguing plot. I had to waddle through the first 150 pages without understanding what is happening but as I started getting a sense of the story I couldn't put it down. I wish i could give it a 5 star but for a few things about this that nagged me. I felt the book could have been edited better and at least 200 odd pages could have been shaved off this mammoth. Too many pages were dedicated to Ushigawa which didn't add to the main story in anyway, rather detracted from it. This is my first Murakami and I will definitely read more!

The ending was enough of a disappointment to keep this from getting the 4 star rating I'd expected to give it for much of the time I sent reading. After nearly a thousand pages, and almost as many characters and plotlines, leaving so much unresolved felt like an insult. I was left with the impression that Murakami realized he had no idea how to wrap things up, and just tacked on an ending.
Oh goodness, the descriptions were awful and long-winded. This book is over-hyped.
Really tried to like this book, but couldn't get into it. Perhaps it isn't my genre...

Not what I'm used to. Definitely out of my comfort zone but it was an interesting book. For something as long as this book is, I almost wish it had been a couple hundred pages longer to tie up some loose ends.

Somewhere in this nearly 1000-page novel, there is a mildly interesting 400-page surreal mystery/love story yearning to get out. As it stands though, 1Q84 is a colossal disappointment. It is a supremely dull read, thanks to its glacial pacing, its endlessly repetitive rehashing of known events, and its paragraph upon paragraph of tedious and unnecessary minutiae. 
 Awful. Skip it. Read Hard-Boiled Wonderland instead.

I think I just wasted 47 hours listening to this book on Audible. 
 I *MIGHT* have liked it better reading the whole 945 pages, but I definitely didn't like the slow pace of the reading done for Audible, and I disagreed with the voice characterization of the main female protagonist. Disagreed immensely. 
 Overall, it was the last 100 pages that had me howling in agony, outraged that I'd spent all this time on this novel I thought was a combination sci-fi/religious commentary/suspense story, and instead is apparently the ultimate love story complete with the rebirth of the baby Jesus. 
 Good grief.
Well, I only got part way thru. Couldn't keep my interest enough to continue such a long book.

This book is a nice love story about a couple who try to overcome severe odds to be together. I had expected something different I guess. The first part of the book was fast paced and easy to read, but I got bogged down midway through the story. It took me far too long to read. Each chapter passed from character to character but never moved on. For example, why was so much time spent on Tengo's father? Why did we spend so much time with Ishikawa? What happened to Tengo's older girlfriend and what was the connection to his mother and Tengo's visions. So much time was spent opening up questions that were never answered. In the end I felt that I had wasted too much time travelling down avenues that never ended. Frustrating to say the least. You can read it if you wish, but don't tell them I sent you.

reference_books.title: The Star-Touched Queen (The Star-Touched Queen, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
Hands down the best part of this book was Kamala the cynical, bloodthirsty, talking demon-horse. 
 I had such high hopes for this one. In theory I should have loved it: a magical fantasy inspired by Indian mythology? Sign me the f up, right?? But it just didn't deliver. The plot was sloppy, the characters were one-dimensional, and the romance relied too heavily on the fated lovers trope, rather than a genuine connection. The writing was lovely, but the floweriness (Safari isn't underlining that, so apparently it's a word) of it seemed to simply serve as a cover-up for those lacking essential elements of a good story. 
 The world was really intriguing, but it also could have used so much more development. I might give the second book a go in the hopes that it focuses more on the world-building and characters, but if it's just going to be more of Maya and Amar being inexplicably drawn to each other then no thank you.

This book works pushes the boundaries both in storytelling and artwork. It thrusts the reader into deep into an alternate world that is so complex but believable that it could create its' own cottage industry. Talking cats with multiple tails, human-animal hybrids, witches that are nuns and angels that are demons, zombie priestesses all after a girl who has a monster inside her that every one wants but are terrified to discover. All this going on in an Art-deco steampunk world that is beautifully envisioned by Sana Takeda with a nod to both eastern and western standards with just a pinch of the Final Fantasy video game series. This book will take the reader to a place they have never been before. It is like Game of thrones on steroids with a manga flavor. 
 The story is too complex to describe in a simple review and I doubt that I could give it the justice it deserves. It works on a massive scale with many moving parts and players. It can seem a little choppy to a casual reader but I felt that I was on the same journey as the heroine; not sure what was inside her and who her friends or enemies where. This was a voyage of discovery for both her and the reader and the confusion was not because of bad writing but more a plot device to lead the reader along. It worked for me. As new characters appeared I found myself wondering what they were about and that is all a reader could ask for. Also the villains of the piece were brilliant. There wasn't a lame character among them even if their motives were unclear. 
 This is a book that left me with a lot of questions but wanting to find the answers and I can't praise the artwork enough. It may not be the easiest Graphic Novel I've read but it is one of the most rewarding and fascinating. Highly recommended and one that can be read again and again.

Persistently gorgeous artwork and well placed panels were not enough to save this tantalizingly ambiguous steam punk weebo universe.  Anyway there were some badass chthulhu inspired Garra/Naruto level transformations to drool on. And the uncanny similarity of ancient God with the inter dimensional monster from Locke and Key was hard to ignore. I guess, this was my issue- for a world this ambitious, Monstress failed to deliver. 
 Also it wasn't free off the usual YA cliches- chosen one, prophecy, troubled childhood, lost big shot parents, blood with vampirish background, infernal monsters and Rosicrucian secrets. Pretty sure, 'the perfect guy ordained to be with heroine eons' ago is waiting to appear in further installments. 
 And cats, annoying cats.

reference_books.review_text:
also posted here: http://alwayslostinbooks.wordpress.co... 
 And here we find another book that I judged by the cover so I made it part of one of my reading goals~ This was a free-for-all read on Netgalley so I thought I would try it out because the cover looked lovely. But that is how far you should go with this book. It is definitely not worth reading and I regretted even downloading and reading it. This book made me want to cry at how badly written it was. I'm not claiming to be a good writer, but sheesh, even I know there's something wrong with this writing. I just couldn't stand it! I HATED IT! But I forced myself to finish it so that I can make a proper review. Unfortunately, I don't think I can make one. All I have is a lot of rants for The Edge of Never. 
 I think that this book is so poorly written that I couldn't even bother to care about the characters or the story. I was so BORED the whole time. I feel that Camryn's life or her perceptions were too overdramatized. I honestly do not understand how anyone could give this book 5 stars. I cannot count how many times I rolled my eyes at the ridiculous lines. That's pretty much the only reaction I had for this book - eye-rolling. Mostly I just kept a straight face because I was too bored. This is a book that tells the story in two perspectives, which can be really be good. But there was this one part where I thought,"Uuuhhh. Hello? I just read that grueling last chapter and you need to repeat the whole situation again? Why?" Her writing is so redundant. Her attempt at humor fell flat. And let's not forget the over-the-top lines: "There's a flutter inside my chest, just between my breasts behind my ribcage." Even the sex scenes didn't rouse anything from me. In fact, they were just ridiculous and boring. I won't talk about the ending, but I hated that too, especially how the last chapter transitioned into the epilogue. 
 One thing I noticed is that Redmerski seems to be using one word a lot - spat (of air, of whatever, etc). What does it even mean? Does anyone know? Because when I look it up on the dictionary, these are the definitions I come up with: "past and past participle of spit," "(usu. spats) historical a short cloth gaiter covering the instep and ankle," "a cover for the upper part of an aircraft wheel," "a petty quarrel," "quarrel pettily," and "the spawn or larvae of shellfish, esp. oysters." So what the heck does it mean to let out a spat of air? Because she surely uses it a lot on this book. Is there some other meaning to this word that I don't know about? 
 After reading this book, these are things that I think Camryn and Andrew would think or say, which should pretty much sum up my thoughts on the characters. Sometimes they do actually say it in the book. The ones in quotation marks are direct quotes from the books. The ones in parentheses would be my extra thoughts~ 
 Camryn: 
 My BEST FRIEND since second grade is a slutty bitch. I'm so much better than her~ All the girls in the world are sluts. I'm the best girl in the world! I am so smart and perceptive~ 
 People don't know what depression is. I know what depression really feels like and no one needs to take any pills. 
 Fast food, soda, junk food, etc. are so gross, but I will eat/drink them when no one's there to see. 
 Thank you for helping me contemplate my life, Andrew. Now will you fuck me to actually make the world better? 
 My best friend was a bitch to me so I should punish her by not talking to her for so long, but I'll make her get on a plane to go across the country for me when things go wrong. 
 Andrew: 
 Hey Camryn, that pervert on the bus has been watching you all this time, but you don't need to know about it. I'll watch him until I need to leave you so that he can harass you when I'm gone. 
 I have to be Mr. Tough Guy so I shouldn't model. I'll just work as a mechanic. (What's wrong with modelling?) 
 Camryn, tell me everything about you! Now! But I won't tell you anything about me~ Even when my life is at stake. 
 Let me own you goddammit so I don't have to fucking leave you and I can finally have sex with you! (Whaaat) 
 SHIT. FUCK. SHIT. FUCK. DAMN. SHIT. FUCK. DAMN. FUCK. SHIT. FUCK. "We look almost exactly alike with the same brown hair and crazy fucking dimples." (What.) (Why does he keep on swearing every time?) 
 Well, that's all I can think of right now, and I don't think I'd want to waste any more of my time for this book so I shall end it here. There are just too many things that are wrong with this book. This is just one of the worst books I've read, and I really hate it. No offense meant to people who actually loved this. I just cannot take it at all. And now, I am afraid to ever read anything from J.A. Redmerski. Are her other books any better? I honestly do not understand her way of thinking after reading this book. 
 NO. JUST NO.

reference_books.title: The Moth in the Mirror (Splintered, #1.5)
reference_books.review_text:
Originally posted here: http://alwayslostinbooks.wordpress.co... 
 The Moth in the Mirror gives a different point of view for some unseen parts of Splintered, book 1, while also bridging a possible transition for Morpheus in Unhinged, book 2. I will admit that it was not what I was expecting. I was hoping for a lot more Morpheus! The title is "The MOTH in the Mirror" after all. So maybe that's why I was a little disappointed. But this was still a really good read overall. In this short story, Morpheus looks into Jeb's memories in order to learn more about him and destroy him. 
 "'Tis a pun, like the one you made earlier, but much more clever." - Morpheus 
 That was one of my favorite line from Morpheus throughout the book. It reminds me a little of Johnny Depp's portrayal of Captain Jack Sparrow, and that makes me love Morpheus so much more. I like how he's so fashionable and a little quirky. And he's so sure of himself. And even though he's kind of a bad guy, he's definitely just charming. I love him so much more even though I know Jeb is the right choice for Alyssa. 
 What I found most interesting about this book is when it's Morpheus' point of view because it shows how the inhabitants of Wonderland think so much differently than those in the human world. I'll admit he seems a little too crazy sometimes with the way he thinks and how he acts on the things he wants. But I mostly like how his feelings for Alyssa has changed him, making him a little more human than he'd like. I'd really love to know how things would work out for him. 
 Huh, I think this is more of a "Why I love Morpheus" post rather than a review for The Moth in the Mirror. :P 
 Anyway, for the fans of Jeb. A lot would be shown on how he handled things when he was away from Alyssa in Splintered, where he mostly kept on worrying about her and wanted nothing but to have her safe. It shows even more how much he cared about Alyssa. It even moved Morpheus a little, and I guess that says something. 
 ************************************************** 
 OVERALL, The Moth in the Mirror made me even more excited to read Unhinged. It gives a more intimate look into Morpheus and Jeb. I personally wish there was more of Morpheus, but I still loved this as A.G. Howard feeds us tiny bites of wonder, humor, charm, and romance. Give me Unhinged now please!

sample_reviews.review_text:
I was able to avoid reading reviews and even talking about this book with my fellow bookworms that's why I had no idea on how the story would end. 
 In this third and final book of Veronica Roth's Divergent series, a secret alliance was formed against Evelyn's system and Tris, Tobias and the others were chosen to go outside the city to find out what is hidden beyond the fence. 
 It was narrated through Tris and Tobias' points of views which for me was confusing most of the time and i had to flip back some pages to check whose POV I was reading. Maybe because I got used to Tris' as the only narrator or they somehow sound similar. The good thing is we know what's going on with Tobias' head and how he feels about everything. The relationship between the two is tested and of course there are also some sweet and "intense" moments between them. 
 What is the symbol on the cover means? I thought it has something to do with Erudites but it's not. It doesn't have anything to do with the factions. (This is not a spoiler, right?) It's really advisable to read the first two books before reading this one. Here, readers will encounter (again) some new characters and some new problems or circumstances in and outside the city. I personally didn't expect that something like that was going on beyond the fence. 
 I really don't know how i feel about the ending. I'm not really disappointed (unlike the majority of people who read this book) instead, I was dreadful (after reading chapter 50) that it made me cry while reading until the last chapter. I feel so sad until now while typing this. It's not a perfect happy ending but I think it's inevitable and it makes me admire Tris, Tobias and Peter (yes! You've read it right!) more. 
 I know some people who don't want to read Allegiant anymore because they were spoiled about the ending and didn't like it. All i can say is give it a chance. If you've read the first two then why not read the last book, right? It can answer your questions and help you understand why that certain thing happens. 
 I enjoyed reading this series and I'm loking forward to read more of Ms. Roth's books.

** spoiler alert ** 
 Lei este libro por el gran cliffhanger con el que nos dejaron en Insurgente. Queria saber de inmediato que pasaba y por eso decidi leer el final de esta historia. 
 Gracias al cielo, ahora no solo la historia se cuenta desde la perspectiva de Tris, Four cuenta tambien la historia desde su punto de vista, lo que da una dinamica que si bien corta la historia de un personaje por momentos, acaba funcionando para el final del libro. 
 No me acabaron de convencer las explicaciones que dan (el dano genetico, el buro de investigacion, etc) sobre porque estaban todos divididos, no se me hizo contundente y eso casi me hace detenerme y dejar el libro. Lo mejor empieza cuando Tris, que deja a un lado la nina debil y hartante que fue en Insurgente, decide que quiere y empieza a actuar como una heroina. Four, digamos que lo vemos de una perspectiva muy diferente y deja de ser el badass que fue en los libros anteriores. Conocemos a un nuevo villano (y el hombre detras de todo) un hombre llamado David, que tampoco se sostiene en sus propias explicaciones de porque el mundo esta como esta. Regresan Caleb, Peter (la gran decepcion del libro, pudieron haber expandido mas su rol), Christina y los padres de Four, que si bien no es la historia mas entretenida, logran un final satisfactorio y cierran su historia. 
 Al igual que todos, el final fue un gran shock y algo que no esperaba. Personalmente, me agrado, fue algo inesperado, que empujo la historia hacia adelante, en vez de quedarnos con un "vivieron felices para siempre". 
 Ahora bien, ?por que 3 estrellas? Sin ser el libro mas realista, coherente y mejor escrito, logra su cometido: entretener, hacerte querer terminar el libro en una noche y logra hacerte reflexionar sobre sus cuestiones morales. Bueno seria, que hicieran un reboot de la historia sobre el futuro de los personajes, ya que quedo mucho que se puede decir de todos ellos.

 I know a lot of people love this series. I wanted to. So badly. The first book was so good, so promising, so exciting. Then after that the story went downhill. The second book drowned me in my reading slump. And when I finally got out of my reading slump after much effort, I really wanted to make myself finish the series. I kept telling myself that the story will get better. Please do not doubt my determination. I really did push myself. But now I really cannot continue to live like this anymore. Reading is fun. It is not supposed to be torturing. I am not supposed to persuade myself to pick up a book to read. I am not supposed to force myself to read and like a book because everyone else loves it. 
 I guess I managed to finish the second book because it was still set in the world where factions existed. In the third book, everything had changed. It turned out that everything was a lie and there was a bigger and a very complicated world outside the world that I believed. Reading this book was very tiring. There were uprisings everywhere. Everyone was not happy. There was not much hope. People were trying to destroy everyone and everything they loathed. Really. Reading all these were too exhausting. 
 I will not get rid of the series. I will keep the three books nicely in my book shelf, and maybe when I have nothing to read, or when I want to mess with my own head, or when my life is too boring I need confusions in my life, I will give this series another try. For now, I am going to just watch the movies.

book_b.title: Serial Hottie
book_b.user_review:
Originally posted here: http://alwayslostinbooks.wordpress.co... 
 Of all the Kelly Oram books, I think this one was the book that attracted me the least. I'm not really a big fan of mystery thrillers so I wasn't sure if I would like it or not. But after much consideration, I think that this was a pretty good book. It's not really chilling or scary or whatever, but there is some mind play. 
 I keep on trying to figure out who the serial killer is. Lots of girls with Ellie's profile were being killed throughout the state. I wasn't sure what to believe. There were a couple of potential suspects, and it certainly wasn't easy when the occurrences and evidence were all pointing to Seth. In my mind, I kept on thinking it can't be, but I was also swayed to thinking that it could be. For me, it was just hard to really tell who the serial killer could be. In my defense, I've never really been into mystery thrillers in the first place. 
 Ellie is a boyish tough girl who prefers hockey, large jerseys or shirts, and hanging out like she's one of the guys. Her best friends are three hockey-loving guys. She knows how to play rough and doesn't mind getting a little bloody. She even throws punches that can seriously hurt a guy. Because of that, the guys just see her as one of them, and some other people even question her sexual preference. But beneath that rough exterior is a girl who is attracted to the new, sexy neighbor across the street. 
 I personally like Ellie most, if not all, of the time. I was never the sporty, guy-ish kind of person, but I do have a lot of experience hanging out mostly with guys. I grew up with three brothers and no sisters, and most of my friends were guys so I could relate in a way. I think that Ellie wears her heart on her sleeve. She's just open and maybe a little impulsive. What I really loved about her are those times she thought out loud, and it was just so funny because she gets caught by other people. 
 Ellie lives in the shadow of her preppy, pretty, and popular older sister, Angela. They have too many differences and they never get along. In truth, they really care about each other, but being siblings is never really easy. Angela always wanted a sister so she always tries to bring out the girl in Ellie - makeovers, guy talk, shopping, etc. She also likes playing matchmaker. I'll admit that she's hard to like, but at least she means well. 
 Their parents were pretty cool people too. Both of their parents have their own favorites and they take after each respective parent. Ellie is more like her dad. She's definitely dad's little girl because they both love sports, fights, and pretty much the same things. That's why her dad has been always so overprotective of her, especially in this book where a serial killer could be after her and guys are starting to pay attention to her. Angela, on the other hand, is a lot like her mom. They're both the girly kind of people and they're always on each other's side. They're a pretty good family, and the whole family even has their adorable moments. 
 Seth is definitely a crazy guy. It was seriously hard to figure him out. He was mercurial. He's definitely damaged, but the mood swings were definitely disconcerting. There were stalker tendencies too. However, like Ellie, I was attracted to him in some ways. I'm not really sure. He has his charm. I guess he's a very complex character. I'd love to see a Seth POV book just so I could understand him better. There were two extras in the end of the book, but I definitely want more. 
 ************************************************** 
 OVERALL, Serial Hottie was definitely an interesting read with a serial killer on the loose and a dangerously attractive new neighbor across the street. The characters were all interesting in their own little ways, but a definite favorite would have to be Ellie. I think that she's just really comfortable with her own skin. The only person who makes her feel uncomfortable is Seth, the neighbor. In an unforgettable summer vacation, Ellie will learn to step outside her comfort zone and learn as well as embrace all the other things in her life.

 And you know what's more interesting? This story isn't just about romance, it also has suspense in it. My oh my! Two of my favorites in just one book. And mind you, I was really into it. The idea of finding out the serial killer and really named him/her in this kind of story made me become alert. I admit that Seth didn't made me fall in love with him like I did with Rob (from Cinder & Ella) but he easily made me swoon, so that's really a big plus. Bueno bueno bueno.... digamos que soy una gran fan de la personalidad Badass de Ellie. 
 Me gusto leer un libro donde la protagonista no esta obsesionada con la ropa o de la universidad o del sexo (YA Y New Adult a veces me cansan), que a medida que avanzaba la historia, para bien o para mal haya trabajado la historia entre las hermanas. La historia con los amigos de Hockey. 
 Asi que fue todo muy divertido cuando presentan a una protagonista Badass, TomBoy, deportista, y genial. Encuentro gracioso esto de que la chica no podia parar de decir en voz alta sus pensamientos. Una genia! Aunque fuera embarazoso. 
 Luego entro en escena Seth, que si, no negare que me gusto pero llego el punto "Psicotico Edward" como me gusta llamarlo y me estropeo bastante la historia. 
 Veran, era el 2008 y yo era feliz leyendo y releyendo Twilight. De verdad que me gustaba la historia, era todo tan rustico y encantador, con ese halo de misterio. Y luego Edward con su personalidad de mierda, bipolar, loco de mierda y cursi. Si si, ya sabemos como termino eso. Todas babeando por el. 
 Luego paso el tiempo y la literatura juvenil, YA, New Adult y todos los libros que caian en mi mano parecian estar escritos con el mismo patron: personajes femeninos debiles, personajes masculinos dominantes y psicopatas que les decian a las protagonistas que hacer, cuando hacerlo, donde hacerlo, cuantas veces, como vestir, que comer, etc etc (Cof Fiftyshadesdemierda cof) 
 Asi que perdonen mi mierda si les digo que soy un poco reacia a leer algo y encontrarme con personajes asi. A pesar de que tenia una explicacion. A pesar de que me gusto Seth por muchas otras razones. Me da rabia que algunas escritoras sigan con este metodo de protagonista torturado y loco. 
 Gayle Forman, Stephanie Perkins, Sara Wolf. Son maestras. Escriben personajes masculinos realistas y no locos de mierda controladores. Escriben sobre los errores, las segundas oportunidades, lo que es ser un SER HUMANO, y no una idea patriarcal implantada en el chip de todas las personas de los ultimos 3.000 anos. 
 Me molesta por muchas razones; por mi absoluto feminismo y el modo en que estos personajes en algun punto llegan a denigrar la integridad de la protagonista, la falta de amplitud de miras ya que (siendo sincera) si cada libro que leo hay un personaje de este tipo; ?Donde queda la diversion? ?Donde queda lo increible de la literatura donde todos aprendemos cosas nuevas y diferentes? ampliamos nuestros horizones, no solo de cultura sino tambien aprendemos sobre la diversidad de personalidades, amplitud de mente y comprension del ser humano. Otro problema latente es la falsa idea de romance torturado que les dan a las jovencitas con este tipo de historias. Donde ellas creen que cuando mas posesivos sean los hombres, mas amor sienten por ellas. Y estan tan equivocadas. Realmente odio cuando en alguna novela (sea de cualquier tipo) salen las palabras: 
 Eres mia. 
 Me perteneces. 
 REALLY? 
 Estamos en el siglo XXI. Quien cojones se creen estos pesonajes para creer que tienen el poder sobre otro ser hmano de decirles que hacer, de creerse sus duenos? 
 Siento que todos cruzan una linea muy delgada entre lo que es enamorarse y querer ser parte de algo, de alguien... a muy diferente, dejar que alguien te posea como si fueras un objeto. 
 Por eso, a pesar de que me gustaron muchas cosas de esta historia, no comparto el deseo de la escritora de crear una vez mas un personaje de este tipo. Si, se que va con la historia, que tiene un porque, etc etc. 
 No me importa. Me cansa leer sobre el "artista torturado". 
 Solo... desearia que la gente escribiera mas sobre hombres reales, honestos, FEMINISTAS y se dejaran de explotar a estos personajes masculinos todos territoriales, psicopatas, celosos y posesivos. 
 Por que, ya que estamos, la literatura entra en la vida de las personas de modos muy diferentes, pero siempre he tenido la fe y esperanza de que sea de un buen modo, para ensenar cosas buenas y hacernos mejorar. No para que sea al contrario.

5 We Stars 
 How odd. Suddenly, I'm part of a we and no longer just me. 
 Pure romance. 
 I could end my review right there and I would have said it all. Ms Bliss has written an emotional, romantic tale that will be your next book hangover. One that will last a while. 
 Callie is blindsided. Her life takes a turn she never expected. Never wanted. 
 Everyone thinks they'll handle shit with grace, but in reality, our fears start to suffocate us. I'm no different-my fears are many and real. 
 Bruno "The Butcher" has a reputation. But Callie is his weakness. When she needs him, he is there. He cares for her. Body and soul. 
 I think that without the struggles in life, we wouldn't savor the beautiful things. Nothing would be as sweet if it weren't for the bad. 
 I can't tell you too much of the story line. Almost anything I could say would be a spoiler and I don't do spoilers. So just let me tell you....the feels. Oh the feels in this one. 
 Paralyzed. 
 Frozen. 
 I feel that way most days now, and today is like every other. Like time moves along and I'm just an observer, not taking part in any way-just sitting, watching the world move by, and I can't touch it. 
 Enshrine is a beautiful story of overcoming the troubles of life. Of searching to find the good in your own life when the bad is so easy to see. So hard to see past. A story of giving people a first chance and a second if they need it. And believing that actions do speak louder than words. Or rumors. 
 I loved loved loved this one. There is enough sexy and tons of romance. Pure hope and romance.

I am Bruno. My husband is battling cancer and has been for over 3 years. I normally try to steer clear of books that hit this subject matter but this is a story you NEED to read. I see what Bruno saw. The beauty behind the illness is easy to see when you love someone. I see the pain he is in, the fear he feels and the depression that beats him down when he has reoccurances. I see Callie. The strength she discovers is the same I see in my husband. The bond they forge is one I am a part of. This is a beautiful romance and a love that I understand. Thank you, Chelle.

** spoiler alert ** 
 This book did not feel genuine. Her battle to beat cancer was not genuine; what should have been an intense suffering, was made light because she had no deep suffering besides screaming "Why me?" over and over again. From my end, there were no intense emotions. 
 And, according to this book, all you have to do to beat cancer is to decide to get off your butt and fight. Cancer is a lot more complicated than that and this book did not express those gray areas. 
 Also, there was too much flowery language. 
 For example: 
 "Although the darkness has brought us together, nothing will tear us apart. Think of me, of us, every time you look at this and remember that my love burns as bright and strong as the rays of the sun." 
 Ick. Too much. If you are into that I fear for your soul.

From the beginning with the Men of Inked series, I have been a Chelle Bliss fan. I was looking forward to her next book and was pleasantly surprised with Enshrine. While the same sass and mystique comes through in Bruno "The Butcher", I wasn't prepared for the subject matter or the gritty, very real, heart wrenching subject matter and emotion that spilled off the page. My heart bled for Callie and her plight and I truly felt her surrender of independence. I loved the twist and family orientation in Chelle's style and look forward to her next book. 5 stars Must Read!

This was okay, I suppose, but it was way too formulaic and young. Actually, this book fits less into the paranormal romance, YA, Urban Fantasy, pick your genre, and was little more than a very young, very tween feeling romance that happened to have some paranormal characters cast into it. 
 In a lot of YA fare, you can't necessarily tell the main characters are high school aged. In this one, she sounded very young, younger than her 16 or so years. She was portrayed as a super girlie girl, which alone is fine (I LOVE the Fever series, and Mac is definitely into girly things). Evie, though, just sounded like a little girl at times. I usually expect my YA leads to have some level of maturity, despite that they are written as technical teenagers. Most disappointing is that she had virtually no character growth whatsoever. 
 True to formula, this one made it all about the boy. It worked out, of course, because said boy's world happened to be the direction in which she needed to go, but I hate when the character sacrifices "everything" because of the boy. Things didn't work out for her because of her smarts, cunning, or other virtue - it was sheer coincidence that following him, choosing him, led her where she needed to go. 
 No real world building, either. Really just the modern world with a mish-mash of various fantastical types, like a mermaid, werewolves, vampires, shape shifters, elementals, faeries, etc. Most of them seem to be props, and serve very little purpose in the story. 
 This book could have been much more than it was. I might read the second and see if it gets any better, but this was ultimately a disappointment.

I wasn't sure about this book at first because the lead protag is really young, silly, bouncy, wears a lot of pink and is a bit spoiled. But after reading one chapter, yes, just one, she grew on me. I found her funny and sweet, trying to do right even when she is huffing and puffing and rolling her 16 year old eyes. Basically because she throws herself whole-heartedly into what she is doing and is so excited about certain silly and normal things. Her love interest is a slow build which felt natural and her inner voice was enjoyable and felt real (or real enough). 
 Evie can see through glamor. She is the only one who can do that, and having been raised by the IPCA (some sort of paranormal watch agency) who now uses her as an operative to bag and tag paranormals so they can't hurt the normal people out in the big wide world. The problem starts when she finds out that someone is killing paranormals and no one knows who or what it is. 
 "All paranormals are classified as endangered; that's why even the icky ones just get neutered instead of, well, dead." (pg 66) 
 Her agency is very clandestine, but well, a government agency and she has drunk the koolaide and believes in her work and their policies. Notice the quote above, they neuter paranormals. Hmmmm. So it is nice as she begins to speak to people outside of the agency and starts thinking for herself. 
 The love interest relationship is very young, cute and sweet. She is a teenie-bopper after all. 
 "Oh heavens, I liked that boy. When I got back to my unit, I stared at the drawing. He really captured me, which made me hope he spent a lot of time thinking about me." (pg 147) 
 Awwww! But it doesn't stay all bubble gum and pom poms, though she would if she could. Evie learns a lot about her world, herself and begins to make decisions based on her experience instead of what she is taught from a rule-book. Illusions are shattered, people are killed and she has to make some hard decisions. This book is both light and dark, easy and difficult, pink swirled into black. Even though it was dark, it was an easy and enjoyable read, I give it 4 stars glowing so bright they hurt your eyes, if you can see through glamour that is! I will be reading the next book, when I need my darkness bleeding cotton candy.

reference_books.title: Love, in Spanish (Love, in English, #1.5)
reference_books.review_text:
THIS IS A DOUBLE REVIEW FOR BOTH LOVE IN ENGLISH, AND LOVE IN SPANISH. 
 I told myself I would give it a couple of days so I can really digest this story. I still have no idea how to put into words how much I loved these books. So, I've had Karina Halle's books on my kindle for a while now, and the Love, In English books were the first I wanted to start reading of all her books. I'm actually upset that it took me this long to read these books. These books were different than any book I've ever read. People think that when reading a "forbidden romance" the two characters cheat and bam, shit hits the fan. That can be true, and with these books it kind of happened, but it was so much more than just "cheating". 
 Lately I have been obsessed with "forbidden romances", cheating in particular. I like reading these stories because it just seems like such a real topic, and I feel most people are afraid to touch on the topic. Let me tell you, Karina hit it on the head. This story was more than a forbidden romance. Honestly, it was a new found romance between the two characters. A love that was so meant to be, a real love story. 
 Mateo and Vera were two souls put on the planet to love each other. Just the way Mateo says "Vera" was enough to make me fall in love with him... How could Vera not? There were so many reasons why they shouldn't, couldn't be in anything more than friends. Sometimes you can feel like the whole universe is against you being happy, and either you can give up, or let that give you more strength to do what you have to do to stay happy. Both Mateo and Vero had everything against them. They aren't supposed to be together, let alone stay together or have a happy life together. I think what I loved most about both of these books, was the love that you can clearly feel coming off the pages as you read. There were a lot of emotions coming from the books. Emotions that made me feel so much. Mateo is way more than your normal sexy book boyfriend. Mateo is just on a whole other spectrum. Love, In English was told in Vera's pov. It was amazing getting to see the start of everything. Vera went to Spain to teach English to local Spaniards. Mateo happening to be one of the Spaniards there. From the start there was this undeniable attraction, but like I said before it was way more than that. Of course there was sexual attraction between the two, but both Mateo and Vera connected as people. They wanted to know more about each other. Their likes, dislikes, dreams. EVERYTHING. Honestly their relationship started as friends, because it couldn't go any further than that. Vera lived in Canada, Mateo had a wife and child, but fate always has other plans. They were destined to be happy together, and even though they had ALL ODDS against them. They never gave up. They came very close to, but they never did. 
 In book 2, Love, In Spanish Mateo took over. Reading a book in Mateo's pov is something everyone should experience. I'm not sure if I'm the only one, but in my head there was a permanent accent that I imagined him speaking in. To say it was HOT is putting it extremely lightly. Mateo has such a way with words. He is just such an emotional guy in every aspect. I feel like his age has something to do with it. He knows what he wants, and wasted enough time doing what he didn't want. He's finally at a point in his life where he doesn't want to pretend anymore. He wants to love, and love hard. Mateo won't take no for an answer either. He's going after what he wants and not stopping until he gets it. 
 Karina, you are just brilliant. The story of Mateo and Vera will stay with me forever. I love love loved it. The journey they both took me on was just such a special journey. I'm seriously so happy I read these books. You will forever have a fan in me! I can't wait to read your other books! 
 If you are a romance lover, you MUST read both Love, In English, and Love, In Spanish. It does have a bit of cheating, but in a very understandable way. If you are okay with that, then please do yourself a favor and read these books. You will love them I promise!!! 
 <3 JMAC

 "I saw him first, but it didn't matter. Because he saw her."

It's safe to say I had about a million heart attacks with the characters. One second I was like "oh ok this isn't so bad" and the next second I wanted to throw my kindle. 
 "I feel relieved because I loved her, but not as much as I loved you." 
 The love. The hate. The hurt. The betrayal. It's all in this book and Kandi does such a phenomenal job at expressing each emotion. Like I knew halfway into the book that Kandi would be a favorite of mine, and I knew without a doubt I will be reading all of her books. Previously written and whatever's to come. 3.5 stars 
 I'm so sad that I have to give only 3,5 stars for this book, especially because it started as a favorite. I fell in love with the first part of the book, the writing style was brilliant, and I read it till 2:00 am, but after a matter of time it became so damn frustrating that never-ever-ever-ever was the timing right for the characters. Yesterday I had to put aside this book for a few hours because I wanted to throw my reader out of the window after B and Jamie couldn't find the right time for the fifteenth time. :((( 
 I truly loved the writing style of the author, and I loved the whiskey metaphor but I wish that the second part of the story would have find another wave to ride, then this book probably would became a five stars favorite for me. :(

I had a plan. I was scrolling through my Kindle looking for a good book to reread - something that I could put down after a while and go to sleep like a normal person. Without putting too much (read: any) thought into it, my finger hit A Love Letter to Whiskey. I haven't read it before, nor have I read anything by this particular author. What the hell, let's give it a go, shall we? 
 Ok. I'll just read a few chapters... 
 (((RECORD SCRATCH))) 
 Just a dang minute! A.) I got sucked into this story almost from page one. 2.) I thought I knew where it was going, but of course I didn't. And C.) There was just no possible break in this story that would have been a suitable spot to place a bookmark. None! So, I did what any red blooded woman would do: I finished that sucker. 
 I went into this almost blind. The blurb is kind of vague(ish), but I had an idea, or so I thought. My recommendation is go in blind. Don't read reviews, don't ask your friends about it, just start reading. I also recommend not starting it at 11:00 p.m. if you need to work in the morning or have kids who wake up at the ass crack of dawn. 
 This book was a little bit angsty. (I couldn't even type that with a straight face!) Seriously, this book is so loaded with angst I did four consecutive happy dances while simultaneously eating a bag of Oreo cookies. Don't judge! However, as the story wound down I got increasingly nervous because there just weren't enough pages left for what I thought was going to happen, to happen. My goodness, that ending!! That's all I'm going to say about it. Heart palpitations, people!! 
 Thank you, Kandi Steiner! My newest gray hairs are dedicated entirely to you.

5 out of 5 stars!!!! 
 I love Kandi Steiner! I haven't read a book by her that I haven't loved and this book was no different! Honestly, I think this is her best work yet and I can't wait for her to share her words with the world!!! 
 Jamie and B have a relationship that is so hard to describe. It's hard to put into words what their story did to me. I can't even begin to write a review that will do this novel justice! 
 This book was the best -- and the worst -- kind of roller coaster ride. The ups were so great and the downs were so down. I messaged Kandi while reading at least twice because I couldn't figure out where the story was going and how much more heartache I could possibly stand. 
 This book was full of angst, but only the best kind. The kind that produces real emotions and makes you really feel what the characters are feeling. I cried for Jamie because B couldn't stick to her decisions. I cried for B because she was addicted to something she didn't feel like she deserved. I laughed with them because they were so great together and they really had a friendship that I want with someone as well. 
 B is a creative soul and one of my favorite passages came after one of many heartbreaks for her in the book. She was an aspiring writer and these words hold so much truth in the real world that I loved them in the book: 
 Words don't get written from a heart that's never felt. They come from pain, from love, from unspeakable depths -- and they were my only release. 
 This was a hard read and yet it was something I couldn't put down. I wanted to just keep reading. I didn't want to eat or sleep or go to work, I just wanted to keep reading these words and live in this world. I hope that many, many people will read these words and share their heart with B & Jamie.

I read so many positive reviews and recommendations for this book from a lot of people and it made me curious. The lovely cover even helped! Upon reading this, I expected it to be more mature honestly. 
 Anyway, as the story progressed, it became a struggle for me to continue because it feels that B and Jamie's relationship is doomed from the start. They continually cheated to other people with each other which really is a red flag for me. Their best-friendship is not even that established. I tried to continue reading but there are so much unnecessary angst and the only reason they are not together are because of their stubbornness. I could have forgiven the cheating if it was a bit justified (though nothing would really justify cheating). I would have been still engrossed while reading it if they have other major reasons as to why they are not together. I just skimmed from 65% and am very relieved that it's done.

I looove a messy romantic read, cause sometimes in life, love don't come easy and people do get caught in the crossfire. 
 This book had me all kinds of twisted, I hated B then I loved B then I wanted to slap B then I loved her again. Her addiction to 'whiskey' was told with such honesty and clarity that you felt for them ever step of the way. When I talk to my kindle a 2am I know I am reading an epic book... oh and when whiskey and water combine oh wow they are

sample_reviews.review_text:
I received a complimentary copy in exchange for an honest review. 
 You ever start a book and immediately realize that THIS is why you read? From the very beginning The Fall Up spoke to my heart. And it's been beating over this story ever since. 
 "It was raining. Isn't that the way all great love stories start....and also usually end?" 
 Well this is a GREAT love story, but I can guarantee it is nothing like you've ever read. Levee Williams and Sam Rivers meet in the most unconventional of places. There is a spark between them the moment they open their mouths to speak. Over time, their meeting place becomes THEIRS. They recognize the sadness in each other as they live with a burden. Every day. They understand the darkness within their hearts because loving someone only brings pain. Something they both know too well. 
 "Don't let go. No matter what, okay?" 
 "Never." 
 I cannot discuss the plot. No. You must live this story. Just know that Sam and Levee's story is inspirational and is one of the most beautiful love stories I have ever read. As I said before you have not read this story. There are some deep and raw emotions here. Sam and Levee are two broken people with heartbreaking pasts. But they find a light in each other. Together, it doesn't hurt so much to breathe. Life and living is possible. And love? It's inevitable. But there are some lighthearted moments. This isn't a cry your eyes out story per se. I'd say its a heartfelt emotional story. It's REAL. The author places you within the lives of Sam and Levee. You FEEL everything. Their joy, their pain, their laughs. And you WILL laugh. Their banter is something special. 
 "There isn't a woman in the world who doesn't have demons of some sort. No matter who I end up with, it's always going to be a struggle.....Levee I'd like to struggle with you." 
 Oh Sam Rivers. How I love you. Adore you. Let me count the ways. I don't think I have ever met a man so self-less and loving. While consumed with his own pain, his love for Levee far exceeds any darkness. His heart desires Levee. His soul forever tethered to hers. And you feel the depths of his love just by the declaration in his words. He speaks with conviction. And Levee? Her love saves. All this time where she thinks Sam is saving her? It is she who is truly saving Sam. 
 "She wasn't the princess. And I wasn't the pauper. She was just a sad girl who liked to write songs. And I was nothing more than a simple guy who was lucky enough to have made her fall in love with him." 
 Their love consumes. Overwhelms. Their love is powerful. Magic. Their love will captivate you and question love and just how much it can take. But their love endures. It overcomes the darkness. It fights through the pain. Their past? It just makes their love stronger. It solidifies everything their love stands for. This isn't an easy love story, but it's theirs. 
 "From the moment I first met you, you made the world lighter." 
 The Fall Up truly demonstrates the versatility of this author's writing. This is different than her other novels, but equally as brilliant, if not more so. It was such an honor to experience the heart stopping ,breathtaking love story of Sam and Levee. A love that faced it all. A love that didn't see anywhere to go from being at the bottom..but up. This was easily one of my top reads of 2015.

Living life in the limelight can be a blessing and a curse. With her professional career at a high, Levee Williams can't help but feel her life spiraling out of control. Demands from her performing obligations push her deeper and deeper into placing unrealistic expectations on herself. A weight on Levee's shoulders that is magnified by the turmoil from her past. Pushing her into an activity that is dangerous and would have repercussions on her career if anyone found out. 
 Reflecting on the past is nothing new to Sam. For his own reasons, he seeks solace from smoking while looking out over the city from a nearby bridge. The last thing he expected was to discover a female tempting her fate on that bridge. Someone unknown at the time, but who would leave a lasting impression on Sam's heart. 
 Night after night, the two tattered souls travel to that bridge to meet again. There reasons as opposite as they can be. One person is there to reflect....the other has the intentions of jumping. Sam is determined to save Levee from a fate that has no return. While the two don't know a lot about one another, fate will intervene and throw their two worlds together. Something that will alter both of their lives in the most unexpected of ways. 
 Where do I begin?? Oh I know.....be still my ever loving Sam filled heart!! The Fall Up is an emotional story that pulled me in from the very first chapter. I sat up far into the night ...well, actually it was early morning by the time I finished devouring the words upon the pages. Levee and Sam have to deal with some serious pressures in life. How they go about moving on is both engaging and intense. 
 This romance was anything but ordinary. Word upon word that left me wanting more peeks into their life. There are some humorous moments that only add to the serious subject matter that this book deals with. Creating a romance that definitely mirrors circumstances one would find in today's world. While there were so many times I wasn't sure where the story was headed, the ending was a compliment to the plot the author worked so hard to create. A GREAT romance that should be at the top of your to-read list!!

"It was raining. 
 Isn't that the way all great love stories start? And also usually end?" Awe, it does seem like some of the great love scenes happen in the rain. Levee and Sam's story starts on a raining night on a bridge. Both of them are there for different reasons. Sam's there to ponder life when he see's Levee and wonders if she's there to jump. 
 'My career was soaring while, personally, I was plummeting.' 
 Levee has everything a little kids dream of -> being rich and famous. But behind the glamour lives a girl who feels a missing connection with the world. Her nightly visits to the bridge create concern for Sam who at the time is just a stranger on that bridge. He reaches out to her to let her know she's not alone if she's struggling. 
 'I was sick of fucking fine. I needed something - anything - to be great.' 
 Sam has his own demons that haunt him. Under the exterior of his tattoos and cigarettes is a man who searching for "something." 
 "Levee, I'd like to struggle with you." 
 By nature Sam is a caretaker. He holds other's needs in high regard. He carries their burden on his shoulders. Those nights on the bridge prove what a good guy Sam is because once he lays eyes on Levee, without knowing who she is, he reaches out to her to make sure she's cared for. 
 'It's just hard when your woman has Gibson [guitar] taste and a thrift store man.' 
 The relationship between the two of them started before either one knew who the other one was and once it got going it was with pure intentions these two fell for each other. It didn't matter that he wasn't rich and she was because they liked the stripped down versions of each other. Money wasn't going to be a factor in their relationship. 
 Ms. Martinez fans will love this story. The banter in the book will have you smiling and Sam will make you swoon. Plus there are other characters in the book to love such as her friend, Henry.
